You study the stars carefully, but they remain silent.
The constellation offers no insight this time.
Whatever message the stars held has slipped away.
You sense a faint presence among the stars, but it quickly fades.
The constellation's light flickers without revealing its secrets.
You wait patiently for a sign, but none arrives.
You almost discern a message before it vanishes from your thoughts.
The constellation politely declines to elaborate.
You feel certain the stars judged your attempt. They offer no further comment.
Even the stars have off days.
You continue to observe the stars, confirming that they are indeed stars.
The stars insist that talking to plants helps. They refuse to comment on whether the plants listen.
The constellation warns that the tallest tree always wins an argument with a blunt axe.
The stars reveal that weeds are simply crops with exceptional confidence.
The stars suggest that planting today is wiser than promising you'll plant tomorrow.
The constellation claims every mighty Oak Tree was once a seed that ignored terrible advice.
The stars quietly remind you that chopping the tree before collecting the fruit is rarely the optimal strategy.
The stars wonder why you're not mining Coal right now.
The stars insist that hitting the rock harder is a valid mining strategy.
The constellations insists you are one Geode away from finding that rare item.
The stars wonder how staring at them all night helps build Strength.
The constellation reminds you that a high Strength level won't save you from the Coal mines.
The stars stare back at you.
The stars whisper that fish are far less cooperative once they realize they're on the menu.
The stars suggest drying your firewood before complaining that it won't burn.
The constellation reminds you that cooking the fish is generally easier after you've caught it.
The constellation insists that a warm campfire has ended more adventures than any monster.
The stars guide you to a secluded steam within the Shrapnel River.
[color=green]This observation grants you with access to the Moonlit Stream Fishing spot.[/color]
The stars guide you to a hidden spot along the Windy Coastline.
[color=green]This observation grants you with access to the Midnight Cove Fishing spot.[/color]
The constellation claims every perfect hide once belonged to something that strongly preferred keeping it.
The constellation wonders why creatures are so attached to materials you clearly need for crafting.
The stars remind you that chasing wildlife is considerably easier without carrying half your workshop.
The stars insist that "I'll just hunt one more" has misled countless adventurers.
The constellation reveals that collecting "just in case" materials eventually becomes a storage problem.
The constellation lights a path towards a hidden opening in the Hills.
[color=green]This observation grants you with access to the Moonlit Hills Hunting Location.[/color]
The constellation points toward a tranquil lake where the water curves like a crescent moon. A hidden shoreline beckons those willing to seek it.
[color=green]This observation grants you with access to the Crescent Lake Combat Area.[/color]
The stars claim that yelling while attacking increases accuracy.
The stars remind you that every dent in your armour is a valuable lesson. Preferably someone else's lesson.
The constellation claims that missing your target is not a valid strategy.
The stars claim every unique weapon began life as "good enough for now."
The stars insist that hitting harder is a perfectly valid strategy.
The constellation claims every arrow flies true until the wind develops a personality.
The stars suggest aiming before celebrating the shot.
The constellation reminds you that trees rarely volunteer to become arrows.
The stars wonder why arrows are always found in the most inconvenient places.
The constellation claims a quiver is merely a very organised collection of future mistakes.
The constellation advises remembering that boomerangs are designed to return.
The stars insist that every spell is perfectly safe until proven otherwise.
The constellation wonders why wizards keep writing things down when they can barely read their own spellbooks.
The heavens insist that magical explosions are merely enthusiastic successes.
The stars reveal that every great mage has accidentally cast something they absolutely didn't mean to.
The constellation reminds you that staring at it all night won't solve your Rune supply problems.
You somehow learn a new form of Magic by simply looking at the stars and pretending to read them or something lol.
[color=green]This observation grants you with the knowledge to use Astral Spells.[/color]
The constellation reveals an ancient rite. Its celestial words awaken the power of Astral Prayers.
[color=green]This observation grants you with the knowledge to use Astral Prayers.[/color]
The stars reveal that blessed logs burn brighter than ordinary ones. Coincidence, perhaps.
The stars wonder who first looked at a pile of bones and thought, "The gods will love this."
The constellation insist that divine favour cannot be bought. Offerings, however, are gladly accepted.
The constellation claims the gods have excellent taste in offerings, though their preferences remain oddly specific.
The constellation observes that the gods rarely explain why they like bones. They simply do.
The stars reveal a crater where moonlight never truly fades. Something ancient still stirs within its scar.
[color=green]This observation grants you with access to the Moonscarred Crater Slayer Zone.[/color]
The stars wonder where your ingredients go when you fail to cook something.
The constellation claims a hearty meal can solve many problems. The remaining problems usually require a weapon.
The constellation insists that eating during a battle is a skill worthy of admiration.
The stars reveal that a full stomach is often the first step toward surviving the next encounter.
The constellation claims every meal tastes better after narrowly avoiding defeat.
The constellation claims locked doors are merely suggestions.
The stars reveal that every graceful landing is built upon countless less graceful ones.
The stars wonder why NPCs cannot pickpocket you as well.
The constellation hints at accepting bribes for more Stealth in return.
The constellation wonders why a very specific item seems to constantly appear on random routes.
The constellation reminds you that it cannot assist with your Lockpick problem.
The stars insist that the best defence is letting the monster become someone else's assignment.
The constellation claims every Slayer task looks reasonable until you actually arrive.
The stars reveal that shields are much easier to repair than confidence.
The stars wonder if Slayer Masters secretly compete to invent increasingly inconvenient tasks.
The constellation insists that "just one more monster" has delayed many journeys home.
The stars reveal that every experienced slayer has confidently attacked the wrong monster at least once.

Seeds of Sustenance - The owner of the Spiced Honey Tavern has been having an issue keeping her pantry stocked, as goods have slowly but surely vanishing in the night. Worried about her customers going hungry, she reached out to you, hoping for a moment of your time.
Only the best for Lira. I'll need to harvest some fresh produce, then hand it over.
These look great, hopefully it'll be enough to last her a while.

As you walk into the warm tavern, a middle-aged woman rushes by you in a blur, carrying a half dozen tankards of ale, then quickly setting them in front of two excited looking patrons.
The whole place is buzzing with rowdy energy, but it remains light and warm. Despite all people clamoring for her attention, they quickly fall to silence as Lira holds up her hand. She gives you a warm embrace, then pinches your cheek shortly afterward.
It's so lovely to see you [i]{0}[/i]. Thank you for coming to see me on such short notice.
Of course, Lira, any time. You sounded urgent in the note you sent me, how can I help?
We've been running through our food supply far faster than we should be as of these last few weeks. I don't know where it could possibly be going, but it's a problem.
I can only imagine, looks like you're feeding half the town in here. Business is going well, it'd seem?
Half of Azamire, and a bit from every nearby town, too. If I don't find a way to get some fresh produce, I might have to start turning folks away.
Don't worry, I can always find a bit of time to help out. What do you need the most?
Thank you so much... I'd like to cook up some stew. Some potatoes and onions would keep this place happy and fed for quite a while, if it's really not too much trouble.
That shouldn't be an issue in the slightest. We'll be back soon!
As you turn to leave the Spiced Honey Tavern, the quieted customers start to stir once again, chattering among themselves or asking for refills on their ever dwindling pints.
It's a large fireplace, it'll take a lot of wood to fill, and a decent bit of effort to get it all burning.
A few folks begin to crowd around the fire, enjoying the warmth, now all that's left is to wait for Lira's stew. [Burn] X/X [Oak Logs] - [Complete Button]

With fresh produce in tow, you make your way back into the Spiced Honey Tavern. A couple of excited looking patrons eye the vegetables, knowing that they'll soon have it cooked and on their table.

Lira beams when she sees you. She motions for you to hand your haul over to a large, bearded man who has an apron half-tied around him.
Thank you so much! We'll get them cleaned up and cooking soon. I don't suppose I could trouble you just a little further..?
Well... The fire's gone out. It's going to take a bit to wash and cut everything, so if you could get it lit for me, it'd be a huge help.
I'm on it, but it's going to cost you...
Oh..? Well, that's okay, I suppose. You've worked hard, and the tavern is doing well. How much for everything?
Well... I'd say at least two bowls, and two tankards, too?
And here I thought you were going to ring me dry for saving my business. You get that fire lit and you can drink until I need to get Rowan to come pick you up off the floor.
Lira gestures to the hearth on the far end of the tavern, and several customers move themselves and their tables away to give you plenty of space to work.

Lira has Rowan and a few customers help haul out a large stew pot which has been filled with all sorts of hearty vegetables, meats, and a dizzying blend of spices that begins to make your mouth water as the pot slowly begins to bubble. As you wait, Lira is true to her word, and you rarely find your tankards less than half full.

After a couple hours of waiting and a few last dashes of several spices, Lira declares her creation finished. Bowls are distributed and a line quickly forms, everyone eagerly waiting to eat their fill. You enjoy yourself as the tavern becomes more rowdy through the night. Before you know it, you find yourself passed out by the fire, and the tavern mostly empty.

That was a good night.

Packing Lunch - A battle-hardened representative from the Slayers Guild has found himself without the majority of his supplies after a band of robbers stripped him of nearly all his possessions. In shockingly high spirits, the man still wishes to embark on a journey to the nearby Corrupted Farmlands, but will need to restock before he can.
What would a man like him even like? Fish, maybe?
Hopefully this will be a suitable enough lunch, then Gol can get on his way.

A nearly bare man stands on the side of the road covered by a terrifyingly small loincloth, laughing heartily as a few folks gawk at his form, then rush by while averting their eyes. He flexes in several positions, showing off his incredibly well-built body and empty scabbard, one of the few things the man seems to own. 

Hapren quickly approaches you, then points in the man's direction.
[i]{0}[/i], I beg of you, deal with this man.
...Deal with him? What do you want me to do, stab him?
What?! Heavens, no [i]{0}[/i]! I just want you to talk to him and get him to leave. Or, at the very least, cover up a little.
And why aren't you doing that already?
Look at him! The man looks like a tree uprooted itself from the ground, shed its bark, and is now harassing my good citizens! I'll make it worth your while, so please, go!
Ah! Another comes to admire Gol's form, yes?
You're an impressive specimen, but no, I'd actually like you to cover up a bit. What brings you around here?
Well, Gol was making his way towards his target when Gol was accosted by bandits!
Oh! I'm terribly sorry then, let's see if we can get you some clothes and then...
HA! Clothes? Nay, they took Gol's supplies and sword! Gol has no need for anything to shield himself from the blows of his enemies.
So you just... walk around like this?
Aye! They robbers took Gol's lunch as well. Once Gol has had a bite to eat, Gol can continue towards his battle!
...I'll see if I can rustle something up for you to eat, then.
Gol pats his stomach expectantly as you walk back towards a somewhat relieved Hapren. He gives you a thumbs up and scurries off, leaving you to deal with Gol yourself.
I need to make sure the bolts are well-made so they'll hold a man of that size, only way to do that is to do it myself.
Gol looks up expectantly as you approach and hand him the fish. One after another, the man sucks them down, then sighs happily. You're not sure if you saw him chew.
Gol was pleased by this little snack! The nice lady from the tavern came by with food as well, but battle shall be Gol's main course!
I'd imagine that must have been Lira, yeah? Her food's to die for, but I'd imagine that it'd be hard to pay in your current state.
Only for now! Gol will make back his fortune tenfold once he has pilfered the nearby dungeon. But Gol is not yet set off.
That would have been too easy, yeah? What's stopping you now?
Among Gol's possessions was climbing gear that he needed to get to the farmlands. Would you be able to provide some for Gol?
Oh, that's easy, I think there was some boots and hooks left in Lira's tavern. Let me go ge-
No, no. Traditional gear will neither fit nor hold Gol's magnificent shape. Topaz Bolts will let me climb just fine.
The tips will cut into any surface, if slammed hard enough. Then the iron shafts will hold me!
Are you sure you don't just want the climbing gear..?
The large man just gestures to his body once again, before striking another-admittedly impressive-pose. You leave to fetch the man his bolts.

Gol takes the bolts from you and considers them with a far more meticulous eye than you expected from him. After a while, his face breaks out into a smile as he nods. He claps you on the shoulder hard enough to shake you to your bones, then vows that he will repay you someday. You notice that his loincloth covers even less from behind as he walks away, towards whatever battle he intends to fight.

Hapren and Lira scurry out from inside of the nearby tavern once they see that Gol has departed. Lira asks about the man, seemingly saddened by him not sticking around, as she hoped he'd be able to drink half his weight in ale. Hapren shakes your hand once, thanking you taking care of the man, and says a light prayer hoping that he doesn't return.

Morally Ethical Grave Robbing - A long forgotten city filled with treasure, riches, and secrets beyond compare has just been uncovered... maybe. It's quite possible that there's hardly anything at all down there, but there's only one way to find out!
Some steel for the heads, and willow logs for the shafts should be plenty strong enough.
I think this should be plenty to outfit the crew with some new tools.

A scattered group of dwarves mills about a half excavated hillside, clutching broken tools and caring for what looks like some nasty burns and singed beards. Funnily enough, they seem more worried about their facial hair than their wounds.

An elderly man in a comically large wizard's hat seems surprised, but also pleased, to see you.
Why hello there! Say, are you any handy with a pickaxe? Decently strong enough to move rocks from one location to another, maybe?
Well, I'm not too bad at either, but it looks like you've got a whole crew here, why aren't they mining?

Because this talentless hack didn't warn us about the tunnel being trapped. It's a good thing that "Whudgrath Roksmak's Crew is twice the prize at half the size"... in case you're lookin' for a crew, stranger.

How dare you sir? I may have wandered off to inspect a few of the enchanted baubles we've found, but I'm far from talentless. Don't you want to learn if it's even worth digging up this hillside before you do so?
We're dwarves, lad. It's always worth diggin', I just hope my folks can live to tell about it!

I thoroughly apologize for my tardiness, but the fact that the ruins are trapped means that there's something inside worth getting at! Most of the trinkets we've unearthed have some kind or form of enchantment as well!
I'll let you two just sort this out...
Wait just a sediment. If what Morlin says is true, it sounds like the payday might be worth getting blown up once or twice more.
More than enough for all of us! I'm more interested in the history of the place than anything else, anyway.
I wouldn't mind myself some fancy magic stuff. What do you need from me?
My folks will be fine, but our tools... a little less so. You mind getting us some steel to make more, while we patch ourselves up?
I'll see what I can do.
I have the feeling I'm going to be here a while...

Whudgrath happily takes the materials from you while his crew gathers round. He snaps his fingers towards Morlin, who quickly heats up the material using few blasts of fire magic.

In a terrifying display of efficiency and speed, using their bare hands and some well-placed smacks of their hammers, the dwarves work the material into shape. Once Morlin cools them, they're then fit to whittled shafts. The whole assembly line starts and finishes just seconds after you take the last bit of material from your bag.
Right then! Are we ready to dig?
Looks like it! I can only imagine what we could find deeper in... Perhaps more about their way of life? Ties to nearby civilizations?
Booze that has been aging for an untold number of years? New, fancy bits and bobs?
Am I the only one concerned about there being more traps? Ancient guardians? Diseases that have been lingering for who knows how long? There is a reason this place is a ruin, right?
That all sounds like fun to me. Time to strike the earth!
I don't suppose I could get you to join them, could I? The sooner this place is dug up, the sooner we can get to exploring it!

Before you can get a word in, a pickaxe is thrust into your hands by a passing dwarf, followed by a helmet and a water flask. You're spun around and placed in front of a bit of rubble. Time to get to it.
Morlin really isn't holding back on asking away, is he?
Let's hope that this is everything that Morlin needs to deal with the cursed door.

Sweat pours down your brow as a cart pulled behind a large star-nosed mole the crew has affectionately named 'Moley' swings by.
The crew loads up the rubble you've broken down as you swing your pickaxe once again. But, instead of the typical smack and shock of resistance you're used to when mining, this time, your tool goes THROUGH the rock. A small, unlit cavern lays in front of you. Just as you call out, the clean-up crew crowds around you, yelling about 'rocks and stones,' whatever that means. Shortly after, you're joined by Whudgrath and Morlin, who filter into the cave and immediately start inspecting a large circular door carved into the wall
Well done! Looks like you've found... something! We've got some kinda door here, hm?
Or to seal something off, perhaps? Either way, it's an exciting find! One that is...
Trapped, I'm afraid. We're going to have to deactivate it before we go any further.
You're sure we can't just smack it and run?
Is that how you blew up last time?
I just like to call it efficiency. I'm coming around to the idea of being blown up, as long as I know it's leading up to a nice payday.
No... this one's a curse, from what I'm able to tell. One that'll take a while to remove.
Oh? Well, okay then, I can come back later, once you've sorted that out?
Your work is far from done! I'll need you to fetch me some runes required for the spell to lift the curse on the door. I'll have a list done up for you.

Morlin flicks his hands, and a leaf of paper floats out of his pack and hangs in the air. You can see something already written on it... "Blindfold, velvet rope, three wheels of cheese..." But Morlin flicks his hands again and another-blank this time-leaf is produced, while the other immediately combusts. 

Words form from nothing, and then the paper floats into your hands. You want to ask about the other list, but decide against it.

You are guided down into the dimly lit tunnel as dwarves gather around excitedly, seeing what Morlin has in store. The old wizard gladly takes the runes from you and begins focusing very deeply...

Everyone holds their breath while he works, moving his hands in esoteric swirls and patterns until suddenly, the man... sneezes. But then! With a crack and a flash that bathes the room in cold blue light, a veil of magic slowly rolls off the door and evaporates into the air. Morlin warns everyone not to breathe in the cursed air, and as folks duck and cover their faces with clothes and pulled up shirts, he laughs and swats the air, exclaiming that there's no such thing.

You hold back the urge to take a pickaxe from the wall and stick it into his back as the door slowly rolls into the side of the wall, revealing... a long, cold hallway lined with suits of armor in remarkable condition. At the feet of these, many offerings were laid out ages ago. Withered flowers and fruits have light stains in the stone, almost completely missed because of the small piles of gems, coins, and other small treasures laid out.

Everyone is quite pleased by the discovery, as the immediate payoff is overshadowed by the looming question: What more could lay further below?

Life's a Beach - While out for a lovely day of fishing along the Windswept Shores, you managed to find a catch you're not quite sure if you should toss back or not. The grumpy old man is a pain to deal with, but with enough time, he might warm up to you.

Or not.
Maybe I'll reel it in, whatever it is.
Wait a second, I think I've got something!

You spend your day relaxing on the coast of the Windswept Shores, enjoying the waves crashing on the beach and sound of wind... sweeping the shore. Like much of the coastline near Azamire, the rocky outcroppings make for dangerous passage for the numerous boats heading up towards the capital, and another victim seems to have dashed itself along the rocks. The shipwreck calls to you, begging you to see what you can pull up from its depths.
Any chance I find something useful? Maybe...
No, no... Who'd toss those out into the water?
No... you can only find those in lakes.
Nah... the pages would be all soggy anyway.

You continue thinking of strange things you'd never expect to find in the water while you marrily fish away, occasionally dozing off as you pull in fish after fish. You swear that you can see something floating out by the shipwreck, but every time you look closer, you lose sight of it.
I wonder if I should toss him back..?
Maybe I shouldn't have asked if I could keep him.

Your hook is caught on something! It flails and flops and fights like no other fish you've ever caught before. You think for a moment that you've got the ship itself with as much raw energy as your catch fights back with. As you reel in, you see... A MAN!

Waterlogged and a confusing mix of grumpy and appreciative, the man hacks up half the sea once you've pulled him onto shore.
I don't suppose you're edible, are you?
I'd quite seriously doubt your morals if you thought so. My name's Dixon, and it seems I've just barely survived a shipwreck.
Do I get to keep you?
You'd think that you were the one who nearly drowned out there with questions like these. Are you going to tell me where I am?
Currently, you're on my fishing hook, and on the windswept shores.
Most shores I can think of are windswept, you're going to have to be a touch more specific than that.
Oh, my apologies, I didn't quite emphasize that right. I meant the Windswept Shores. Capital letters n' all.
Far from my home port then. Mind if I join you for a spell?
I just pulled you out of the sea, and the first thing you can think of doing is fishing?
I figured it'd be a good way to get you to pull your damn hook out of my coat.

You simply pluck your hook from the man's jacket, then lean away as he coughs up a bit more water. Among the debris that washed ashore, the man finds a decent enough rod and sits down beside you. Any attempts at further conversation are met with grumbles or silence. Eventually, he asks about the nearest town he could rest in, and you mention Azamire. He returns to his silence shortly after.
How do people even use these things?
I'll stick with a rod for now. Best to give it to Dixon.
The man stands and cracks his back, then tosses his catch into a loose bag. He seems to debate if he wants to continue talking to you at all, before he nods.
Well, thank you for pulling me out of the drink. You might be a touch special, but I can't deny that you helped me out of a jam.
Perhaps it was a little insensitive when I asked if I could eat you.
...Maybe you should have let me drown.
I'm just kidding, I'm just kidding... Mostly.
Sure, sure. Speaking of catches, I'm sure you'll catch a lot of junk, but if you stick around here, you might find a decent enough net. You may have even found one already.
If you wouldn't mind. Usually they run for a decent bit of gold, but perhaps I could offer you a bit of trade instead?
I think we could make something like that work, I'll let you know. I'll find you in town later?
The man nods, seeming content with that, then heads up the road towards Azamire. Maybe you're already feeling wistful, but the shore feels a little bit lonely without his grumbles beside you.

Dixon isn't hard to spot. Shortly after arriving back in Azamire, you find that he's already managed to procure himself a cart and he has started to sell off his catch. You offer up the net and he starts to beam, pleased at the quality of it. He mentions that it'll come in handy as a local tavernkeep just swung by, asking if he'd be interested in providing fresh fish for her tavern in exchange for a place to stay, and a bit of pay on top.
As several more folks begin to crowd around, asking about his prices, he talks about how they happen to be the highest quality fish from far off lands, and that he's basically losing money selling them at these prices. You start to wonder if you could do the same, considering you've got the exact same fish, from the exact same place.
Mage in the Making - A young woman has been trying in vain to cram all of her studies into a few fraught hours before her mentor arrives to town, much to the dismay of Lira and her patrons.
I'm sure nothing could possibly go wrong arming her.

You hear a cry ring out from the entire tavern followed by several rapid apologies from a distraught lady in the middle of the Spiced Honey Tavern. A concerningly large scorch mark has been left on the floor, with a table or two completely blown to pieces.
I'm sorry! I'm sorry, I- I-, I can pay for that!
It's fine, sugar, I was needing to replace those tables anyway, and you've already done me the favor of turning them into kindling.
Rowan was going to mop today anyway, don't fuss over it so much.
I know a spell! If I just-
I think my tavern has seen enough of your magic for now, okay?
[i]{0}[/i], how lovely to see you! A new mage has come to town and I'm sure you'd be able to help her out, yeah?
Wait, what? Help her out with-
She says she's practicing! It's lovely, I just need her to do it... not here. Thanks, bye!
...Hi. I'm Magnavous, and I'm... trying to be a mage.
I think I've gotten a fair bit of the picture. Your studying is...
Rocky, to say the least. But I think I'm getting close!
Right. Is there anything I can help with?
Well, I seem to have run out of air runes, do you have any that you'd be willing to spare?
I'll see if I can come up with some.

You and Magnavous were rushed out of Lira's tavern as you talked and found yourself on the porch. Through the window, Lira continues to give you concerned glances, worried she'll have to fix up the front of her establishment. You usher her away from the building, and ask her to practice in a small glade near town, and that you'll come with some air runes as soon as you can.
I never fancied myself a teacher, but let's take a stab at it.
Let's hope she caught all that.

With the few supplies she had left, it'd seem that Magnavous has turned the serene glade you once adored into a smoking crater. A smouldering tree breaks at the middle and crashes to the ground as you approach.
I suppose no more picnics here for a little while...
No, no, not at all! Honestly, your magic seems... shockingly powerful, just a touch...
Dangerous to myself and everyone around me?
I was going to say 'uncontrolled'. I think you're plenty powerful, the issue is more so with the fact that I think you're starting a little too big.
Hmm... But starting small would take more runes, and I can't just ask you to fetch me some every time I want to cast a spell.
Have you considered trying to make your own?
Where did you think they came from?
I don't know! I was supposed to have a mentor who'd teach me all of this, but he never turned up.
Who was he supposed to be, anyway?
I've only heard the stories I've heard in the capital... His name is Morlin, and he's said to be a dashing man.
He's a master of the arcane, has felled countless beasts and has unearthed some of the most powerful relics ever found...
Um... I think I know him.
You've met him!? Is he as wonderful as the stories say? My father sent me here to study under him, and I waited for a long while back in town...
I helped him out for a bit at a dig site nearby... A bit eccentric, but definitely talented.
Did he mention me at all? That he had to be off soon to meet his apprentice?
Uh... No... But the archaeological site he uncovered seems to be quite promising, there's a good chance he's just busy.
Oh... okay, hopefully that's what it is! Once I can control my magic a bit better, I can go and meet him myself!
I'd like to learn how to make my own runes, can you show me?

You take out a couple of books you had intended to give her and run through the basics of runecrafting. She seems to absorb the information well, nodding along with your explanations even though it was a foreign concept to her just minutes ago.
Maybe she'll be a bit better now?

Magnavous proves to be an exceptionally quick study, and before long she's creating her own air runes with little issue at all. Her propensity to destroy her surroundings with her magic doesn't seem to extend to runecrafting, to which you're incredibly thankful.
This is fantastic! Thank you so much.
It's not a problem at all, I'm happy to help.
Now, maybe I can start a bit smaller...
Well, before you do, how would you feel about using a staff?
They helped me focus my magic in the past, but...
My father stopped getting them for me since they got blown up so quickly...
I see. Well, maybe now that you'll be trying with spells a little more suitable to your skill level, it'll go a touch better?
What'll I do if I break it though..?
I'll make sure to bring a few spares.
I'll try practicing with the smaller spells in the meantime! Oh! And maybe I'll make a couple extra runes...
As you leave Magnavous behind in the crater, you hear a reassuring lack of explosions or other generalized destruction.
Surely... Surely, teaching her to arm herself can't go wrong.
I have faith in her. Kind of.

The crater is no better or worse than you left it, which you'll take as progress. You find Magnavous trying to wash away bits of ash and charred trees with a few well-placed water spells. More often than not the spells completely gouge chunks of earth from the ground, but they more-or-less seem to be going where she's aiming, at least.
Hello! I'm getting better, I almost don't destroy everything now!
Well, that's something! Maybe with these, you'll fare even better!
They're beautiful! I think these will be perfect for me.
Thank you, thank you, I try.
Soon enough, I'll be able to meet Morlin, and then I'll be able to become a mage worth speaking about, with all of my own tales and adventures...
There's a chance your father may have...
I know it might be har-
Yeah. I mean, look around. This is what my magic was like after years of practice.
I got my family into trouble in the capital dozens of times because of my... studies.
Being exiled out here isn't all bad, and the fact that Morlin is close... Well, just a happy accident, I suppose!
You're still going to go looking for Morlin anyway?
Why not? With your help, I'm actually starting to become a bit competent, and if he's just found some new big site to work on...
Any hands would be helpful, I'm sure.
And if you learn a couple things along the way, help him out here and there...
He might legitimately make me his apprentice!
That's not a half bad idea at all.
But... before I go... I don't have any more essence. I feel like I'm right on the edge of a breakthrough, could you please get just a bit more for me?
You sigh, but head off to fetch some more essence to keep Magnavous's studies going somewhat smoothly. If she claims she's close to a breakthrough, might as well foster it.

As you come back with essence for Magnavous, you see that the crater is... substantially better? She looks to you with tears in her eyes, before dropping the remnants of a staff and rushing towards you. She wraps you in a hug as you notice that she managed to-you presume-use a combination of water and air spells to clean the ash and soot from her previous attempts as studying, and remove most of the land back to its original shape.

The land is damaged, but her efforts to fix it are clear as day, and you congratulate her on her training and give her a brief hug back. She thanks you for acting as her first mentor, and says that she thinks she's ready to trouble Morlin. You check over her gear and give her the essence and send her on her way. She turns back a few times as she walks off, waving and paying you more compliments than you feel you deserve. You feel as if you've learned just as much as her, just in a different way.

The Harvest Festival - Azamire's Annual Harvest Festival is right around the corner, and everyone is doing their part to help make it as great as it can be. Of course, the town will need your help to make it happen!
I'm not too sure how much they'll need... let's get quite a bit.

On one of your many frequent outings to Lira's tavern, Hapren sets his sights on you, and immediately beelines over to where you're seated in the corner. He pushes your books aside and flags Lira down, who immediately catches your eye and gives you a sheepish look. She waves away a serving girl who started to walk over, and takes a seat next to you.
Well well well, isn't it funny running into you here?
When I'm not training or adventuring, I'm basically always here, studying a bit... Why would it be funny to run into me here...
Wait, I actually just came in like... two minutes ago. Have you been followin-
What is important is that you deeply care for this town, just like me, right?
The Harvest Festival is coming up, and we're behind. Please?
But where's the fun in that?
Plus... it's kinda a lot. Lira needs help too.
I was kinda the one who told him when you come in here... sorry.
It's okay, but when this is all done, I want enough ale that I cannot walk out of here. Or hear Hapren begging for more assistance.

The two of them go through a whirlwind of planning, talking about decor, food, games, and more while you struggle to both keep up and see your part in it all. Eventually you just settle into the corner and continue pouring over a map you bought off a local surveyor some time ago, until finally, Hapren asks if you caught all of that.

You shake yourself from your stupor and Lira asks if you could bring them enough maple logs to keep the bonfire going, and cook the food for festival. You nod and head out, happy to be away from their prattling.
I'm going to need you to grow... a bit faster.
They haven't been being very specific about how much stuff they want...
As you drop off the last load of wood, Hapren claps his hands and pats you on the shoulder, pleased with your work.
Well done! It's genuinely kind of startling just how much you can accomplish.
Well, if it's for Lira and the festival, I'm happy to do it.
Right over here, just checking out what you dropped off! These will be great for the food.
Yeah? I can't say I've experimented much with the logs I use...
For some dishes, I'd argue it's even more important than the spices you use. These maple logs will give our dish a sweet, smoky flavor.
Speaking of this dish, I assume we're making Azabuns this year?
Well of course! We might as well not have the festival at all without 'em! But... we're missing something.
Well, our Harvest Festival is to celebrate... you guessed it, Azamire's harvest, but just like in my pantry, some food has gone missing. But I can't be fussed with that right now.
We need a fair bit more corn. I've seen you tending the fields from time to time, is that something you can handle?
I'll be back before you know it!

You set off for the fields, ready to bolster the last bit of Azamire's harvest for the year, with a bit of your own hard work. Hapren looks on expectantly, waiting to see if you say anything about helping him as well, then turns to Lira with a sad face. She only shakes her head and walks away.
Take one, cook it, pass it on. Take on, cook it, pass it on...
I think that's almost all of them.

You enter the tavern and sling several sacks of corn onto the bar, to which Lira immediately jumps up from her stool, inspects several ears, and nods positively towards you. Without a word, she pushes a tankard of ale into your hands, and waits for you to drink it down.
Thank you, but what's this for?
The start of that payment we talked about.
You know, you ask for ale as payment... often... I know I'm a tavern keeper, but I care for you. Is everything okay at home?
What..? Yes, of course! Your ale is just to die for, and you know I like the house blend more than anything.
What do you even put in it?
Well, a bit of coriander, hibiscus, juniper berries, orange peel... But I can't tell you the rest of course, I don't want to lose my leverage over you.
But, speaking of recipes, this corn was the last thing we needed for the Melvor-famous Azabuns!
I'll be calling in some people to help assemble them, but I'll need your help cooking them.
I don't trust these vagabonds to not burn the food, or themselves, but I know you're capable.

Lira lets out a loud whistle, and like a well-oiled machine the entire tavern pushes the tables together and drapes several clean cloths over them. It'd look like the start of a banquet if it wasn't for the crates of raw ingredients starting to be distributed among the patrons and the couple dozen more citizens that have started filtering in. 

The townsfolk crack open the boxes and barrels of raw food and water and get to work in a show of efficency that shocks you. You wonder if Lira has access to some form of magic to make them work with such a fervor. But as you start to guess at her powers, you see tankards distributed and filled as Lira walks around checking progress. Seems you're not the only one taking drinks as payment.
I hope these turn out nicely.

With a good chunk of the town working on them, and a few of Lira's staff helping cook the buns, the work goes faster than expected. It certainly helps that the townsfolk keep the atmosphere lively with several songs while they work and drink, though most of them would be more applicable to working in fields or mines, instead of assembling cute buns.

As you finish, Lira tops off your tankard before she notices someone off near the edge of the tavern. She quickly grabs a tankard from someone nearby who knows better than to argue, and then thrusts it into your hands, then hurries away. You down your fresh drink first, wondering why she gave you another, until-
Hello there! How goes the assembly line? Are you free for a second or several?
Nothing, nothing. Think we're about finished up here, what else do you need?
I've got a lovely idea to light up the town square. I hope to fill some lanterns with some gems from the town's treasury, and when they're lit... I hope it'll glitter beautifully.
That's actually... a pretty good idea. Are you worried about thieves at all, though? Sounds like a lot of loot to be leaving out.
They'll be under watch, don't you worry. I've already signed off on the gems being used, but there's just one thing...
You don't have the lanterns and want me to make them?
This is why I always come to you for help! You're always one step ahead of everyone else.
...I'll try to be a little less competent in the future.
Last thing, I promise. For this event, that is.

You leave the assembly line behind as they begin to tidy up and return the tavern back to its usual configuration. Hapren calls out several thank yous as you leave, but you don't turn, lest he throw on another task or two should you pay him any further mind.

Hapren happily takes the lanterns from you, passing them down a line where a few of Azamire's guards-headed by Jass-drop gemstones into the lanterns and get them hung up. People begin filtering into the square as the sun slowly slips below the horizon. You can't help but start getting swept up in the excitement as more and more of the modest town square is filled with decor, food, and life.

People from all walks of life stop by, many from Azamire, but some from the surrounding villages, bringing plenty of their own special dishes, songs, and traditional garb. Many are just variations on one another, but the differences really stand out between each other.

You dance late into the night and-of course-enjoy your fill of Azabuns and other regional delicacies, pleased with your contributions to the festival, even if you really think Hapren should enlist some more help next time.
Setting Down Roots - The Blackthorn Sisters have made one of their frequent appearances in Azamire, but seem to have brought a bit more than their usual cart of goods. What brings them to town today?
I wonder what ever happened to this place?
Should be cleaned up enough now. [Talk]

You walk up to the large vine and pelt-covered wagon that has parked itself on the edge of town. You see two familiar faces, Petal and Clove, sisters that stop by and sell herbs, potions, pelts, and meat. They sit in front of an old burned-out house on the back of a large wagon packed with furniture, discussing plans for what their new home should look like.
Looks like you've brought a bit more than potions and meat this time, eh?
It's so nice to see you again, it's been too long!
We finally bit the arrow and decided to set up shop here. It's what Petal wants to do, at least.
Come now, you know I'm looking out for the both of us.
Plus, Azamire has always been one of our most lucrative stops. Who knows, with how fast this place is growing, maybe we'll do even better than before!
Azamire might be where I rest, but the woods will always be my home. I can't stay tied down for too long.
Well, I hope that we'll be able to do our best to make you feel welcome, regardless of where you may be.
Oh, don't mind Clove, she's just... trying to appear strong and mysterious.
You know, she always gets excited whenever we get close to Azamire, starts trying to take down big game to show off to yo-
Petal, I prefer animals and monsters, but I can make an exception.
I'm just teasing you. Just saying that settling down isn't all bad.
There's certainly worse places to go, I can tell you that.
Though... I can't say you two have picked the most... lovely of spots in Azamire.
Your mayor said that we could have the place for free, as long as we got it all fixed up.
There's so much space for a nice little garden in the back as well! I might not have to constantly trek into the woods to get basic herbs anymore.
If only there was some strong, helpful individual who'd be willing to help break down all the rubble...
...For a healthy bundle of herbs and meat when we get established?
Pass me a shovel, I've got my pickaxe right here.

Petal claps her hands and motions for Clove to hand you a shovel. She rolls her eyes and scoffs, but noticeably shies away-just a bit-when you take it from her. The house is a mess, but the foundation is still good. With a lot of work, it's in a great spot in town, and could be a wonderful home and shop.
I wonder what Clove might find for dinner. [Provide] X/X [Steel Arrows] - [Fletching Tab Link]

Both Petal and Clove work on the house while you break up and remove the rubble. Petal tends to the wild tangle of plants out back, while Clove always seems to be nearby, either breaking down old furniture with a hefty axe, or sweeping up in the spots you've finished. While the two of you work, Clove tries to strike up bits of conversation while Petal stays mysteriously absent, even when she finishes up outside.
I guess sticking around here won't be all bad.
No? I don't think so. I get out quite a bit, but it's always nice to have somewhere to come back to.
It doesn't ever feel... smothering? Knowing that people might wonder where you are, fuss after you...
Well, yeah, of course, but she's my sister. I don't know, I guess... I don't want folks to start expecting anything of me.
I don't think you'll need to worry too much about that. There's plenty of odd folks around here, you'll fit right in.
Gee, thanks, I feel welcome already.
Any time. I'm kidding, of course, but really, unless you're someone like Lira, who runs the tavern, most people just... go about their days.
Plus, you're a hunter, it's kind of normal that you'll head out for days or even weeks at a time, depending on your mark.
Speaking of which... I don't know the lands too well, I'm used to throwing myself into the woods wherever we travel and just making the best of it.
But... I think I'll actually start being able to hone my craft a bit, sticking in once place for a while... Getting familar with the landscape and hunting grounds.
I might look around a little bit now, and find us some dinner, actually. If you think you can manage without me, that is.
However... I hope to find us some dinner, too. I know Petal won't let you leave here without feeding you. By any chance, would you happen to have some arrows I could use?
We made a long trek to get here, and I've gone through most of my stock.

You chuckle at the idea of needing to manage without her, then having her turn around and ask you for help instead. You head out to find some, and as you do, you walk past Petal, who has a dozen or so people in tow, all armed with various tools or carrying lumber. Shockingly efficient, that one.
This stuff grows worse than most weeds. [Cut] X/X [Ambervine Bush] - [Woodcutting Tab Link]

The arrows you hand to Clove aren't anything special, yet she still takes plenty of time running through a handful of them, inspecting their quality and bend, along with the arrow tips at the end of each, before giving a self-assured nod. She gives a little wave before heading out.
You know, where we come from, giving someone arrows for a hunt is as good as a proposal for marriage?
Taking an arrow to the shin, I believe it's called, though hardly anyone still believes in that silly custom.
Is that so? And where exactly might that be?
It's from a district in the capital I highly doubt you've gotten to, don't worry about following up on it.
With your professions, I'm surprised you both came from the capital. What made you turn from the city to being...
A couple of women who trek through the boonies and sleep in the dirt?
Spend that much time around that many people and see what you think of it after a couple decades.
I think we just wanted out, a bit of room to stretch our legs and see what the world had to offer.
And now you're settling back down.
Oh, I'm sure we'll still go out and visit all the corners of Melvor from time to time, but you know, neither of us are getting any younger.
And it's nice to have an occasional bath from time to time. Hard to find that out on the road.
I can only imagine. But with how fast your house got put up, I'm sure you could have a whole bathhouse put up in a couple hours if you were so inclined.
How'd you get those townsfolk to come and help you so fast?
Well, those farmers have plenty of pest issues, I hear, and I just so happen to dabble in poisons along with my normal stock of potions.
Got anything you think might be handy against... bigger beasts?
Not just yet, but I'll keep you in the know. Along with those, I'm working on some herbicides too... took care of most of the tangle in the back, except for those damn Ambervines.
I'd ask Clove to go whack them with that axe of hers, but you seemed to have scared her off. Be a dear, would you?

You roll your eyes and set to work on the brush behind the house, knocking down the Ambervine where you can. Like Petal claimed, many of the other noxious plants that were back here seem to have withered away.
Hopefully Petal hasn't severely poisoned the ground. [Plant] X/X [Sunflower] - [Farming Tab Link]
Huh, well, I guess the herbalist knows what she's doing. Who'd guess? [Complete Quest Button]
You wipe your brow and just start to lean back against the wall of the house when Clove comes in the newly constructed gate and drops several birds on the ground and sets her bow on a nearby crate.
From smacking rocks to whacking bushes, you truly are a menace to the natural world.
Those birds might say the same about you.
I don't think they'd be saying much of anything at all, anymore. I didn't give them the chance.
You might have sampled one too many of your sister's potions if you think that bushes are any more talkative.
Are you about done brutalizing the shrubbery?
They'll bother you no longer, m'lady.
Wonderful! Then there's just one final thing for you left to do!
Where'd the rest of your helpers go?
Back to their homes, but they don't get to have dinner here. You do.
Plus, it'll put a smile on my dear sister's face. You'd like that, wouldn't you?
Goodness Petal, just get on with it!
Like I mentioned, I want to start growing my own herbs, but I know that blight can be a nasty beast to deal with this time of year.
A few sunflowers can do wonders at holding it and a surprising amount of other types of corruption off.
And how will that put a smile on Clove's face, exactly?
They just make me happy... I don't know, always liked 'em.
But that hardly matters, the garden is going to be important for keeping any kind of livelihood goin' while we get set up.
I just hope Petal's herbicides aren't still lingering around.
They shouldn't be, but if you start to feel strange, please take extensive notes, I might want to replicate it for my poisons!

Petal looks a bit too excited at the prospect of you getting sick from her treated land, while Clove occasionally stops by to check if you're feeling off at all before quickly dismissing herself each time.

As you finish up with the flowers, you catch a whiff of Petal's cooking and let yourself inside. The place isn't 'homey' just yet, but it's far better than the wreck it was just a bit ago, and trust the two of them will give it the final touch-ups it needs.

Clove sets the table and waves you away when you try to help, so you turn to Petal, who brushes past you with three steaming birds balanced on her arm, with a pitcher of... something in the other. 
Using herbs she'd gathered, Petal seasoned the meat to perfection, and Clove produces a few fruits she collected while she was hunting. They pair beautifully with the... concoction that Petal assures you is safe to drink. It's sickly sweet and could be considered tasty, if it weren't for the fact that it leaves you feeling as though you've plunged into an icy lake, but only for a few moments after each sip

Petal pushes your chair towards Clove's every once in a while, and slowly but surely she begins to turn bright red, but plays it off casually. Eventually, you all finish your meals, and Petal takes down a few notes as to how you felt while you drink her beverage. They both thank you for your time, and encourage you to come back once they've set up shop.
A Glittering Trap - Gol has been tasked with taking down a beast near Azamire, and what good would a battle be without a friend by your side?
Let's make sure these are sturdy enough to handle... whatever we're fighting. [Provide] X/X [Rune Spear] - [Fletching Tab Link]
These look good, let's get Gol. [Talk]

A small crowd has gathered around in a tight semi-circle near the front of The Spiced Honey Tavern. There are folks cheering, exclaiming for more or begging to be let into the 'act'. Never one to sit out an exciting moment, you make your way into the throngs of people and find Gol, a towering man with more muscles than sense. He sits under a table and hoists it into the air while several tipsy patrons delicately balance on top of it. He laughs as one of them pours a tankard in his mouth from above, then gently lowers the table back down to the ground. He flexes for the crowd as more people climb onto the table, but he stops mid-pose as his eyes meet yours.
Gol must cease his entertainment for now, good people, for Gol has found his friend!
Of course! You've been instrumental in Gol's rise from a coinless pauper to what he has become today!
I will say, you are looking a bit more... put together than last time.
That he is! After Gol's travels, he has found many a coin, armed himself better than before, and is now ready to lead his friend to the same riches!
Well... I can't say that I'm not a little interested in what you had in mind, but really, that's not necessary. I'm just happy to see you on your feet, and a bit more clothed than last time.
Gol must insist! Gol has been tasked with slaying a beast just a short jaunt from here, and with your assistance, Gol is sure to be successful once again!
You may not help Gol fight the creature directly, but setting up a site to fight it is very okay!
Oh? And what might it be?
Why remember silly details like the beast's name? Gol only remembers where the beast resides, along with its penchant for gems and shiny things.
...I'm slightly surprised you used penchant successfully...
Depending on the day, I’m not sure I’d use that correctly myself.
Gol is smarter than he looks The brain is a muscle just like all others, and should be exercised to keep it sharp.
To become smart like Gol, every day, you must split a log with nothing but your head.
Your vision may go fuzzy... and your sense of smell may never be the same. But nothing beats the first time you're able to stoke a fire with wood you've splintered with your own body.
More and more by the minute.
But... concerning training aside, it really is good to see you well, Gol. I'm down for your adventure. What do we need?
Gol knew you would be! Gol will lead the way, his sense of direction has been honed as well.
But before we depart, Gol would like spears, and many of them.
The beast Gol has been entrusted to slay is a slippery one, and we will need to prepare an arena to fight it in.
What'll you be doing in the meantime?
He will consult with the locals to ensure the best path to the beast. Best of luck, friend.

You watch as Gol dusts himself off and waves to the crowd that has lingered, likely hoping for a bit more amusement before they get on with their days. He calls for Lira with a bit more warmth and familiarity than you were expecting, then the door to the tavern swings shut.
I feel like I'm arming Gol for war, I hope whatever it is goes down quickly. [Provide] X/X [Rune Javelin] - [Fletching Tab Link]
We'll have a problem if this isn't enough. [Talk]

With your rune spears in tow, you enter the Spiced Honey Tavern and find Gol with several maps laid out in front of him, with a surprisingly methodical route planned out for your journey. Lira comes by and tops off his tankard.
Ah, and here's your friend now! You two stay safe, okay?
Gol is always safe, but he will also ensure his friend's safety as well. You have Gol's word.
I'll hold you to that. Best of luck!
You two seem to get along nicely.
Lira appreciates Gol's humor and physique in equal measure, along with his ability to drink as much as half her tavern.
Gol also helps move things around, from time to time.
I feel as if you could help her relocate the whole building if you set your mind to it.
The flimsy building would not hold up to Gol's might. Trust Gol. He has tried before.
Than you have nothing to fear, friend!
Gol's only enemies are beasts, monsters, and taxes.
Not the people that robbed you when we first met?
How'd they pull one over on you, anyway? You're a mountain of a man.
Nay. Gol refuses to fight people unless his life depends on it.
Gol has spilled enough blood of his countrymen, Gol wishes to do so no longer.
Indeed. But this talk has excited Gol. Have you got the spears?
Would you be willing to make some that are also... smaller?
They're... somewhere between bolts and spears, I'd say.
Then yes, that is what Gol desires! Gol will meet you on the outskirts of town when you are done.

You set off to procure some javelins as well, wondering what kind of beast might need both to take down. You hear a couple passerby call out to Gol, asking if he can spare a moment to help them right an overturned wagon, to which he laughs and asks them to lead the way.
Let's hope that payout is as good as he claims.
This should be enough to fill a chest or two. [Talk]

The javelins have a good heft, and feel solid enough for whatever Gol intends. You wish-not for the first time-that you had more information about what you'd be fighting, but shockingly feel that Gol has the situation handled. The man's... unique, but certainly capable.

When you meet him, he takes the javelins from you and seems pleased, then leads the way deep into the woods. He seems confident about his heading and leads you to a large outcropping that juts from the sand.
This will be an excellent place to lure the sea beast to!
The sand will dry it out, and the rock will give us solid ground to fight upon, as long as the tide is low.
Oh, you were being literal when you mentioned it being a slippery beast?
Aye, so Gol was told, at least. A slimy one at that.
Out of water, its eyesight is poor, and the beast is said to be quite daft. Gol hopes to lure it up here from the water after preparing a battleground of sorts.
I'll leave the spears with you then, I'm sure you've got something in mind?
Gol is something of a visionary when it comes to these kinds of things.
Gol has fallen for many a trap in his day, he knows how to think like these beasts.
You mentioned it likes shiny things too, hm?
That it does! Again, much like Gol. The beast has good tastes.
We will make it seem as if a ship carrying riches has run aground, and spilled forth its plunder.
There are many wrecks along the coast here, we shall bring them here when the tide rises.
I uh... Don't think I can move whole chunks of ship, Gol.
No, no, of course not. You are better for the finer details, friend, Gol will handle the heavy lifting.
Could you get the gems while Gol finishes up here?
Sounds like a plan to me! See you soon.

As you head off, Gol sets to work on relocating some of the coastal debris. He sinks his fingers into the spongy wood of the back quarter of a wrecked schooner. It's far from a full boat, sure, but even Gol looks small next to it. His feet sink into the sand as he begins to push, and sure enough, the wreck begins to move-slowly but surely-across the sand.
I'll make this extra messy, so it glows even brighter.
This should be everything we need. - [Complete Quest Button]

You return to the ambush site with enough gems to fill a small chest and find Gol perched on top of his handiwork. The tide is higher than before, sea foam curls and retreats just over the edge of the outcrop. Gol's scene is extraordinarily convincing, with the wreckage arranged to look as though a ship washed ashore and was split on the rocky outcrop. He even seems to have relocated the mast of another ship and propped it up on the wreck, allowing the tattered sail to tangle itself nicely amongst the debris. You carefully wade through the waist-deep water, avoiding the spears jutting out of the sand, and clamber onto the rocky platform.
Gol... this is scarily good. You've really outdone yourself!
What can Gol say? He has a knack for setting a good scene.
The gems look lovely as well. If Gol hadn't assembled this himself, Gol may even wander into this ambush.
Well, do your best not to. You mentioned that the beast had a bounty on its head, yeah?
That it does! It has been tearing through ships like Gol does ale. That's why Gol had this idea in the first place.
Good line of reasoning, I'd say. So... will the gems be enough, do you think?
Our hook is good, but Gol thinks we lack bait, still.
Gol is a bit more keen on the... pugilistic arts, and rarely has the patience for fishing.
Gol wonders if you know a good way to lure the creature into our ambush.
If I were to take some Glowfin and cut them up, I'd say the bait would be pretty convincing for a sea-based monster.
This does sound promising. Gol will put the finishing touches on our battleground while you handle the bait?

You nod and set off to gather enough Glowfin bait to lure whatever creature this may be to shore. Gol immediately gets to work on the finer details, putting a surprising amount of care into perfecting the wreck, making it truly look natural.

Gol seems positively buzzing with energy, pleased to see the plan come together. Gol did a phenomenal job making the wreck look natural, which was only further helped by the tide coming through and helping the wreckage sink into the sand. 

You do your best to squeeze the glowfin bait's juice all around the chest before tucking it in amongst the gemstones. In the twilight, the chest looks like a burning beacon, with the glowfin juice refracting off the gemstones radiantly.

Gol leads you away from the chest and you scrub your hands in the water, careful to avoid impaling yourself on the spears tucked into the sand all around your ambush site. After an hour or so of waiting in the water, a wet, hulking monster slowly lifts itself out of the sea and half walks, half slithers towards the gem-filled chest. 

Gol slaps your shoulder hard enough to dislocate it, silently yelling in excitment before leaping out of the water and towards the beast, who hardly knows what to make out of the golith running towards it. Gol tosses javelin after javelin, their rune blades sinking into the creature's slimy flesh. He narrowly tucks its large, snapping maw as it turns to retreat towards the water. Like a fish on a barb, the angled spears it walked over now impale it and it shrieks, tearing off long, writhing tail in the process. Gol tries his best to keep hold of the creature, but its thick slime coats him entirely, and it just manages to slip back into the ocean, but not unscathed.

Gol is pleased regardless, claiming that the tail is enough to show most of you twos' efforts. True to his word, he finds you in Azamire several days later with your half of the payout, and you feel it was well-worth the time... but part of you wonders if there's a way to track the beast down and take it out once and for all.

The Four Sentries - Morlin and his crew have made substantial progress in unearthing the lost civilization you helped uncover, but have run into another roadblock. With your help, perhaps you'll finally uncover the city proper?
They're asking for stuff without even seeing me, now...

You stumble across Magnavous bumbling through Azamire's square, asking people if they've seen you. Many either shake their heads or mention your various comings and goings, but few have solid answers as to where she could look next. You stand back and watch as she shakes down a couple others, who point you out. She looks pleased to have come across you, and quite a bit more sure of herself than the last time you saw her. She still firmly clutches one of the staves you made her, but she walks far more proudly and confidently.
Having fun standing there and watching me? You could have come and said hello.
You got there eventually! I wanted to see how long it'd take.
Well, if you've had your fun, we must make haste! I have so much to show you!
Wait, he's officially your mentor now?
Indeed! With no small part thanks to your help, but I will catch you up along the way.
The long and short of it-which you'll see when we get there-is that Whudgrath has uncovered what seems to be the gates to the city.
What? Like one of these would ever be simple.
Imagine that. You come out to find me and say, "Hey [i]{0}[/i], things were incredibly easy and straightforward."
"We've taken care of all the hard work, come and collect as many armfuls of treasure as you desire."
Well... yeah, when you put it that way....
Well, the stone is getting harder to work through. Morlin thinks that it may be magically enhanced since we're getting closer to the city.
I have a theory that the properties of Dawnsteel may be enough to get through it but...
With all of my magical studies, I wouldn't say I'm particularly suited for mining work.
Nothing to be ashamed of. There's a reason Morlin hired a dwarven crew, eh?
I'll meet you on the edge of town when I'm ready.

You head off in search of enough material to outfit Whudgrath's crew, and then some. No use needing to come back half a dozen times because they needed more tools. Plus, the more useful you make yourself, you could argue in favor of a bigger cut.
I'm sure this is what I need to do.
Let's see if this stops that vapor. [Insert]

With enough Dawnsteel to outfit a small army, you meet up with Magnavous. She takes you out to the dig site, which has seen some drastic changes since you were here last. The hillside has been completely carved away, revealing that most of what you'd seen previously were ancillary buildings, and possibly even a second, more recent town built over the top of it within the last couple hundred years, according to Magnavous.

Whudgrath meets up with you shortly into your tour of the site, and happily takes the Dawnsteel from you. He leads you on a short walk down a carved out recess in the ground, that ends in two massive doors which rival the capital's famous gate. It’s dim, the ceiling not yet fully carved away, but even so you can make out four enormous slouched statues set into the walls, with all of them being about five times your size, even hunched over as they are. They're all quite weathered, but it's still clear to see they were modeled after wizards of their time, each with painted stone robes and outstretched but empty hands. Most noticeably, they are very obviously not human. They all have four arms and long, rectangular faces. Each has a gemstone set into its forehead and seems to emanate a vapor of some kind...
Lovely work you've got here... Don't know if you made these or found 'em, but my boys will appreciate it nonetheless.
Ha! Won't even make you swing a pick this time, think Morlin's got some more important work for ya.
Yeah? Is it down that same tunnel we found past that cursed door, or... is it... this?
Ah, that little passage! Turns out, that was a teeny little side exit that workers used to use...
Think it ended up leading to a bunkhouse or somethin'.
We think these doors lead to the city proper.
I'll spare you the finer details, but Whudgrath and his crew have carved out the whole hillside, and we haven't found another way in.
And I don't assume we can just dig around the doors?
Be a pretty terrible gate if we could, hm?
Much of what Whudgrath’s crew has dug through seems to be more... loose. The stone of the entrance is magically reinforced.
To find a way to undo it. So, we're stuck with the door.
I see. I don't suppose you've tried knocking?
It was the first thing Whudgrath did.
I blew up a lil' bit.
Never better! But now I'm pretty keen on opening it up too. Gotta be something good in there, I'm sure.
Set into the four statues are a set of passages, which, roughly translated, talk about being sealed, armed, and adorned.
Well, they're wizards, so armed and adorned likely mean... staves and jewelry. As far as sealed though... Maybe it'd stop whatever it is that they're... leaking.
Ah, the vapor. Morlin took a look at it earlier, worried it was poisonous. It was magical in nature, but it’s anyone’s guess what it was.
Any clue on how we can plug them up?
I had a stint in a military company a while back, and it always seemed that the crossbowmen were the best answer to riddling those flimsy little mages with bolts.
The gemstones of the four mages stick out to you, and make the answer feel rather clear. If you're to make bolts to 'seal' them, they'd likely line up with the gemstone motif they have going on.
That seems... pretty sensible, though... morbid.
We'll give it a shot, then.

Before you head out, you inspect each of the statues once more while Magnavous and Whudgrath set to work on their own tasks. The site still needs a lot of work. The gate is barely lit by what little sunlight filters in from outside and the few lanterns at its base. You're sure you'll get a better look at the statues when the chamber is fully prepped, but the gemstones still catch the faint cavern light perfectly as you look them over. Topaz, sapphire, ruby, and emerald - all gemstones that'd fit neatly as tips of your bolts.

Feeling self-assured, you head off to prepare to seal the four sentries.
At least I know I'm helping her confidence.

Gemstone-tipped bolts in-hand, you slowly work your way around each of the statues. Each fits in the openings nicely, and lock into place with a firm and resonate snap. Magnavous begins to do the same while Whudgrath holds a lantern aloft. Soon enough, the vapor that twisted and curled up towards the ceiling has been stopped. All at once, the statues seem to heave and twist. Where they once hunched and gaunt, sealing them seems to have changed the stone outright, causing the figures to warp into more imposing, able-bodied versions of themselves.
Step one down, two more to go. They seem to be in fighting shape...
Now, I'm as game for a scrap as anyone, but you don't find it concerning at all, giving them weapons?
It feels right. Besides, I'd say they feel more like guardians of this place than combatants.
Right, and... do you think the city's guardians would take too kindly to us plundering their home?
I'll call Morlin in soon, once we determine what we'll arm them with. He'll be able to protect us, if they decide we're a threat.
I'll do my best to appear... friendly. How's my smile?
...It reminds me of a dog baring its teeth...
Hmm. Maybe a no on the smile then.
The four of them look like mages, just like you Magnavous.
And you made me this delightful staff. Think you could do the same here? One for each of the base elements?
They'd be a bit more like toothpicks for them, no?
Well, Morlin has been teaching me this spell that allows me to take multiple items and combine them into a much larger version of themselves.
How oddly convenient... How'd that come up?
It was in his first published book, "101 Spells To Make You A Master Wizard!" I've been trying to get through them all since I got here.
Huh, alright... Seems simple enough. So, you probably just need a couple of each staff, or..?
Well... I'm not too good at it yet. We've been running all over this dig site for a while now, I haven't had long to practice.
But you can do it, right?
Yes! But... it's just not very efficient yet.

Part of you wishes that Morlin could just come do the spell, but deep down, you know it'll be good for Magnavous to do this for her training. At the very least, it'll help her feel a bit more confident, even if it does mean you have to make... substantially more staves.
You know, that old man makes a good point...
I hope this works...  [Complete Quest Button]

As you hand the staves to Magnavous one by one, they slowly but surely get combined into one. Eventually, they get big enough that Whudgrath and his crew take over in holding them, and then placing them into the statues’ hands. When the four of them are armed, they slam them into the ground and the orb at the end of each begins to glow.

Morlin enters, and lets out a low whistle when he sees the progress that has been made.
My my my, I see you all have been making good progress!
That we have! And what have you been up to?
I've been here for... quite a while.
Do you see this beard? Just how old do you think I am? You've got to stay well rested at my age.
Plus, my apprentice is becoming quite capable! Thank you for helping her out, by the way. Both here, and before she found her way to the site.
I think Azamire would be a burning crater if I didn't, but it's my pleasure. She's quite capable.
Enough about me, we've only got one more thing to do before we're done!
That's right, but I have no idea what to adorn them in. They've already got... robes, kind of.
This is where a master wizard comes into play, children.
They're clearly missing their swag, as the kids say.
I've never heard a kid say that.
Have to say I'm in agreement.
Well, you clearly aren't hip, like old man Morlin. Behold!

Morlin throws back his robes to show off a concerning amount of jewelry. Dozens of necklaces, bracelets, and rings adorn his body. They sparkle brilliantly in the low-light, so much so that you worry you'd be blinded if it was any brighter in the cavern. He goes on to talk about how most keep it far too simple, limiting themselves to only a few enchanted pieces of jewelry at a time, but that a master wizard such as himself isn't held back by such limitations. Whudgrath asks if they can just use his jewelry, to which he scoffs. He glances over the statues and produces a list.


Much like last time he tried to make a list, the first page is cryptic, detailing something about an excitable lizard housekeeper and her many cleaning adventures, but he burns it before you can get more than a glance as to its contents. He hands the veritable laundry list of jewelry to you, and assures you that your efforts will be reflected in your cut of... whatever may lie inside.

Everyone begins layering on the amulets as best they can, taking wild guesses as to how many and where they should be placed. The four statues begin to look positively gaudy by the time you finish, and you start to wonder if it would have been better to use the same enlargement spell as you used for the staves... just as the first of the four begins to stir.

The adornments melt into their stone skin, and each statue's eyes begin to light up one by one, shining with an eerie energy. Magnavous ducks behind you, and Whudgrath behind her, while Morlin waves his staff menacingly at the statues. You all sit in a tense silence as seconds feel as if they stretch into minutes. The statues slam their staves into the ground once again, this time eliciting a shriek from... Morlin, your mighty protector.

In tandem, the statues take position by the colossal gate, and each hammers their staff against it one after another, the whacks shaking the cavern enough to knock you all to your knees. When the sentries cease, they begin to push arduously against it, the bolts you pressed into them fragmenting and shooting out from the gaps in their facades, letting the vapor they held back rise towards the cavern's ceiling once more. 

Slowly but surely, the gate grinds open, and the statues don't let up until the doors scrape to a halt. With that, they wander into the darkness, leaving you all behind, wondering what lies beyond the gate.

The Sealed Grove - The leader of Azamire's forces has some concerns about a nearby grove that seems tainted by some kind of dark energy. With the situation beginning the spiral out of control, she has called in the best Azamire has to offer.
These trees almost grow faster than I can chop them down!
I think I see a clearing up ahead! [Push]

On a stroll by what was once the Soothsayer's Grove, you find yourself startled as a blue vine whips out and lashes itself around your ankles. Startled by the intrusion, you barely have the chance to think about how this was meant to be a 'safe path' until you're hoisted up into the air and tossed around. Suddenly, a tall, dark-haired woman jumps out from the darkness and cleaves the vines in two with a single swipe of her sword, sending you back towards the ground, where you land with a thud.
Ow... Thank you... I think? What are you doing so far from Azamire, Jass? Aren't the militia lost without you?
What are you doing near the Soothsayer's Grove? Haven't you seen all the signs I've put up?
Do the signs say, "Beware dangerous sentient vines?"
No, they say, "Danger," and "Stay Out!" Someone or something, is causing everything around this place to go absolutely wild.
You should really consider my sign idea, it's a lot less vague.
Would you have stayed out if that's what they said instead?
...No, I would have thought that I could have handled some silly little vines. Point taken.
I wish I knew. Every attempt I've made to get closer to the grove has been met with vines, trees and the occasional monster.
Well, no one throws me in the air and gets away with it! Plus, I ought to help you, since you saved me.
Can you keep me on the ground if I cut a path through to the grove?
I've done it once already, haven't I? Grab an axe, we're going to make some kindling out of this grove.

As if it heard Jass's threat, more vines snaked out from the underbrush and towards you. True to her word, Jass takes a firm stance and chops through them like a butcher hacking through meat, giving you an opening to make your way towards the grove.
Surely Gol will be able to handle... Whatever is in this forest.
Back into the woods we go. [Talk]

The bushes and trees are thick, and for every one you chop down, it feels as though three more shoot up in their place. Their rapid growth would be a lot more impressive if it wasn't for its murderous intent. How they stay out of sight is a mystery, but as you cut deeper into the tangle of plants, thunderous bellows and growls sound from nearby creatures you feel lucky not to encounter.

You do your best to make your way inward, and eventually, the outer thicket gives way to a calmer bit of forest. Jass catches her breath and wipes the vegetation from her sword and armor. The two of you stand on a ridgeline surrounding a deep crater, filled with plantlife you've never seen anywhere else. It almost looks like a jungle, with dark trees towering from the pit and threatening to spill out. All manner of dark shadows prowl through the vegetation, and you're very happy to be far above it, at least for now.
You're not going to like what I have to say.
We are going to have to go down there, aren't we?
What? No, absolutely not. You can practically see the evil leaking out of the grove.
We're going to have to cut out way back out.
Honestly, I like the sound of that a lot better than wandering down there. But why'd we come in here in the first place, then?
