I wanted to see for my own eyes how much the jungle in the crater had progressed, before we did.
It's not good. The crater itself was barren at first, except for a singular pale, twisted tree in the very center. This whole jungle has sprouted up in just a few days...
The thicket around the crater-which we just hacked through-as at least four times as dense as the other day.
You said there was just a single tree in the center of the crater? That feels... odd. Wasn't this place meant to be a grove at one point?
Years ago, yes. Until this place was turned into a logging camp and cleared out. Never really had any issues until...
When we get out, we'll make a plan on what to do about this place. For now, are you ready head back?
I'll use my other arm this time.

The two of you cut through the thicket back the way you came, and found less resistance exiting than entering. You make your way to Azamire, and started to form a plan while recharging in Lira's tavern. You set yourselves on sealing the grove, keeping whatever may be inside the crater locked away, and hopefully preventing the spread of the outer thicket as well.

As you start to wonder who might be helpful, in slaying corrupted beasts and dealing with wild plants before finally sealing the grove, Lira-who has clearly been listening in-swings by and recommends Gol and Petal for the first steps, and Morlin for the last. Without a word from either of you, she sends a couple of her patrons to fetch them. Sure enough, the two of them are more than up for the challenge, and recommend dealing with the beasts first, then tending to the thicket before sealing it. This works out well, as Magnavous sends a message back on Morlin's behalf, saying that he'll come as soon as he's able to return his sense of gravity-whatever that means.
This bait positively reeks, but that's kind of the point.
Let's see if we can find ourself some monsters. [Bait]

Excited by the prospect of a new challenge, Gol grips the Dawnsteel javelins tightly, sets off into the outer thicket, and is seemingly swallowed by the vegetation, quickly dipping out of sight. Petal quickly pulls out her poisons while Jass prepares to cut her way through the vines until you hear Gol... laughing?

Much less concerned for his safety, the three of you eventually make it to a clearing where the plants seem to be retreating from him. Gol lays atop the corpse of a beast several orders of magnitude larger than the mountain of a man, making it even larger than the three of you.
Gol quite enjoyed that little bout!
It's a shame about the wee beastie, though.
What, were you hoping for more of a fight?
Gol respects his opponent greatly, it did the best it could.
The thicket impeded it as much as it does the rest of us. Nature is very much not in harmony here.
The creature was in pain, Gol did his best to free it.
That's... very noble of you. It's clear that something is off here, but... I figured it was kind of the opposite.
I haven't seen much yet, but it'd make sense that this is more of a matter of corruption than nature running wild.
We'd best seal this as fast as we can. It will only get worse.
There's no way of driving the corruption out?
I'd need to be five times the herbalist I am, and that's just if it's a poison or plant-based corruption.
It could be magic, which I can't do much of anything about.
You're doing plenty, and we're lucky to have you here. Sealing the grove will be more than enough for now.
As long as we're able to halt its growth, having a single crater in the middle of the woods locked away should be fine, until we figure out how to fix it.
Gol recommends putting up some better signs though.
See? Gol and I are on the same page, Jass.
Though, on second thought I'm not sure if that's a good thing.
So, we can't just throw Gol into the forest and hope that he's able to get every single one of the corrupted beasts.
No, but it was good to come. We let Petal get her potions and herbs ready. She mentioned needing a fair bit of time to prepare to tame the outer thicket.
That's right. I'm making a special brew for this... My hope is that I can stunt the plants' growth, not just poison the land into inhabitability. Not to mention it'd take a lot more poison for that.
While you work on that, Gol and I can bait the creatures back into the crater. That way when we seal it, they'll be locked inside.
Sounds sensible. We'll let you know if Morlin manages to find us as well.
The corpse that Gol left behind was staggeringly large, so anything less than bait that is equally large won't do. I'll see what I can come up with, then come back to camp.
Rosemary is normally pretty pleasant. Will it really repel monsters with Petal's solution?
I'll let her know I'm about done. [Talk]

Giant Fish Bait packed in your spare bag sounded fine and dandy, until you realized that you'd have to walk along the edge of the rampant forest. Gol, by some miracle or stroke of luck, just so happened to be nearby when one of the same beasts as before just about grabbed you in its massive jaws. It let out a terrifying howl, and followed after the two of you. Worried about your pace, eventually Gol decided to throw you over his shoulder and run towards the edge of the crater as the vegetation pulls out of Gol's path, which would have felt a lot more disheartening if it weren't for the scores of eyes following after you. 

As the two of you crash through the treeline, you toss the bait-filled bag and send it careening into the crater. Gol dashes to the side and doesn't stop running, even as the beasts go lurching over the edge towards the pack. He doesn't set you down until the forest stops moving, which you don't mind one bit. Eventually, you deem it safe to return to camp, and do so quickly.
Friend, Gol fears your bait was a bit more effective than intended!
But it worked! I hope. There shouldn't be more than a couple stragglers if anything.
Gol thinks you should work on your cardio before trying something like that again.
I only got to see a glimpse of it, but it was rather entertaining.
It's kinda cute how small you look cradled in Gol's arms.
I wasn't cradled, I was heroically and tactically placed on his shoulder.
If anything, the elevated position was probably even better for making sure the corrupted wildlife smelled the bait.
It was a smart plan, Gol just wishes you communicated it ahead of time.
Sorry Gol, it was a kind of... improvised plan.
Well, one way or another, I think we're about ready for the next step. Petal?
[i]{0}[/i], you're rather handy on the farm, no? I remember you helping me with my garden.
Clove still loves the sunflowers, by the way.

I believe that if you plant rosemary along the rim of the crater, with a bit of a boost from one of my infusions, it should be more than enough to keep most of the critters at bay while Morlin seals the grove.
Seems like a good plan to me. But... has Morlin gotten here yet?
The man with the bushy beard floated into the sky!
He said he would be, still just dealing with some issues from his spell, apparently.

You look to Petal and Gol, who shrug-seemingly not too concerned with the flyaway wizard. You make your way back through the growth once again, the hacking motion and dodging of vines becoming quite routine at this point.
The runes the old man is asking for... This barrier seems like some nasty work.
I think we're finally ready to put up the barrier. [Complete Quest Button]

As you finish planting the last bit of rosemary into the ground, Petal comes by and dashes it with her solution, making the seed instantly spring up and twist into a much larger bright blue version of itself. Being next to it starts to make your eyes water, and as you turn your head and cough, you notice Jass and Gol hacking their way through the thicket, clutching vials of Petal's mix that should halt the growth of the plants.

Just then, a scream comes from the sky, and hurtles towards Gol. Morlin the Mage seems to-just barely-slow himself as he reaches Gol, and quickly settles into his arms as the large man catches him.
I was wondering when you might turn up. We just finished up with our part, you were just about late.
A Morlin is never late, nor is he early. He arrives precisely when his anti-gravity spell decides to send him hurtling towards the ground and straight into this strong man's arms.
Also, I must say, this is exquisitely comfortable. You all really should try this.
Then good, shall we get this all wrapped up then? What do you need of this masterful mage?
Can you call yourself a master if you can't control your spell?
Considering I haven't seen anyone so much as levitate more than a couple feet off the ground, I'd have to say yes.
I think we're about ready to seal the grove. Petal?
We have a bit more of the solution to halt the thicket's growth outside of the crater, but just about. Did either of you see any more beasts?
Not one! [i]{0}[/i]'s bait did its job well.
Ah, well, good, because I seem to have misplaced... all of my runes.
How do you think you would keep hold of your worldly possessions while flying towards the ground, hm?
Gol can send the old man back into the sky if you'd like, friend! Gol does not need a spell for this.
No! No no no. Please, could you fetch me some runes? I need a bit of time to reacclimate to the ground...

You glare at the old wizard before finally letting out a sigh and asking for a list of runes he needs for the spell. He goes to produce a page from his bag, but realizes that it is also missing, so he opts to just list them aloud instead, with little fanfare.

On your way back through the thicket-hopefully for the final time-you notice that Petal's solution must be working. The blue vines from before seem... placated, and barely twitch as you walk by, taking care not to step on them. You make it past the worst of the vegetation with little issue, and find yourself back on the rim of the crater. 

You find Morlin tied to a tree, the rope seeming to be the only thing stopping him from drifting back skyward. He happily takes the runes from you and gets to work while the rest of the crew finishes applying the last of Petal's solution to the most agitated bits of the forest. With a shout, Morlin claps his hands and a dome begins to materialize over the lip of the crater. Jass starts putting up new signs, taking advice from Gol all the while. Soon enough, warnings of a deadly barrier, evil beasts, and a corrupted array of flora lay below, along with certain death.

As you peer through the translucent barrier, you see that the jungle below looks wild and untamed, just as before. You hope that one day, you'll be able to return to discover what made it grow so rampant in the first place, and maybe even fix it, if you're lucky.

A concerned citizen wants to scrape together some semblance of a fighting force for Azamire's defense against any would-be bandits or those black-robed figures looking to finish the job, but she's barely in fighting shape herself.
Just putting some pointy rocks on some wood, nothing too tough.
I think they've gotten the idea.

The cinders from the assault on Azamire have only just fizzled out, much like many of the survivors' will to go on. Everyone that remained had lost something. Their homes. Family members. Friends. You and [Companion Name] sit on the soot covered cobbles that once made up the town's main thoroughfare, watching another family carry what little they have left and shuffle out of town, hoping that some nearby village may have been spared. Neither of you blame them.

A woman with a bloodied stump where her hand should have been approaches the two of you and falls to the ground beside you with a sigh.
Well. You two headed out as well?
I can't turn my back on Azamire. Too many folks have done too much for me, growing up.
I take it you're leaving, then? Can't blame you, but this is home for the both of us. Even if... Home's looking a little worse for wear.
Gods no! No shame to those who are, but those rotters took more than just my hand. Teri... didn't make it.
Fool of a man got between me and one of those wretches' beasts. Seemed like he was going to pull through... but then he didn't.
...We'll make them pay, Jass. [Companion Name] and I won't let this go unanswered.
You're not alone in your sentiment. I came by to see if you two might be interested in a little project.
A couple of people who aren't running for the hills want to fight back. But they're farmers. Builders.
I used to be pretty good with a bow, but it'd be a bit tough with this hand... or lack thereof.
Want us to show them the ropes? Been a little while since I shot a bow, but I can show a couple of farmers where to point it and how not to shoot their friends.
...Are you forgetting what happened a couple of years ago? I still feel the need to duck every time you-
Okay, fine, [Player Name] can do the teaching, maybe I'll learn something too. Is there anything else that I could help with?

Actually, yes. Like I said, most of these folks hardly know anything outside of their trade. Showing them how to put together a couple of arrows could go a long way towards making them self-sufficient.

The three of you chat back and forth for a while, putting together the idea of a lesson plan, putting up some ramshackle targets meant to resemble a humanoid figure, and some scavenged gear. Jass brings back a dozen or so dusty villagers from town who seem to carry a wide range of emotions. Some, determined to fight back against the cloaked figures who destroyed the town, some who looked lost and aimless, and some somewhere in between.

[Companion Name] takes half of them and gets to work showing them how to make bows, something they were always better at than actually firing them, while you take the other half and get to work showing them how to make arrows.
If I didn't know better, I'd say they were aiming at me.
I knew they'd be bad, but wow.

Many of the folks picked up your teaching pretty quickly. Even Jass, just managing with a single hand, did a fine job putting together some flight-worthy arrows. [Companion Name]'s lesson seemed to go about as smoothly, and they produced a few bows to share amongst themselves for the next bout of training. The villagers quietly, but excitedly, show off what they managed to make, or laugh about how poorly their creations turned out, depending on their results.
Thank you two for all of this, by the way.
Of course. It'll be important for us to not get caught out like this again.
This group has a long way to go, still. We had guards, but they lasted all of a few minutes before those things started cutting through the town.
It's a start, though. And besides, keeping these people busy is just as important as making sure they're trained.
Dwelling on everything that happened... Well, that's no good for anyone.
Anyway. Shall we get to shooting?
As long as [Companion Name] doesn't stick me with an arrow, sure.

[Companion Name] glares at you, but you've known them long enough to know there's no real anger there, just like they know you have no malice in your light banter.

Though, you start to think otherwise when the villagers pick up their bows and start trying to hit the targets. You feel as though their arrows pass by you more often than the targets. You get to work quickly, trying to show them how to draw, aim, and fire, before they really hurt someone.

You certainly lost a bit of skin from arrows that passed by a bit too close for comfort, but after a while, the villagers' shots start to resemble straight flight paths. A couple folks pick it up faster than the others, among them, [Companion Name], though you still could hardly say you felt safe just yet.

Initially, Jass seemed to be a bit frustrated at not being able to join in the demonstration, but fell into her own role guiding people and repeating your instructions to those that seemed to struggle the first few times around, or giving pointers that even you started to incorporate into your own shots.

By the end of the day, the villagers didn't seem to actively be putting one another in danger, and looked far more determined than they did at the start of the drill, and you entrust them into Jass's tutelage, for better or worse.
While out on a fishing trip, a little girl has gone missing with only her fishing pole and a single tooth left behind. Not much to go on, except one small detail. It isn't a human tooth.
Swords are plenty sharp, that'll do.
Let's hope they can figure out how to swing 'em.

You just start to drift off to sleep before a frantic pounding at your door makes you jump up and start grabbing for something nearby to protect yourself. Your door opens a bit more gently than you'd expect considering the knocking, and you find [Companion Name] looking worried with a young woman behind her. She holds up something about as thick as your finger with a sickly pale yellow hue.
Her daughter was out fishing near the river and didn't come home for dinner. Sorry to interrupt your sleep, but I figured you'd want to help.
You're not wrong. And the thing you're holding?
Golbin tooth. The only... blood, that was there was blue, so...
The girl is okay, at least for now, I'd imagine.
Good, good. Then, just the two of us are headed out?
Thankfully, no. Jass has been making a bit of progress with her 'militia' and they want to join us.
It's anyone's guess how many Golbins there will be. It'd be smart to let them come to us.
What if we set the same scene as... the incident, have Jass's people waiting for them?
Just please... hurry. I'm hopeful my little Ana is safe, but... it's not like they took her for a fun little stroll around the woods. I know she must be so frightened...
Don't worry, we'll do everything that we can.

You gather your things and leave your bed behind, meeting up with Jass and a couple of folks just outside. Some of them hold the bows [Companion Name] helped them make, some holding new ones they must have created themselves. However, any decent force has variety - archers wouldn't fare well if the Golbins got in their ranks - and their inventiveness hasn't improved in the short time since you helped them last. Jass asks for a couple of new toys for the folks that haven't taken well to the bow.
Just catch some fish and don't look suspicious. Easy.

The folks take up their new weapons eagerly. Though it has only been a short time since Jass gathered them, the combined militia now totaled a couple dozen. You notice as you hand out swords, though most don't have any conventional fighting experience, these people tend to lean capable. Lumber Workers and farmers who've built functional bodies through years of hard labour. Against a trained fighting force, sure, they'd hardly stand a chance. But against a group of ragtag Golbins? You like their odds.

They might not have much experience, but the folks that couldn't hit the broad side of a barn - or just otherwise hated trying to use the bows - I've had running drills with sticks and leftover tools.
They got a long way to go, but they know enough to hold their own. I'm not sending them in to die, don't worry.
Good, good. Azamire can't get much smaller if we want to keep calling ourselves a town.
If this ambush goes well, they won't need to fight much. Just need to look scary and grab one or two of the Golbins to tell us where they brought the girl.
If everyone's ready, let's head out to the river, then?

[Companion Name] leads you to the river where the girl went missing. You fondly recall learning to swim with [Companion Name] here, years ago, and wish you were here under less dire circumstances. The militia disperses through the surrounding forest, headed by Jass who quietly gives orders, trying to get people hidden as best she can.

You and [Companion Name] settle in by the riverbank, and pull out your rods, hoping to catch a bit more than just a few fish. You're a bit too nervous for idle conversation, so you both quietly fall into a rhythm, just trying to look like two innocuous people fishing late into the night.
I'm not going to let [Companion Name] beat me!
That should be about all of them.

You worry for a moment that one of the militia members is being too loud before you see it. A group of Golbins, sauntering up with hardly a care in the world, barking orders at one another, trying to surround you and [Companion Name]. It's... more than you expected, and as you start to get up to defend yourself, an arrow sinks right between the leading Golbin's shoulder blades.
Make sure to leave a couple breathing!
Bet you I'll kill more than you. Try not to die.

[Companion Name]'s look of anxiety hidden under bravado is quickly replaced with confidence as the woods explode with movement. The militia lets loose a volley of arrows that pepper the unprepared Golbins, scattering them and sending a few more to the ground. What's left of them gather themselves and charge towards you and your friend, or the quickly approaching villagers armed with swords.

You look around as the movement begins to settle. The Golbin force was larger than you had anticipated, but your efforts went as well as could be expected. Among the bodies littering the forest floor, from what you could see, only a couple were human, which was better than expected considering their experience.

You rush over as you hear a shout from Jass, who managed to pin a dark green Golbin to ground. The beast would have hardly came up to your hip had it been on its feet, and you could hear it whimpering and begging not to be hurt. It quickly rattles off fragments of information that it thinks could be useful, detailing how its clan was taken over by a rival group led by someone it called the 'Ringleader', its own name - Gloob - and how it really really wants to live. Jass slaps her hand over its mouth and asks it where the girl they kidnapped was, and why they took her. Gloob goes one step further, and says that it'll lead you all there to its nearby camp, and that they were going to try and paint him and sell him off too, whatever that may mean.

You discuss it briefly together, and decide to 'trust' it to do as it says. Surely enough, the camp is close, and the leftover defenders quickly scatter as they see they're vastly outnumbered, leaving their camp behind. You and [Companion Name] quickly find Ana in one of their tents and take her home, while Jass and the militia handle a dozen or so other folks who had been captured from elsewhere throughout the countryside. Ana's mother meets you just outside of Azamire with tears in her eyes, thanking you over and over again for saving her daughter.

Azamire has slowly but surely begun to get back onto its feet, and that's cause for celebration. The town's impromptu mayor, Hapren, has thought of just the thing to get folks together, a bit of warmth and food in the center of town.
A little cleanup could go a long way to making things feel a bit more put together.

A handful of people you haven't seen before walk past, likely another group of refugees from one of the nearby villages that fared even worse than Azamire, attacked around the same time. The town's new mayor - the son of the previous mayor that was lost in the attack - welcomes them and directs them towards one of the newly repaired buildings that they were using to shelter people before more buildings could be made to house them. Once he wraps up, he sets his eyes on you and [Companion Name].
Hey there, you two. I hope that things have been as good as they can be, considering...
Exactly... There's no easy way to put such a tragedy, huh?
There really isn't. You inherited quite the mess, didn't you?
Don't suppose either of you would be willing to take over, would you?
Afraid not. Never had the decorum to fit into a role like that.
Didn't figure. Well, would you two mind helping me out with a little project, then?
What do you have in mind, exactly?

Hapren brings the two of you over to the center of town, which has been piled with debris from Azamire's cleanup efforts. He talks about how he'd love to throw a little gathering for the town, just so folks can get to know one another and feel a bit of normalcy despite how hard the last while has been. A few people try their best to break down the rubble into movable chunks, but progress is slow, and Hapren asks for help before starting to work on the pile himself.
Nothing too flashy, just gotta pull up enough fish to show them how it's done.
Huh, there really is a lot of junk in the water. Wonder where it's coming from?

With you and [Companion Name]'s help, you manage to break up the debris in short order, and Hapren directs much of the salvageable materials to be stored for reconstruction efforts, and the wood that is too mangled to be used to be left in the square to be used for the bonfire.

Just as you set your tools down, a few tired looking folks make their way into the center of town, fishing gear in hand.
If I couldn't see them swimming around, I'd swear the stock of fish had run dry.
Feels like we're pullin' more junk out of the water than fish.
You could say that. I see that the town square is just about ready, but I'm sorry... It'll take us a week to have enough fish at this rate.
Wait, you're using Mackerel Bait, right? Only way I've managed to pull anything out of there.
...No. Honestly, don't think I've ever used much more than a worm, really.
Well, you don't need it, but it sure doesn't hurt.
Since we're just about done here... While we get things set up, would you mind lending them a hand?

[Companion Name] looks to you and searches your face, trying to gauge your reaction. You shrug, and then offer to help. Getting together a bit of bait to help the fishers out, then showing them how to work with the river shouldn't take too long, and it'd be nice for the town to be able to keep itself fed.
Maybe Hapren would appreciate the meat?

You all spend awhile on the pebble bank, sitting and waiting for a fish to bite, as one typically does while fishing. You and [Companion Name] talk to the fishermen for a while and learn that they used to be able to pull out enough fish to feed half the town, even without the bait. When you dump bait in the water, and start using some on your hooks, things pick up, but it's still rather slow. You watch even more junk float by. Bits of tree branches, huge clumps of soil, and then, a dead Golbin. The fishers point out that it's been like this for a few days, minus the Golbins at least.
Something must be going on up river, this is just odd.
You all can keep fishing. Try not to reel in... anything green.
You're going to go check it out, aren't you?
Of course we are. You're coming too, obviously. Unless you want to see me floating by, next?
I haven't shown them how I usually tie my hooks yet, I really-

They stop their protesting as you grab their shoulder and pull them behind you. You know from all your time together they'd never really let you go by yourself, but as they grumble behind you, it's clear they're not pleased about running off to find... whatever is, up river.

After a few minute jaunt upstream, you see it. A massive boar standing over a group of dead Golbins. It pulls against ropes that had been tied to trees along the river, and then thrown over the top of the beast. As you approach it catches sight of you both, assumes and breaks the last of its restrains as it charges towards you!

With the help of some villagers and their carts, you manage to bring back the Golbin's pet taming project. Hapren is shocked, then pleased, as he realizes that this is a far better catch than a few fish from the river.

As the sun sets, the wooden debris from the square is burnt and thick slabs of boar are grilled and given out to everyone in attendance. More and more curious folks poke their heads into the square and are met with warmth and light conversation.  A few folks even start up with light songs as the night progresses and Azamire's paltry stores of booze are enjoyed by those who indulge.

Azamire's attack is far from forgotten, but this quiet moment amongst the survivors does well to begin healing the towns aching wounds.
Gloob and Jass have been 'working' together for a while, and now need your help to launch a daring mission... or stupidly walk into a Golbin's trap.
I should be able to follow Gloob's schematics easy enough.

As you walk back into Azamire, you feel a swell of pride at the number of newly constructed buildings. They're small, and it hardly takes you long to count them on two hands, but still, Azamire is rebuilding, bit by bit.

Your delight is interrupted by a shriek as you hear a... Golbin run by, chased by the newly appointed Militia Captain - Jass. The chase doesn't last long, and Gloob is held down while Jass berates it, talking about how she's no fool and knows a trap when she sees one.
I see that things are going well.
SHE'S GOING TO EAT ME, PLEASE HELP!
We're keeping you here because you were meant to help us, beast!
What I said was true! You should be able to sneak into the Ringleader's fortress at night, it'd be fine!
The guards have wood for brains! You'll see what I mean!
We'll do no such thing! We ought to string you up for what your little pack did to Ana!
This beast, is trying to get us to sneak into its boss's hideout tonight. Says all the Golbins will be out escorting a shipment.
...humans. That's what the Ringleader wants from all of the Golbin tribes he subjugates!
I told you that when you saved me from that group days ago!
What do you mean, saved you?
I'm... little. Never been useful for much, the other Golbins said. Too 'so-fist-uh-cated', they'd say.
They were going to tie me up and try to put me in one of the shipments, too, since I wanted to 'act like a human'.
And why the blazes would they do that?
Because if a tribe doesn't pay up with enough people, the Ringleader takes his tithe in other ways. Turns us into ents.
Something about needing a creature's lifeforce. But I wasn't even ever part of that tribe, I got outcast from my own years ago.
And then they captured you again sometime after the Ringleader took over?
Why were you in the group that attacked us, then?
One of the Golbin's fancied himself a knight and wanted to use me as a squire. Carry his weapons n' stuff.
We don't even have knights. But everyone thought it was funny, so they let him until it was going to be time to lump me in with a shipment.
So... You've never even hurt a person?
No! I even traded with some of your people up north. I would make stuff, then sell it for books. I learned lots.
You believe this little green booger, don't you?

You manage to pull Jass aside long enough to get her to calm down. She apologies, first to you, then even to Gloob, and says that when she learned that they were capturing people to 'send them somewhere' it sent her over the edge. She asks Gloob to fill you in on what he told her. Every full moon, a bunch of robed figures end up coming to the Ringleader's fortress within the Elder Grove. They come with large, wooden wagons, and leave with people that the surrounding Golbin tribes have captured.

He goes on to say that the Golbins at the fortress leave with the robed figures, escorting them... wherever they go, he doesn't know. With the nearing full-moon, it'd be a great chance to get a peek into the fortress, and that he'd even go, but that he'd need some climbing gear and hooks to scale the fort's outer wall. Either hopefully or foolishly, you decide to trust him, and he details how he'd go about making the equipment. You and Jass decide it'd be good to bring [Companion Name] along as well, and that they'd go over Gloob's memory of the fort to plan the scouting mission while you make the gear.

You, Gloob, and [Companion Name] set off into the Misty Thicket on the night of the full moon. Gloob brings you through the woods quickly, and it's tough to keep up with his speed. You and [Companion Name] find yourselves huffing and puffing just outside of the Ringleader's Fortress. In the moonlight, you all see a train of wagons and hobgolbins heading to the north along an old dirt road, but quickly lose track of it as they slip into the dense thicket.

With them gone, the three of you use the gear you prepared and scale the walls, landing quietly on the other side. Gloob brings you to several spots throughout the relatively open grounds. A small, ramshackle prison, with several ents patrolling just outside. You pass by a handful of sleeping areas for the fort's living guards, until you reach a large wooden hut Gloob says is the Ringleader's home. Finally, he leads you to a stockpile of various bits that a Golbin would find valuable, taken as tribute or looted from nearby towns. Hides, half-rotten food, weapons and armor, gold, and most notably, dozens upon dozens of caskets of flammable oil and booze.

You and [Companion Name] wait for Gloob to lead you into an ambush, but the trap never comes. True to his word, once he finishes with the important parts of the fortress, the three of you scale back over the wall and head back to Azamire. When you return, you immediately begin talks with Jass about launching an assault on the fortress with what you've learned, and set plans into motion to get the town ready. Clearing a path to bring wagons to the fort, and securing an exit route for prisoners will be essential before launching an attack. Plus, it gives Jass more time to get her people ready, too.
The old Northern Road will take Azamire's wagons close to the Ringleader's Fortress, but due to a rockslide, it's unusable. With a bit of effort, it should be usable once again!
Chisel first, then make them into volatile bombs. Easy.
Don't drop them don't drop them don't drop them.

Gloob - who is now allowed to freely roam the town after your scouting mission proved his loyalty - fetches you and brings you to Jass's newly constructed 'barracks'. In reality, it was just an enclosed room with some storage for gear and a few targets set up, but it was coming along nicely. Within her office, a map of the surrounding lands was laid out, recently purchased from one of the infrequent caravans that just started to come by once again.
Ah, [Player Name], you're here. We're planning our path to the fortress, but our scouts ran into a bit of a snag.
No one is hurt. But a bit of the Old Northern Road that passes through the Foggy Canyon has been buried under a rock slide.
Then it seems we should just find another path, no?
That'd be great, but this is the only feasible way to bring wagons up to the fortress. We'll need them to carry gear, and... wounded, after the battle.
Don't fret though! I know how to clear it! I just need a bit of help from you.
Just... you and me, clearing a rockslide? How well can you swing a pick?
No no, I have something far better.

Gloob gives you the rundown on an idea he's tried before. With a bit of effort, careful chiselling, and sulfur, fire runes could be made into shaped bombs could carefully carve a path through the rockslide. Not only that, he's actually already prepped some runes they traded for, but needs help with the chiselling and then... putting a bit more volatile fire energy into them.
I don't suppose they're interested in talking this one out.
That seems like all of them, for now.

You carefully bring the volatile runes down to the Foggy Canyon along with Gloob and set to work tucking them into the rock. Gloob lights them as you move away, and sure enough, they work exceedingly well. Gloob stands triumphantly as bits of rock pelt the two of you after the series of explosions.
And that is why reading is cool!
Wait, what does this have to do with reading?
I got the idea for these bombs after reading about a wizard that was banished from her family for blowing up half her estate. Tough luck, right?
Wow, do you think it was on purpose?
No clue! But it got me thinking about what happens when magic goes wrong, you know?
I should... be a little more careful with fire spells in the future.
It's always good to practice caution! Shall we get back to bombing the crap out of this canyon now?
Of course! It actually seems that some of the rocks are already moving out of the way in fear, should be a bit less to handle.

As the question leaves your lips, several golems rise from the piles of rock, doubtlessly less than pleased with your explosive intrusion on their turf. They seem quite keen on smashing you into the ground so they can return to their nap.
Maybe I should ask someone in the mines..? Nah, what's the worst that could happen?

The golems now lay crushed at your feet. Gloob held his own well, using his speed to distract them and a few carefully placed bombs to take out a few of his own. As the two of you catch your breath, one of the walls of the canyon cracks and Gloob jumps back and wraps himself around your leg in fear. A massive sheet of stone falls to the ground in front of you. After the dust settles, Gloob removes himself from your leg and clears his throat while dusting himself off.
Well, uh... That's certainly not great.
Shouldn't be hard to break up and move, but if the canyon walls keep collapsing, we'll hardly have a road left here at all.
Or... Even worse, it could come down while people are travelling through.
Then we've got to support the walls, yeah? I... haven't read much on building stuff like that, yet.
[Companion Name] and I have actually helped out in Azamire's mines a few times through the years.
We'll need some rock bolts, which we can make out of steel, then we drive them into the walls.

You walk Gloob through finding good spots for the bolts, and leave him to mark spots in the canyon that'll work well. Then you start to work out how to create strong enough rock bolts to keep the canyon walls from collapsing in on themselves.

The sides of the Foggy Canyon hold once you and Gloob finish up hammering the bolts into its walls. Even as you finish up blowing up the last of the rock that remains along the old Northern Road, your handiwork holds, and after you've finished your work, you no longer fear having a sheet of stone land on your head. You look down to the little Golbin by your hand who beams with pride at a job well done, ecstatic to have been able to put his mind to something and see something tangible come out. The two of you head back to Azamire to report a job well done, and that the Northern Road is clear to use once again.

A path must be cleared for the prisoners to get out of the Misty Thicket fortress when you launch the attack against the Ringleader, lest they get caught in the crossfire between you and the fortresses' guard.
Gold coins aren't good enough, eh?

The moon was completely hidden by clouds on the night you found yourself outside of the Ringleader's fortress, yet again. The scouting trips had gotten more frequent, though you only had time to go on a few of them lately. But Jass hadn't brought you out for a scouting mission, this time. The two of you wait for a patrol to pass and she brings you to the covered end of a tunnel. You two climb in and follow it for a while, until hitting what must be the wooden wall of the fortress. Gloob is crouched down here, inspecting the wall, not needing any light to see it clearly.
Not sure how far down the wall goes, but we can't just dig down further.
If it goes all the way down to stone, I wouldn't even know how start trying to get through the stone. I'm no rockhound.
And forget about keeping it quiet. I know your people have been at this for a while, right? I'm sure moving all this soil is tough.
You'd bet. We've got to carry it all out and then sprinkle it through the woods. If a patrol came across a random pile of dirt, that'd be... suspicious.
Makes sense. So, you need to get through this wall. Any ideas?
Well, Gloob says he can get a tool to get through it... Right Gloob?
Yeah, I'm... know to locate some stuff, from time to time.
I made a lot of contacts when I was traveling about. We'd have to trade for it.
Well, they typically deal in silver bars. I think it'd usually be about seven or eight bars, but this tool is special item.

You ask what the tool even is, and Gloob starts to describe a magical length of metal fashioned after a knife that, when activated, starts to vibrate rapidly. It should be enough to quietly carve away at the wall, albeit slowly. You leave Gloob to his inspection of the wall, and head off to get some silver.
Just press it into the wall and cut, no problem.
I don't think anyone heard me.
You hand off the bars to Gloob back in Azamire, and not long after, he shows up on your doorstep, carrying a sheet wrapped around the vibrating knife he described. He happily hands it over.
Thankfully, it shouldn't take you too long to get through with this.
Just kinda... press it into the wood and it'll activate. I've marked the hole you need to cut in red paint, okay?
Thank you, Gloob. This is really helpful. I know it might feel a bit odd helping us humans out, but I just wanted to let you know that we appreciate your help.
I hope that folks aren't giving you too much trouble around town, are they?
Not at all, actually. Maybe a couple weird looks here and there, sure, but they've been more than welcoming.
Even your mayor! Sounds like he's going to try and get me set up with a workshop of sorts!
Oh and I'm really starting to grow on Jass, and [Companion Name] is having me do a few things around, and also...

Gloob starts to run through... more of his social life than you bargained for, and around the twenty minute mark you cough and mention that you really ought to get going to the fortress. Completely oblivious, he wishes you luck, and you set off. Back down at the end of the tunnel, sure enough, Gloob has marked a large cutout for you to follow.

You're able to cut through the wall after a fair bit of effort, and finally, the chunk of wood settles. You set the tool down beside you and decide to leave it there, in case anyone needs to improve upon your work. Once you're done, you carefully leave the tunnel and cover the entrance once again, before reporting back to Jass. She sends for a few people to go continue with the rest of the tunnel and assures you that it'll be ready for when you need to get the prisoners out.
[Companion Name] has been strangely absent lately, and on the rare chance you do see them, they usually quickly excuse themselves. What's going on?
Good food always makes you feel better.
Maybe I should have gone for something more nutritious...

Late in the evening, you head to the recently built home for [Companion Name]. It's nothing fancy - like most of the new constructions in Azamire - but all of the folks who've been contributing the most were given priority in separate lodgings, and they've done wonders for bringing back a bit of normalcy.

What hasn't been normal is how little you've seen [Companion Name] lately. You've had plenty of times where you weren't attached at the hip over the years you've known one another, but you know they've been around. It almost feels as if they've been avoiding you.

You knock several times to no avail. Just as you turn to go, you see a limping figure approach, notice you, and then turn away.
Ohhhh..! Hello there, ol' buddy ol' pal. I'm just... gonna, go... this way...
Forgot that I needed to chat with... Hapren! That's right, needed to chat with Hapren.
[Companion Name], I'm not really sure what's going on, but if I did something, please... Let me know, okay?
I didn't forget your birthday or anything, did I? I'm sorry, okay..?

[Companion Name] turns towards you and wobbles on their feet. Even in the low light, you notice the dark red patch blood on the front of their cloak, and trailing down their arms. You rush towards them and manage to catch your best friend before they hit the ground. You quickly run through a list of places you could bring them before settling on their own place. You quickly fish their key out of their pocket and carry them inside. You'd complain about them being heavy if it weren't for the fact your heart was beating out of your chest, knowing how hurt they are and having no idea on why or how.

Digging through both their supplies and yours, you find enough to get them patched up. Across their chest is a large gash with bits of... wood, sticking out of it? You extract it all, bit by bit, in the lantern light, and stitch them back up before wrapping them in gauze. The rest of their wounds are comparatively minor, and take much less time to deal with, but they are numerous, and in various states of healing, some old, some fresh.

Once you're done, [Companion Name] looks more mummy than person, but they'll live. You cover them up to let them rest, and decide to help along their recovery with their favorite food.
Time for a little bit of payback.

[Companion Name] manages to quietly eat the cake you give them, and you decide to wait a while before beginning your round of questioning. Once they finish the first half, your questioning begins, and they fake passing out. You roll your eyes, and threaten to take the rest of the cake away and they spring back up, but quickly nurse their wounds after the sudden movement. You ask what happened, how they feel, and what they why they've been avoiding you, but [Companion Name] remains silent for all of it. When you finally ask why they didn't bring you, tears well up in their eyes.
I... I couldn't put you in danger, [Player Name].
What do you mean, you couldn't put me in danger?
If you were doing something dangerous, then I especially should have been there!
That I didn't want to lose you too!
That I had to keep Azamire safe and if I brought you with me, you might not come back!
We've already lost twenty more people on the route to the Ringleader's fortress in the past couple weeks.
All but two of them were to a single weird ent. Way bigger than the rest, and covered in these weird... talismans.
That's what did this to you?
I didn't want to bring you in case... It had something we couldn't handle.
We lost so much in the attack, but at least... I still had you. I couldn't lose you, too.
So you tried to fight it on your own? [Companion Name] why-
I just wanted to see it! I've been practicing on the smaller ones all this time.
Tonight, I figured that I could get a look at the big one, learn what it could do, come back to town, and come up with a plan against it.

They detail the events of the night. How they came across the creature, and the talismans in its branches flashed with a bright blue light as they tried to run away. How they floated up into the air and were sucked towards the ent while they flailed about in the air, and then how the ent sent them flying after the talismans in its branches flashed bright blue. [Companion Name] was sure they were going to die, until they saw that the talismans in the ent's branches matched the similar charms forming a line in the nearby treeline. The giant ent shuffled back and forth at that line, but wouldn't cross it. Then, they limped all the way back to Azamire.

After a through amount of ridicule and chastisement, you hug them and tell them you're glad they're okay.

In the morning you detail everything that happened to Jass, who gathers up the archers of her militia and send them out with you and a wounded [Companion Name], who leads you to the grove with the giant ent. It seems that it has been joined by several of the smaller ones, but you aren't dissuaded.
Let's make them a bit smaller, turned into ash.

The ents are all down, and the archers do their best to shoot the talismans out of the trees incase they do... anything bad. [Companion Name] holds their bow at their side, pleased to have gotten a little payback, then kicks at an ent's branch that seems to be trying to crawl away.
Thank you... I'm sorry I tried to play the hero.
If you didn't... I probably would have. I don't want to lose you either.
Please, don't do something like that again, okay? I need you too.
Okay okay... You too, alright? Promise?
Seems the trees aren't quite 'dead' yet, huh?
Doubt they'll survive being turned into ash, don't you think?

Everyone gathers up the ent parts. They don't seem dangerous anymore, but you do notice that - slowly but surely - they're starting to gain new growth. If you waited long enough, they'd likely become a threat again. The archers help by snapping off new branches and tossing them back into the pile, and occasionally making sure that none have managed to crawl away.

The last bit of smoke goes out as the final pile of burning ent runs out of fuel. You were almost tempted to start trying to grill something, but the idea of the smoke being evil and getting into the food dissuaded any attempts. [Companion Name] leans against you, both for comfort, and because they are far from recovered from their wounds. You tease them lightly about getting smacked around by kindling, to which they reply by driving the butt of their bow into your foot. You tussel their hair and give them a hug, and tell them that you're glad they're safe.

Azamire is as ready as it ever will be to take down the Ringleader. The old Northern Road is clear, Jass's crew has finished the tunnel to the prison, and you have defeated the worst of the Misty Thicket's roaming guards. Now, all that's left to do is burn the fortress to the ground.
If I want any supplies, I should take them from the cart before the attack starts in earnest.

As you walk through Azamire, the town is abuzz with nervous energy. Several wagons are lined up and everyone who isn't fighting have come out to wish you well. Hapren approaches, and mentions that the town has gotten together and prepared some combat supplies into the back of one of the carts for you, and hopes that it helps.

You all set off, and as the sun begins to set, the cold mist of the thicket starts to seep into your clothes. The militia is tense, but ready. There are people to save, and taking out the Ringleader would go a long way towards making everyone safer.
Don't have any qualms with this, Gloob?
I might be green, but I'm no Golbin. Let's take him out.
Never better. Plan is the same, still?
That's right. The tunnel under the prison is ready to get the prisoners out, and we'll have people posted at the exit.
As soon as people start escaping down the tunnel, the guards will notice everyone's missing and sound the alarm.
Once that happens, archers will try to hit that stockpile you mentioned with flaming arrows.
Should deal with most of the ents inside, and make a ton of noise. You'll be providing the fire, of course, we need several braziers lit.
After that, we head to the gate and hack it down. The archers will keep us covered.
And then we're in. Try to avoid the fire, and head for the Ringleader?
Exactly. Can't miss 'em. Big blue fella, covered in every gaudy fabric he fancies.
Things are going to get really hectic once this starts.

As you finish your conversation, the fortress's outer wall comes into view. Gloob and small group of the militia break off and head for the tunnel while the rest of you set up on the hillside just outside. Several braziers are set up, and everyone starts to load them with wood while you and [Companion Name] get to work.
We have to get through this gate!

Alarms start to sound as the militia's arrows are lit. You clutch your weapon in anticipation, wishing you could to go check on the tunnel to see how Gloob's breakout went, but there's no time. The hillside is lit up with the fires you and [Companion Name] started, and hobgolbins on the wall begin to shoot towards you. But it's too late. Burning arrow after arrow soar up and over the wall, towards where you pointed out the stockpile. No one can see over the wall, so it's tough to tell if anyone is on target until a resounding BOOM make you cover your ears, even from this far away.

Many of the defenders are thrown from the wall entirely, and as you and the militia charge, the swordsmen dispatch the stunned hobgolbins that fell on the wrong side of the wall. Arrows start to fall again, as the fort's guards gather themselves, and they're met with your militia's own volleys.
Don't stop running until you hit the gate!
We can do this! Push on!

You and [Companion Name] reach the gate first and take out your axes, followed by a small group of other militia members who follow suit and get to work. Another group comes with large shields that they hold with both hands, more table than shield. But they work well as the shield group form a defensive shell around you and overhead, giving you room to work without worrying about an arrow finding its way in your unprotected back.
We will not fall. Not this time.

The occasional pained grunt, or worse, the painted gurgles of someone who was struck somewhere lethal, dampen your mood. You knew people would fall today. You can only imagine how the people on the hillside are faring. Just as your mind starts to lose focus, thinking about those you'd lose, you see a burning light at the end of your axe. As you pull it back, you realize you're through! You give a cheer that turns into a battlecry, and your group follows suit. A few more axe strikes and enough holes are opened to let Azamire's troops push through the gate.

The fort grounds are... hellish. Most of the ent guardians already crawl on the ground, crying out with groaning wails as they burn, with nearly every structure already completely engulfed in flames. You wonder for a moment if there's even a point of being inside until a massive blue Golbin covered in singed fabric cries out as he locks eyes with you. The rest of the fort's surviving defenders stand in the middle of the blazing stronghold with the Ringleader, smashing weapons against their shields, waiting for orders.
Humans want to be hand delivered to masters?
Ringleader need new stock, others just ran out.
Come to me. Time for you to die.
Keep the rest of them off [Player Name] and [Companion Name]!
Know that we fight not just for those back home, not just to save yourselves...
Together! Go! Now! Kill them all!
[Player Name], I'm with you. Trust me! I'll keep you safe!

Not a single person falters as they stream past you, charging with weapons and heads held high. You don't turn away as you see some being driven through as the Ringleader's forces crash into your own. Time slows as you push through, trusting your people to keep you safe. As you make it through the bodies, the Ringleader stands with a gnarled smirk, holding what must be half a burning tree as its weapon, seemingly unbothered by the flames that flicker up its arm.

You hear people roar in the battle behind you, some in victory, others... likely as their last act of defiance against the opposing force. You steel yourself and step forward, challenging the Ringleader.

Before you lies the broken body of the Ringleader, sickly purple blood spilling from his wounds. You finally spare a glance to those around you, and you realize... it's over. Less than half the attacking force remains, but Azamire's people still stand.  Gloob stands among the militia, deep green body covered in the blue blood of hobgolbins, and he lets out a cheer, one that the remaining militia proudly meet. Jass barks out orders, pointing out wounded with the stump of her arm, then starting to pull one of the wounded towards the gate with her other.

Half a dozen emotions cross [Companion Name]'s face the second you look at them, but most among them all, relief. They embrace you for naught but a moment before heading towards the Ringleader, who barely manages a ragged breath. As you approach, the beast lets out a throaty cackle before it devolves into a choking cough. You ask it two questions. Where did the shipments go, and who are the people it works for?

He just sits and smirks, the flames of his burning fortress dancing in his eyes.

"They'll come back soon."
After a short stay back in Amazire, you and [Companion Name] find it hard to rest. There's still so much to be done. The Ringleader was merely the first step.
They travelled a long, long way.

The day following your attack on the Ringleader's fort is met with a mixture of joy, relief, grief, and... uncertainty. 
While the assault was successful, casualties number in the range of a few dozen, a large blow to the already wavering population of your home.

However, with the number of refugees coming and going nowadays, ebbs and flows in the local populace are getting hard to keep track of. While callous, you are thankful that no one you knew well fell - through a few of the original militia recruits you and [Companion Name] were among the bodies you brought back on the wagons.

Yesterday's events weren't enough to keep you or [Companion Name] down for long, though. The two of you set off back to the fort at first light, searching for tracks of the caravan you saw leave the fort on your first scouting mission. The set of buildings behind their thick wall still smouldered from the night before, reminding you both of the battle.
Time to stomp around the forest a bit, eh?
Heading north... been a while since we've been this far from home.
You've always wanted to see the world.
Couldn't ask for better company, either. Though... wish the circumstances were a bit less...
We first scouted the fortress out... what, two weeks back?
Feels like it could have been yesterday, or half a year ago.
It's been a long two weeks.
Think we'll still be able to track them?
With several wagons and a pack of hobgolbins, I don't see them as being particularly sneaky.
And I doubt this stretch of woods sees much traffic, either. Let's see what we can find.

Sure enough, the prisoner caravan cut a long, winding trail that isn't too hard to follow. Torn up grass and foliage here, a few trees moved aside there. Concerningly, the path looks... well-travelled. You're glad Azamire was able to put a stop to the Ringleader's export of people from the area, but you can't help but wonder how many towns fared a similar fate to your own.

Following the caravan takes you ages. You travel north, out of the Elder Grove and just an hour's walk outside of the town of Hirane until the tracks stop. Several wagons were stopped here and burned, presumably by the hobgolbins bringing them. It seems that several captives were killed, though for what reason, you don't know. From what you're able to gather, the group split into well over thirty different parties, all heading off in different directions. Doubtlessly impossible to follow them all, even without the added difficulty of being much harder to track than the wagons.

You worry for a moment about Hirane's safety until you realize that the golbins would have to have a small army to raze a town of their size. Being situated on the Heartroad - one of the main throughputs to the capitol of Melvor - certainly had its advantages. Being able to trade for finely crafted arms and armor were chief among them, but the Golbin's presence still gave you pause.

You and [Companion Name] decide to head into town, and the general mood of the place is... tense. Folks who seem to be citizens quickly hurry past haggard, haunted-looking villagers. It's a sight you're well acquainted with, though you're surprised to see it here. You and [Companion Name] are quickly approached by a fussy-looking man with a immaculately cared for mustache and a permanent scowl etched on his face.
If you wish to seek refuge within the town's walls, you must go to the registrar's office and submit your documentation.
You can expect a wait time of-
And it's a pleasure to me you too. I am [Companion Name], this is [Player Name].
...That's usually how a conversation starts, at least.
I simply do not have the time for idle-chit chat. You two are just one group of many flowing into town.
I apologize if I come off as rude, I am simply trying to be as efficient as I can be in these trying times.
And what exactly ails your town so?
...The same as everywhere, this side of the sands.
Cloaked figures attacking with beasts never before seen or heard of.
They're razing farmland, attacking trade caravans, and burning hamlets to the ground.
You'd think we were at war, with how frequent and destructive the attacks are.
Anywhere outside of a walled-in town seems to be fair game to them. That... is, why you're here, no?
Well, yes, but not for refuge. We were tracking a convoy belonging to a group of them from the south, but they dispersed about an hour outside of town.
That'd be by... the Elder Grove, no? Nasty business with Golbins down there right now, I hear.

Unsurprisingly, Curo had no idea what [Companion Name] was talking about, until the two of you walk him through Azamire's attack on the fortress and the defeat of the Ringleader. While skeptical, he sends out a scouting party to confirm your claims. Through an only slightly more pleasant conversation with the man after a light change in disposition, you learn that people have begun flocking to Hirane out of fear, or lack of options.

They've done what they can, but are quickly being stretched short with many of the nearby villages being attacked, and much of the farmland nearby being abandoned out of fear. When you and [Companion Name] press him for more details, he's dismissive, and says he may be able to help, should you prove useful and your claims of razing the Ringleader's fort prove true.
Wow, they're well stocked. That's helpful, at least.
Seems like they've got it mostly handled, now.

You and [Companion Name] drop off another package of supplies, hopeful that what you've been able to provide lightens Hirane's burdens a bit. One of the women in charge of the relief tent cheerfully accepts, a bit surprised by the weight of your goods.

Just as you turn to go, Curo approaches you and [Companion Name] with an uncharacteristic smile, holding a leaflet of paper and being flanked by two people who seem to be scouts. He waves off a few people who vie for his attention.
I wasn't expecting the two of you to get to work so quickly.
Honestly, I only wanted to put you to work since I thought you were full of it, talking about rising up against that fortress.
Believe you? Based on the reports I've gotten, I feel like I best start commissioning portraits of you to hang in the mayor's home.
I don't know how a couple of villages out in the boonies managed to mount such a force, but I say, I'm impressed.
That fortress being taken care of makes all of us safer.
And I'd say... one good deed deserves another, hm?
That it does. I already have my people working on providing a report, worry not. They'll bring it to you in a few hours.
Make yourselves at home, I'll have the guards know not to give you any trouble. And uh...
Not used to doing this... I'm sorry for how we first met.

Curo purses his lips at that, seemingly a bit lost on what to say after that. He opts for a slight nod and then excuses himself, his caprones following quickly after.

The woman you dropped off your goods with politely, but shyly, asks if the two of you could lend just a bit more help since it sounds like you'll be stuck here anyway. You look to [Companion Name], who just shrugs. Might as well. She quickly leads you off to a nearby cooking tent, where a line of hungry refugees waits eagerly. It seems that the current staff are struggling to keep up.

You and [Companion Name] find yourselves breathless and exhausted after providing as many warm meals as you could. The crowd has been quelled substantially, with only a few stragglers coming up every half an hour or so. The head chef dismisses you, and thanks you dearly for your help, while making sure that you don't leave without a warm meal yourselves.

The two of you start to dig in, right as one of Curo's earlier companions wordlessly jogs up to you and holds out a sealed scroll. Once you take it from his hands, he gives a small salute and turns back the way he came.

You read over the scroll in the dim evening light to see a collection of detailed notes from months of observations. You read of the guard's clashes with armed groups, freed captives, and even a few raids on encampments of the unnamed group. Finally, you find what you're looking for.

You read an entry regarding a skirmish that took Hirane's scouts far to the east, to the edge of a town called Clearwater. The scouts continued to assail a caravan of these armed bandits until a massive sandstorm blew into the region and forced their retreat.

It wasn't much to go off of, but it's a start. The two of you finish your meals quickly and ready yourselves to head east.

After pouring over the reports from Hirane's scouts, you're sure of one thing. The hooded figures that attacked Azamire and seem to be kidnapping and transporting townsfolk have headed far to the east. To what end, you couldn't even begin to wager a guess.
With enough of these, we should be able to make it to Clearwater!

You exit Hirane's gate and find yourself deep within the countryside. You travel east along the Heartroad, knowing that if you go far enough, it should be next to impossible to miss Clearwater. From what you were able to gather from folks in Hirane, Clearwater acts as the major waystation between the east and west sides of the Desert Plains. You heard of many small resting points and hamlets between here and there, but few were notable enough to commit to memory.

The Heartroad is generally well constructed and maintained - even this far from the capitol - but as grass turned to arid soil, and then eventually sand, the Heartroad becomes harder to keep track of. Despite what the locals in Hirane said about there being places to rest between there and Clearwater, most of the buildings you pass are abandoned, swallowed by the sands.

The sun beats down on you overhead in a way you're unfamiliar with except for on Azamire's hottest summer days. There's no reprieve from the heat, just sand stretching out in what seems endless waves of gold.
This is... a little warmer than I expected.
Do we have any water left?
About one more flask between us. Want it now?
I didn't think so few of the waystations would be abandoned. We'd have had to carry more than both our weights in water to make it to Clearwater without stopping...
I'm not saying it's time to panic, but-
I refuse to lose to the sun, just days after we took down the Ringleader.
Got an oasis in your back pocket that I don't know about?

You grab [Companion Name] and pull her to the side, off the Heartroad and crest over one of the dunes. Your eyes don't deceive you - or your mind can't conjure up particularly appealing mirages - the small green crowns you saw from the road belong to large cacti. You stick one with your knife and a miserably thin trickle of slightly sappy water pours out. It isn't white, and after a small taste, it doesn't seem acidic or leave your tongue tingling. It doesn't seem poisonous, and that's good enough. Beats frying to death, anyway.
That hurt, but I guess it's fair.

You wipe the cactus water from your mouth. The two of you tapped into many of the ones nearby and start to stray from the original patch. You find yourselves giggling and swaying too and fro, despite definitely being more hydrated. You're worried that something may be wrong, but how could it be? You feel so good. [Companion Name] nearly collapses against you in a fit of giggles, the sand undulating in mesmerizing patterns underneath you.
You are the best, you know that, [Player Name]?
No, stop it, stop it. I mean it. I never would have been able to come out all this way if it weren't for you.
And nowwwww I feel so so so good.
Do you think *hic*, that maybe, the cactus water is...
Pffffft. Nooooo. This is how I NORMALLY am. Look at how normal I'm being right now.

The cacti that stand in front of you now seem... bigger. And they move. But everything is moving, so that's not particularly strange. What is strange is that one of the cacti swing one of it's spiny arms at your head when you try to cut into it with your axe. The needles in the side of your face snap you out of the cactus water's hallucinogenic effects.

Everything around you stops moving, except for the... angry cactus in front of you. And all of the ones behind it. They shift through the sands and reach out with their arms. They're real. You call out to [Companion Name] who seems to be having a similar revelation.
That was worth free passage for life? Huh.

The cacti's spines are rough to content with, and require a far more protective approach to fighting than you're used to employing, but all is well. The patch of cacti lays slain at your feet, and the... effects of the cactus water seem to have subsided.

You press on to Clearwater, only taking occasional, small sips of the cactus water you collected when you absolutely need to. You're definitely more giggly than usual and sway lightly on your feet, but the worst of the effects never take hold with your moderate approach.

The town of Clearwater is a sight for sore, sun-baked eyes. Your feet ache, your skin is sunburnt, and you're absolutely parched. A small crowd of townsfolk gather about, laughing at your misfortune and warning of some of the dangers you may see deeper within in the desert.

When you ask about the figures, much of the levity is replaced by fear. A good chunk of the population here seems to have come from the abandoned exterior towns fleeing the... Soulsmiths. It feels weird to finally have a name to the group that destroyed your home. Here, dealing with them has been a constant, and the name holds no gravitas. The townspeople say they've seen the caravans head east, towards the capitol, and warn you to stay far away from the eastern Heartroad for now. When you and [Companion Name] tell tales of Azamire and the Ringleader, and your goal of seeing the Soulsmiths brought to justice, it seems like half the town opens their homes to you, keeping you fed and hydrated as you two recover.

After some well-deserved rest, the two of you continue east finally out of the dunes and back into grassy fields. You pass into rockier terrain as you approach the Flinkcrest Highlands. Large jagged boulders dot the rocky soil, jutting out at odd angles.
How do you think they... got like that?
Yeah. Kinda... random, how they're all over the place, no?
...Maybe. But what, it's not like someone would haul them out here, right?

With that, [Companion Name] continues to peer over the boulders as the two of you travel along the Heartroad, as if they'd spring to life and tell her where they came from. You've had enough of sentient things that should otherwise not be, so you try to avoid staring too much.

Finally, you arrive at a little inn that seems to have been built into a stone wall and garrison that takes up the expansive entrance of the Broken Pass. The Sleeping Stone is legendary, and for good reason. Not only is it the home of the Slayers Guild for the eastern region of the continent, it attracts world renowned adventurers who wish to venture into the Perilous Peaks to prove themselves to be the best of the best.

The Broken Pass is the quickest way to the capitol, but it's typically travelled by highly armed caravans that can both pay the toll to pass the gate, and can fend off any beasts that travelled down from the mountain proper. When you hear of caravans being rerouted south - around the mountain range - due to a particularly feisty pack of Stonehoppers, you're quick to offer you and [Companion Name]'s services. 

The owner of the Sleeping Stone does you one better, saying that if you take care of them, you'll get free passage through the Broken Pass for life. The deal's too good to pass up.
Hopefully this will persuade them to come out and say hello.

You tally up the bodies of the tall, awkward beasts. Stonehoppers were a bit of an odd blend of creatures. They were scaly like a lizard and use a long whip-like tail for stability. They have two large wings that aid them in jumping from rock to rock - hence their name - but they were technically flightless. The 'birds' walk on two powerful legs that they used to kick at their prey, which fortunately made it easy to get them tangled up in traps.

What surprised you about them was their number. It felt like every time you caught one, you'd see two more jumping overhead.
They're getting a bit more wily the further into the pass we go.
And there's so many of them. What do you think they even eat?
Speaking of eating... how do you think they taste?
Like chicken, hopefully. They're about thirty times the size, though. Hopefully not too stringy, with all their muscles.
But do you think you could eat something that maybe would eat people, if they had the chance?
Oh without a doubt. I wouldn't do it if it ate someone recently, of course.
But what, are you telling me you'd turn down the chance to try dragon?
Depends on the type, you know.
Some of them breathe poison, can't imagine that meat would do your body any favors.
Fire-breathing dragons may be a bit burnt tasting...
OR their meat is naturally smoked with a perfect sear on the inside... imagine slicing one open and being able to dig in...
Just know, there's probably something out there talking about doing the same to you and me.
Fair's fair, if you ask me. Eat or be eaten, n' all that. Literally.

The two of you go back and forth on what creatures may or may not taste good, chatting idly back and forth as you collect the last of your traps.

As you finish prepping the last of the Stonehoppers you caught, you see one that's easily twice the others' size bounding along the cliffside. It jumps downward and pushes into a cave carved into the rock without paying you any mind. [Companion Name] looks to you eagerly.

You both clamber up the rocky wall of the Broken Pass and nearly catch a taloned foot to the face as another of the beasts head back inside to rest, seemingly not very bothered by your presence. Crawling into a beast den would be ill-advised, especially one that can kick so hard it could shatter your bones and send you bouncing around the cavern's walls. Best to smoke them out.
You really better to taste good.

The Stonehoppers living within the cave are... much larger than the little ones you managed to catch with your traps. The one that passed by as you were climbing must have done so because it didn't even register you as a threat. Now that their den is filled with smoke and the two of you stand with weapons at the ready, they seem to have changed their minds about whether or not they want to take you seriously.
Any chance I can go back to catching the comparatively smaller ones, and you can handle these... monsters?
As long as you pay me, every time we come back through the Broken Pass.
Can hardly say that you earned free passage for life if I get to have all the fun to myself.
Fine then. Let's make it a bet, then. Whichever of us takes down the least cooks dinner of of them, then.

You're both a touch nervous, despite the friendly wager. It's hard to feel particularly confident when you only come up to the Stonehoppers' thighs, but fortunately, the beasts are mostly leg. As you dodge out of the way of one of their kicks, you flinch when you see the cracks left in the stone where their foot connected.

You're beginning to understand why free passage for life was put on the table. Surely someone would have taken it sooner or later with the inn's usual clientele, but it's no cakewalk, that's for sure.
I mean... They won't mind if we borrow them, right?

You and [Companion Name] tally up your kills and... somehow, it's a dead tie. You clean your bodies and do a once-over of the den, just to make sure you got them all and neither of you could squeak out a last minute victory, but you really did get them all.

You both throw up your hands and congratulate one another on a job well done and camp out in the Broken Pass, cooking a meal together. Usually you just dig into your travel rations, but this is about as good of a chance as you'll get on the road. With some local herbs and a generous bit of seasoning... yeah, it does taste like chicken. Quite a bit more gamey, and virtually zero fat, but a great meal nonetheless.

You settle into your sleeping roll and watch the embers of the fire float up into the sky.
Always felt just a little too small, didn't it?
Yeah, a bit. I'll be happy when we do go back, but I'm not in any rush.
We'll finally be in the capitol, soon. I've dreamed about it ever since I was a kid.
Me too. But next time, let's charter a boat, hm?

After a bit of shuteye, the rest of the trip is... uneventful in a positive way. You pass by the eastern gate to the Broken Pass and tell them how you've dealt with the Stonehoppers and show them proof, to which the guards are both impressed and thankful, and promise to let those at the Sleeping Stone know.

You pass by a few villages along the rest of the Heartroad, many of them clearly prospering due to their proximity to the capitol. As you pass over the Bridge of Kings, you see the grand gates of Melvor before you, with a long trail of people waiting to be let inside.

Through talking with the crowd and a few guards who do their best to keep the peace, it sounds like the city has been under a light lockdown to new travellers because of an influx of smuggled goods. Only those bearing visitor passes or proof of citizenship are allowed entry. Visitor passes are sold for... rather exorbitant amounts.

As a group of pompous aristocrates wave their passes and bottles of wine about flamboyantly. They let out strings of taunts and insults as they walk past the line of those looking to be let into the capitol. You and [Companion Name] look to one another with wry smiles.

You follow the group along for a while until one of the richly dressed men smacks a wide-eyed child on the nose with their pass, then hurries along. The child's mother shouts after them, and the angry line of onlookers finally snaps at the mistreatment. Some of the drunken nobles cower in fear, afraid of the consequences of their own actions, while others egg the crowd on further, clearly enjoying the attention. The guards try to keep the peace, though they are clearly fed up with the 'social elite' as well, judging by their glares.

Taking advantage of the situation, you bump into one of the nobles in the and slip your hand into their coat, withdrawing a sleek sky blue visitor's pass. You keep walking as its original owner shouts after you for daring to touch them, but they're drowned out by the angry mob soon enough. [Companion Name] slides in right beside you, holding one of her own. The two of you open them up, realizing that there's no identifying information that is required, the pass alone is proof enough that you may enter.

Just like that, the gates of the capitol won't stop you. You don't even feel a little bad.

By following crumbs of information regarding the group you now know as the Soulsmiths, you've found yourself thrust into the middle of the capitol of Melvor with hardly a clue on what to do or where to go next.
Let's grab some feathers and go.

You'd heard tales of the capitol many times by those who'd travelled the continent and happened to stop by Azamire for trade or rest, but their stories hardly even begin to scratch just how... much was laid out before the two of you. Thousands of people, many speaking languages that you couldn't even begin to place. Buildings that stretch so high into the sky that you have to crane your neck to fully see. Market stalls filled with an endless number of trinkets and clothes, while some on the other side of the random plaza you'd entered emit smells so strange and tantalizing you involuntarily start to drool.
