You try your best to take in everything, excitedly chatting with [Companion Name] as you both try to point out the endless rush of... everything, until you find yourself pushing out of the crowds for the first time. You're thankful for the space, until you feel a strong hand clamp down on your shoulder and yank you backwards. Your hand goes to the weapon at your side until you realize you... walked onto a firing range! An arrow whizzes past your nose as you turn to the person who grabbed you. A tall, tanned man dressed in a gaudy purple cloak and a longbow strapped to his back pulls you out of danger, to [Companion Name] who breathlessly catches up to you.
New to the capitol, I presume?

There's a few dozen things I'd recommend to newcomers for their first day, but getting skewered in the middle of the archery contest is not one of them. But meeting me is at the top of the list. Talm. The pleasure is yours.
There you are! I took my eyes off you for two minutes!
Sorry, I was a bit distracted by... all of this.
Can't blame you. Melvor is a real bute, ain't it?
It is, you have a wonderful city... Thank you for making sure I wasn't impaled.
Of course! Can't have one of my golden geese taken out before you get the chance to help me win!

My lovely wife has shown me a vision. Me on top of the podium, being crowned the winner of this year's archery contest, with the two of you gleefully cheering me on! Under normal circumstances, about a zero percent chance I'd win...
But, between you two and I, I plan on cheating as much as I possibly can, and the two of you will help me with that.
...What makes you think we would do that?

Well, first and foremost, Era's visions are never wrong. But secondarily, ask around. Some random noble's family wins this every year, and it's not because they're the most dedicated to their craft, I can tell you that.
A combination of bribes and the best bows and arrows that money can buy turn mediocre into world-class talent, apparently. And I'm sick of seein' it.
...And let's say we do help you, because we care about the little guy sticking it to the city's nobility oh-so-much, what's in it for us?
A reading from my lovely wife, of course. One each. Assuming I win, of course. Trust me, you couldn't afford it, normally.
I appreciate you making sure that [Player Name] didn't become an archery target, but-
...You know, a vision might just even help you with your little Soulsmith problem.

Talm winks at the two of you and then holds a finger to his lips, clearly giving no further information than he's already provided. Based on how quickly you and [Companion Name] looked to one another at the mention of Soulsmiths, he knew he had you hooked. Without even asking if you'd be interested, he talks about how arrows fashioned with the feathers of a Sea Griffon always seem to find their mark, and would quite fancy having some of the arrows for himself. Unfortunately, he has no feathers, just the location of one that has been terrorizing a few fishing boats.

You and [Companion Name] leave the capitol as quickly as you came, and after a few hours of travel, find the windy cliffside that the nest was said to be. And sure enough, a large pack of the beasts swoop overhead, clearly upset by your arrival.
We'll get that reading one way or another.

Feathers gathered, the two of you make the trek back to the capitol. The city is just as overwhelming as before, but the clear goal of finding Talm again manages to help you push through the enthralling nature of the new sights and smells with ease. Talm is amongst the competitors, warming up. He's doing a remarkable job even without the feathers, nearly splitting his own arrows far down the range, and you begin to wonder why he feels the need to cheat at all.
Ah, just who I wanted to see! Hopefully the coastline is one oversized bird safer, thanks to you two?
...Try a pack. We've got your feathers. Now, it'd be nice to know how you-
Well, what am I to do with feathers? I can't very well throw them to the target, you know.
I'd appreciate it if you fashioned them into some arrows. Steel tips are fine, that's what everyone else is using, don't want to stick out too much.
Wait, we said that we'd get the feathers, not make them for you.
You're an archer, you should know how to do that.
Well, yes, of course I know how, but I have to make sure my aim is true regardless.
Isn't that what the feathers are for?
Remember, we're going up against other cheaters too. Every little advantage counts.
You don't get your readings if I don't win.

Talm's sing-songy taunt elicts a glare from [Companion Name], but after a brief standoff, she sighs and hauls you away, grumpily beginning to cut some arrow shafts. You get the impression she'd rather use that knife elsewhere, but has decided to behave, for now.
None of this looks too rare, thankfully.

The two of you make your way back to Talm, this time with a bundle of arrows, to which he recieves with a small and a small, polite show of clapping. He takes one and inspects it carefully, before bending it so far that it snaps in two. He tuts to himself and shoves the splintered arrow back into your hands.
Now now, this simply won't do. My bow may also be a bit special. Like I said, I really want to win this. The with the force I'll be sending these arrows down range, they don't stand a chance.
What do you want us to do? Make the shafts out of metal, too?
No no, of course not. Thankfully, Era came through for us and provided me with a little... somethin' somethin' ahead of time.
And now, I leave the responsibility to the two of you. No need to thank me.
I've never been more sure of anything in my life.

Talm hands you a scrap of paper that looks more akin to a grocery list than anything that'd directly help win the competition. A handful of ingredients, brought up to temperature and then distilled into a potion called 'True-Shot', could be imbued into the arrows to give them incredible strength and flexibility.

You head back to find Talm, hopefully for the final time. Just as you manage to finish applying the solution, Talm is called to the range to take his shots. Each of his arrows finds their mark at the other side of the range, faster and more powerful than any of his opponents. The competition rages on and gets more fierce as competitors are eliminated. Talm's near permanent smile is slowly replaced by a look of genuine concentration his six remaining competitors do their best to outdo one another. Criteria for each shot begin to change as the distance and size of the targets can no longer be changed. The seven of them started shooting at pea-sized targets a few rounds back, so now, they begin to fire upside-down. On horseback. Blindfolded.

Every few rounds, Talm manages to stick around as another competitor misses their mark. Even knowing how much help Talm is getting, you cannot help but cheer with each shot he lands. Unless he's going up against the best archers the world has even seen, you start to believe they have just as much assistance as he does. Talm makes it to the final round. One target, a hair-thin string gently dangling on the other side of the range. Both him and the other competitor fire at the same time, but Talm's blue-feathered arrow knocks the competitor's arrow out of the air, and severs the string on the other side.

The crowd erupts into cheers, and you find yourself cheering as well, as Talm is brought up to the top of the podium and given a trophy about a quarter of his size. After ample celebration, he finds his way back to you and [Companion Name], and after a combination of gloating and thanks, tells you to find him when you're ready for your rewards.
After helping Talm win Melvor's archery competition, you've done your part. Now, it's time for him to honor his side of the deal and hopefully provide information regarding the Soulsmiths.
This mission might be next to impossible.
Now we just... take a little mould of the lock.

Even in a city as bustling as Melvor, Talm is a remarkably easy figure to find. After just a few minutes of asking around the range, you find yourself face to face with the tall, smiling man. Without a word he gestures for you to follow him, so you do, trusting he knows what you're after. You're lead deep within the alleys and byways of the capitol, some better, some worse. As you round a corner you find yourself at the back entrance of a brightly painted stone building, door already open for you to enter. As the three of you enter, the door quietly shuts behind you without any prompting.

You're brought before an absolutely stunning woman who greets the three of you with a wordless smile, and gestures for you to sit on cushions laid out in front of her. You do, and the room quickly fills with a twinkling blue fog. You panic for a moment before deciding that they don't seem to mean you harm, and you inhale deeply.

Your vision fades away, then comes back to you as you're flying far overhead a large white building, whose doors seem to suck you in. You fall through the floor of the building and weave through shelf and shelf of books, all the way to a large vault made of a blend of metals and magic you instinctively know as you pass through its walls. Within, you find a gilded tome that seems to glow with power. The moment you touch it, you snap back awake next to [Companion Name]. She seems... upset, seemingly a bit disturbed by whatever she saw.
What... was that? Did you see the same thing, [Companion Name?]
I uh... doubt it. What'd you see?
A large white building with what was almost a maze under it, and then a vault.
Ah. You saw the Abyssal Vault, did you?
Best of luck getting inside, I've only been a few times, myself.
Era, you can't spoil it. That's half the fun.
They have much ground to cover, and little time.
What do you mean? [Companion Name] are you alright?
Since my dear already spoiled the surprise, it sounds like you two need to engage in a little...
Heist. Of sorts. Should be a cakewalk.
We just got to town. I don't think jail is on my list of places I'd like to see.
It shouldn't have to be, if you're careful.
The vault requires a key, but before you can make one, you'll have to obtain a mold of the lock.
And if we were to do something so unscrupulous, which we aren't by the way, how are we to know you wouldn't turn us in?
If you're after information on the Soulsmiths, and it has lead you to the vault, stopping you would be... unwise.
Feel free to try and gain lawful access to the vault if you wish, I promise you it would not be fruitful.
And how do the two of you know about them? And that we're... interested?
Era and I indulge in the visions she can provide quite often, really.
One of them showed you two, and through that, what you've been up to.
And what you must face. Go now, return when you've gotten what you need.

And with that, Talm helps Era up and takes her to a room behind a nearby curtain. It doesn't seem like you're invited. You check on [Companion Name] once again, about the vision she had. She gently, tells you that she'll talk about it later, just that it was a bit scary. 

The two of you wander around the city, a bit less awestruck than when you first arrived, and soon enough, find yourselves on the doorstep of the Ivory Athenaeum. From what you learn, speaking with some of the guests and staff, it'd seem that the titanic structure holds the largest compilation of humanity's knowledge ever created, with a near endless number of books on every subject one could think of.

You ask about the lower floors, and learn that they are restricted to the general public, needing a direct invitation from the King himself to be let inside, since the books down there contain dangerous information. The process of obtaining an invitation is told to you through a long, well-rehearsed deluge of information. What sticks out to you is the time involved. An average of thirty years for those prestigious enough to be allowed a chance. Too long.
The vision proved particularly useful, didn't it?
This looks about right. Back down we go.

You want to let out a cheer as the Abyssal Vault comes into view, but you obviously know better than that. You put [Companion Name] up on your shoulders and she slowly but surely presses a wedge of clay into the arcane locking mechanism. The vault is exactly as it appeared in your vision, and you do your best to memorize the magic that courses through it as [Companion Name] deals with the mould. You know from your vision that you'll have to imbue the key with the same magic for it to actually work when you come back and let yourself in.

Now that you've properly mapped out the route to the vault, you're able to get back to the entrance with little trouble. Understandably, the patrolling guards are both few and number and a bit inattentive, it's not like many people would be crazy enough to try this. You and [Companion Name] make it back out of the Ivory Athenaeum, and finally allow yourself to breathe.
...I can't believe we'll have to do it again.
We already made it in once, what's the worst that could happen?
I don't even want to humor that question with a guess.
We'll be fineeee, I'm sure of it. 50 gold say we make it back down there without a problem.
How about we bet bail on it, hm? I can't even imagine how many years we'd get.
Well, you don't need to imagine. Because we just did it! Let's get started on that key, hm?

You take the mould and start to jot down everything you'll need onto a piece of paper. Everything for the perfect alloy to match the material of the vault, along with what you remember of the magical barrier that surged through the exterior of the vault.
I don't think he's going to let us out of here.

Sure enough, the patrols and traps seem to be exactly the same as the first time you came down here. It isn't particularly a surprise, but it still lets you relax a bit as you slink through the endless rows of bookshelves, back to the door of the vault. Your dark clothes and molded face-mask restrict your breathing a little bit, but on the off-chance that someone sees you, you'll be glad for the anonymity it provides.

You reach up and slide your key into the lock, and with a clunk - one that's a bit louder than you would have hoped for - the Abyssal Vault door cracks open, just a pinch. You and [Companion Name] slip inside and find row after row of plinths, holding not just books, but what look like dangerous phials of liquid, weapons, and maps. [Companion Name] whispers across the vault to you.
What's the title of the book again? There's dozens of them.
I didn't see... It was just bound in black leather, and gilded with gold. Bout... this big.
I'll let you know if I see it. Don't die.

The two of you quickly search through the displayed items until you find what you're looking for. The black, gilded tome from your vision. Amongst everything else in the vault, you'd almost call it unassuming. 

It hums with some unknown magic, and you give it a ginger touch with your hand. When you don't immediately get vaporized by some unknown power, you lift it from its resting place and crack it open. The first page says... Something in a language you've never seen before. You snap it closed and gently wave it for [Companion Name] to see. She carefully crosses the vault and takes the book, and the two of you head back to the entrance. However, the moment your hand touches the metal of the door to push to back open, it snaps shut. A loud hum fills the room, along with what sounds like an alarm outside of the vault.

As you look to [Companion Name], a large golem seems to coalesse from the ground, made of the same alloy as the rest of the vault. [Companion Name] readies her weapon, and you follow suit.

As the golem falls and melts back into the floor, the door to the vault blessedly clicks open once again. You and [Companion Name] gather yourselves to see... roughly fifty guards running in your direction down the hall, likely with many more behind them.
I said we'd get down here safe. I didn't say anything about getting back out!

The two of you begin scaling the bookshelves outside of the vault and run as fast as you can. Fearful of destroying the collection, the guards refuse to fire upon you but give chase back down the halls, slowed by the same traps meant to stop intruders. The tops of the shelves have just as many, if not more traps.

The two of you run like your lives depend on it, because they likely do. Every time you're singed by a magical barrier or narrowly dodge a guardsman's pike, you just think about how many lifetimes you'd likely spend in Melvor's jails. That is, if they didn't just outright execute you. You make sure not to hurt anyone, because murder wouldn't likely get you any better treatment if you were to be captured.

By some miracle, you manage to make it to the stairwell leading up out of the lower floors. Stunned guardsmen scramble to bring their weapons at the ready - clearly not anticipating any intruders actually making it back to the entrance - and the two of you manage to burst back out into the main floor of the athenaeum.

You rush outside and into the throngs of people being evacuated outside. Guards point and shout at the two of you as you melt into the crowds but fail to give chase as you quickly slip deeper and deeper into the mass of concerned citizens. The two of you find yourselves at the edge of a canal and jump in, swimming under the water all the way to an exposed sewer grate. You let yourselves inside and strip off your disguises and toss them into the water, both silent as the adrenaline slowly works it way through your bodies. You quietly laugh and lean against the wall of the sewer with a sick squelch you don't even notice. You did it. You got out, somehow.

After the miraculous heist of the Abyssal Vault, it's time to return to Era and Talm. Maybe they'll be able to tell you something about the book you managed to steal, considering you haven't the slightest clue on what it says.
I doubt Talm will let us take his equipment after this. The recipe won't do us any good afterwards.
As useful as it might otherwise be...

[Companion Name] flicks the gilded tome open and closed, looking at it from every angle she can, and trying a few different pages. Like you, she hasn't the foggiest clue about what the book says, and the place that would likely know, is still searching high and low for it. You and [Companion Name] have left your little sewer hideaway and sure enough, the disguises you donned before the heist worked. No one comes to put you in shackles and haul you off to some dark dungeon. As far as anyone else is concerned, you're just one of the many thousands of tourists to the capitol.

You head back to Era and Talm's home and find it... in flames. Talm worriedly tries to douse the flames with many other passerby, until a capitol mage buries the building under a deluge of water. You rush to Talm. Your presence gives him pause, and he gestures for you two to follow him.
Come on. We need to see what's left!
Talm, what happened? Is Era with you?
She knew she would be, of course... We just didn't know when.
The visions aren't always... precise. Come with me, please.

The urgency and pain in his voice spur you and [Companion Name] to follow. The three of you push into the smoking building and find the back room drenched, but relatively untouched by the flames. The room is a disaster and there's signs of a scuffle that are clear even despite the water and fire. Talm sighs, but seems more calm than he was before the two of you arrived.

He opens a chest tucked in a corner and pulls out what seems to be alchemy equipment. He laments how Era will feel about him giving away trade secrets, but shows you how to make the same vision-inducing smoke you inhaled before your heist, saying that it should be able to help the three of you find Era. You think about bringing up the book, but figure it can wait for now.

Talm crowds around as you burn the large pouches of the specialized herbal blend. It doesn't seem as strong as the last time you had it, and you're unsure of if you did something wrong or if it's just part of a building tolerance.

Nevertheless, you find yourself feeling much of the same sensation as before, but this time, you float over a small, ramshackle hut deep within what you presume are Melvor's slums. The only distinguishing characteristic is a single crescent-shaped grey marking by its door. As you come back to, Talm blinks his eyes, seemingly coming back to reality as well. [Companion Name] holds her hands over her face, waving the smoke away and asking if you two saw what you needed to.
You didn't use the smoke, [Companion Name]?
I will if I need to... but...
That's understandable, I'm sorry, I didn't think about...
I saw a building out in the slums. There were... probably hundreds just like it. I'm sorry, but that's all I got.
It's okay. The Sightsmoke shows you... whatever you need to see. Era would know how to explain it better.
But don't worry, I saw the path to the area. Just point out if you can, okay?

The three of you set off, leaving the burned building behind. Talm leads you through the city with such ease and purpose you get the feeling he's been here a long, long, time. As you travel, the people you see become less friendly, and more dirty. Desperate. The slums were doubtlessly going to be here, like any other large city, but to see them up close was a staunch difference to when you first arrived in the capitol a few weeks ago.

Rougher looking folks give you a large berth when they lock eyes with Talm. The generally friendly man now walks with murderous intent, his bow now set aside for a longsword and shield that he carries openly. He looks back to you frequently, making sure you're looking out for the shack as diligently as he'd hope for. And sure enough, you see it. The crescent shaped by the door - just like in your vision - is so loud to your eyes, you almost don't understand how [Companion Name] and Talm don't see it.

You point it out, and without a word, Talm approaches the door and sends it off its hinges with a startlingly powerful kick. You eye [Companion Name], who charges in right behind him. Swords clash almost immediately.

Just like you remember, all that time ago. Hooded figures with beasts you've never seen or heard of, clash with you and your companions. However, unlike back at Azamire, you don't fall. You drive them back into the building, where more of their beasts materialize from nothing, following a few quickly spoken words and a flash of light. They bare down on you, but you push them back, again and again, until the last of the hooded figures falls.

You worry about the commotion until you realize that... the guards likely don't make it out this far.

You search the building and find many of Era's things. Books and scrolls in a similar script to the gilded tome you took from the Abyssal Vault, and many others in different writing that seems to flow and move like water on the page. But the woman herself doesn't seem to be here. Talm slams his fist into a nearby table in anger, splintering the wood.

You look to the man, who hardly seems to notice the few small cuts he took to his arms and side. He doesn't look back to you as he reaches a hand out to one of the dead figures. Their body begins to contort, cracking and lurching with sickening jolts, as the body seems to right itself once again. The man rises, standing on his feet once again despite several wounds that should have left him as nothing but a corpse.

[Companion Name] says it before you can. Soulsmith. Talm turns to you both, finally snapping out of his pure drive to find his wife. He sputters out an apology, and promises to explain everything, he just needs a little time. He begs you to come back in just a little bit, if you can stomach it. [Companion Name] backs away slowly before pushing into you, bringing you both outside, leaving the man alone.

Talm has revealed himself to have some form of control over the dead, just like the Soulsmiths who burned your home. While he may hold no love for them after the kidnapping of Era, he has a lot to explain. Quickly.

[Companion Name] and you are still reeling from Talm's reveal. What is he? What'd he do to that Soulsmith? If he has the same powers as them, why is he against them? The two of you bounce questions off one another in an endless, confusing jumble of words until you realize you have none of the answers, and can hardly even begin to guess.

There's only one way to learn. You both enter the shoddy hut on the edge of Melvor's slums, weapons in hand, and find Talm right where you left him. His hands are covered in blood as he seems to be patching the least damaged clothes of the hooded figures together, piling them on top of the... walking corpse until it resembles a living person. Talm seems almost surprised to see you again, manages a few attempts of pleading his allegiance, but then sucks in a deep breath and just... tells you to ask away.
Why'd you turn on the Soulsmiths?
I... I didn't turn on them, I've never been on. I'm a Summoner. A very old one, at that.
My clan has... had, similar powers to this upstart band of wannabes.
The things we could do back in the day... The Soulsmiths don't even come close. Yet.
I've been called devilish. And I am currently enthralling the corpse of my enemy to take me to my kidnapped wife.
But, for the intention of your question, no. I'm not.
If anything, I'm rather aligned against the Soulsmiths, and most who seek to use Summoning, for that matter.
You said you're old. How old?
I was around before... this capitol. And the one before it. Era too.
What I, and the clan you know as the Soulsmiths use, is a form of magic called Summoning. You've likely heard bits and pieces of it since you started your journey.
Summoning is broken into many different disciplines. My clan is gone, but our discipline, clearly, is not.
What they use is an offshoot of what I use. My people were called Lifebinders. People after us will call it something else.
I can more-or-less reverse the effects of aging, and I've done so for myself and Era for many... many years.
What's the book we got from the Abyssal Vault?
You raided one of the most secure locations in the capitol for... what's basically a children's history book.
Next question. Can you use that summoning magic on yourself? Because you might need to.
You clearly knew parts of what our visions were going to be. You didn't think to tell us THAT?
It's an IMPORTANT children's history book!
It details one of the most defining events in our world's history... I... literally cannot tell you what, though. The few of us from... Those times, are magically bound against it.
Era can help you with reading it more than I can, but suffice to say, if you want to learn about the Soulsmiths and what they want to do, this book is as good as you're going to get for now.
Era's visions may have holes, and may be hard to interpret at times, but they're never wrong.
From what I've seen... I needed to help you. The whole thing with the archery contest, meeting you two... It wasn't an accident.
Well, I didn't expect you to try and get yourself shot, but beyond that, all planned out. For what, I cannot say.
Now. This thrall is about as pretty as I can make him. Shall we see if he can take us to Era?

You caught [Companion Name]'s flinch when Talm said that Era's visions are never wrong. But why? What'd she see? You've tried asking, gently, over the last couple of weeks, but you've hardly gotten anything other than it being 'bad'.

Talm utters a command in a language you cannot understand to the thrall, and it shutters for a moment, before walking off at a leisurely pace. The three of you follow close behind until you get to the main gates of the capitol. You flinch as you approach the guards and Talm pulls the thrall between you and him. He takes on a drunken sway and starts slurring gibberish as the guard looks your party over. The woman pinches her nose and remarks that you 'smell like death' and waves you off.

You do your best to wipe off the thrall's blood that leaked through his pilfered robes once you're out of eyeshot, cursing quietly to yourself. The thrall leads you far out of town and out into the countryside. Once you hit the treeline of a nearby forest, Talm curses and releases his command of the thrall, who slumps to the ground. He says he knows where they went.

You're lead to a large stone tower that blends well into the rocky landscape. It once had a large wooden door that now lays splintered in a dozen large chunks on the ground. Talm exclaims that they attacked his 'real' home, and that the security system was set off.

Having dodged your way through an impressive array of traps, you slowly made it up to the tower's uppermost floor. Era lays in a pool of blood at the foot of a large arcane telescope, made of a metal you can't even begin to place.
...None of you will live to regret this.

Seeing Era on the ground, Talm wordlessly launches himself against the group of Soulsmiths occupying the floor, not seeming to pay any mind to whether or not you and [Companion Name] join him. Of course, you follow right behind. Soulsmiths deserve no quarter.
What does Era wish for us to see?

You lower your weapon as your last opponent falls, with [Companion Name] finishing up right after you. Talm pushes a Soulsmith against the wall of the ringed tower and the man brings his hands up in fear. He chokes out a plea for his life before Talm rams his blade into the man's chest and into the stone behind him, pinning him to the wall.

The three of you breathe silently, taking in the sight around you before... a slight cough sounds from over by the telescope. Talm leaves his weapon in the wall and runs over to his wife's body, immediately reaching out to perform... some form of magic on her, like he did with the man back in the shack. You and [Companion Name] turn away from them, leaving the couple to their privacy, or as much as they can have, considering the circumstances.
Messy... You have all... Gotten the place so bloody...

[Companion Name] and you look at each other, grimacing a bit as the following silence is punctuated by the sounds of tearing flesh and sickening gurgles. You feel a bit faint listening to Talm work on his... not dead wife. If one can reverse the effects of aging then... perhaps mending wounds falls under that domain as well. You see [Companion Name] shoot a glance in their direction then quickly avert her eyes, clutching her mouth after a quiet heave. You think better of it.

You nearly leap out of your skin when you feel a couple of light taps on your shoulder and come face to face with the incredibly pale visage of Era. Her wounds stitched together, the only remnant of them being the tears in dress from which any number of weapons pieced her. 

She welcomes you to her home and starts to apologize for the mess, before then frowning, realizing your part in its current state. The fact that she was on death's door just moments ago seemingly not bothering her in the slightest. If they're truly as old as Talm claims, you wonder how many times someone could have crossed a similar scene.

Era gestures for [Companion Name] and has Talm bring a chair over, to which she practically slumps in. She runs her hands over the book with fondness, then gives a few directions for adjustmenting telescope. She invites the both of you to use it.

The stars stretch out before you, incalculable in number. As you peer up at them through Era's telescope, they twist and turn in so many beautiful arrays and patterns you almost want to weep. As you try to commit them to memory, they dance ever so carefully out of reach again and again. You take breaks when the floor beneath you sways like the gentle rocking of a ship at sea. [Companion Name] takes your place in these bits of downtime. You chat here and there with Era and Talm, who both look at you with a degree of fondness that comes off as... almost warm, though the feeling almost feels misplaced.

The sight is punctuated by that of Talm's new thralls, the broken bodies of the Soulsmiths being twisted to work on... repairs and cleanup. The sight is as macabre as it is absurd. A pair of thralls mop up after one another in a circle, each trying to clean the trailing blood from their comrade. You shudder at the sight. When one of the thralls tries to remove Talm's sword from the wall and ends up tearing its arm out of its socket. 

You nearly faint. Talm curses softly, and Era simply chuckles. You make note to never get on either of their bad sides. Ever. You know the Soulsmiths are truly wretched and you'd never spill a tear over them, but the level of... flippance that Era and Talm have at seeing their undead bodies lerch about feels unnerving, at least for now.

You rest and recuperate in their home, taking turns with [Companion Name], peering through the telescope and trying to glean insight from the stars. Once the thralls were disposed of and the traps turned off, the tower really was nice. Though, some of the things you saw may sit with you for a long while.
The stars have finally shown you what you needed to see. A lone cold point, deep within the mountain range west of the capitol. That is your next target.
Melting alone won't do it. We'll need to hack away at the ice, too.
I think I can just about crack the door open.

Your head feels fuzzy, at each breath - if you even are still breathing anymore - feels shaky and labored. You've grown far more accustomed to Era's telescope, but it still makes you feel as if something within your very being is shifting after long enough. You can practice astrology without it, but as you've learned through numerous conversations, Era's telescope is special. While Talm's summoning domain is Soul, Era's is knowledge and divination. You can't even begin to imagine what kind of creatures she can bring forth. The smoke and telescope are just two tools that allow her to practice.

And now you have done so as well. Similarly to how you felt with the Sightsmoke, you feel as if you raise from the tower and pass through its walls. You grasp for the shingled roof, but your hands pass through it without so much as grazing it. You careen up into the sky, far beyond the tower and up amongst the clouds. Your body rights itself, and you feel yourself slingshot towards the Broken Pass, then turn north, to an inlet in the mountains covered with frost and snow. As you shoot towards a stone door carved into the cliffside, you close your eyes... and end up back on the floor of the tower.

You are covered in ice, and your teeth chatter violently, but you feel so... so warm.
[Player Name]! Are you okay? You were here, there was a flash of light, and now you're...
I know where we need to go.
I don't know why we need to go there, but I know we do.
You think we'll finally be able to read our children's book if we go risk our lives somewhere?
I think so. And... so much more, possibly. You interested?
You'll finally be leaving us behind, hm?
Aw. Are you feeling sentimental, dear?
Well, they did help me win that competition.
Well yes, but it was foretold that I'd win because you two helped!
Was there something in those visions about... using a thrall to serve me breakfast in bed?
No, that was a Talm original.
I know you two are rather squeamish, but you'll be seeing a lot more death before you're through this all.
I don't mind corpses, or even making a few myself. But when they show up with a platter of bacon, I might just lose my appetite.

Era and Talm laugh at that, while you and [Companion Name] may feel a bit more genuinely about the situation. Nevertheless, your goodbyes are heartfelt. The two of them wish you well on your travels, and you get the feeling that this is the last of them you'll see for quite some time.

You and [Companion Name] head west, stopping in a small town by the name of Riverbend to resupply, then make the trek north, to what the locals call Rimeriver Crevice. The place is an uncharacteristically cold bit of land that stretches far into the mountains with 'not much of note'.

You are glad you stocked up, as green, grassy hillocks turn to freezing glaciers and rolling snow dunes over the course of hours. There's doubtlessly something unnatural about the weather, as even you can tell that the sleet is magically enhanced. Each flake seems to chill you to the bone. Your bundled forms eventually reach the doorway you saw, etched into the cliffside, shielded from the weather... mostly. The door itself has immense braziers on either side, and seems to be frozen shut. You wager a guess that it needs to be thawed.

The ice melts agonizingly slowly, but eventually, with some prodding with your pickaxes between the two stone doors, you're able to push your way inside. Inside the cave is comparatively balmy. The interior is well-furnished, but certainly abandoned. Many of the doorways along the single stone hall you travel are shut and bound by some form of magic that reminds you of the Abyssal Vault, but... much, much older. 

The few rooms that are open seem to have once been living quarters, built more for capacity than for luxury. However, there's not a single hint of where anyone could have gone. No bodies. No messages.

You and [Companion Name] push further inside, to a room at the end of the hall that opens up into a large open cavern that seems naturally made. You walk up and bump [Companion Name] with your shoulder as you head deeper into the room.
It feels like it's been a bit, since it was just you and I, doing something for ourselves.
I would never have guessed we'd have gotten wrapped up in something so... much bigger than ourselves.
Neither would I. But it's cool, travelling the world together, no? We always talked about how we wanted to.
Maybe under different circumstances, but yeah. It's hard to think of just how much has happened in so little time.
You can say that again. I missed this.
When this is all over, let's do a bit of travelling under better circumstances, hm?
I'd drink to that. Where would you want to go?
Somewhere where it doesn't feel like something is going to eat me or stab me every couple of minutes. How about-

With that, a loud rumbling roar tears through the cavern and sends the both of you to your knees. You clamp your hands to your ears and turn your head up to see the call's source. A yeti. The shaggy beast lumbers over, its blue knuckles dragging across the floor as it seemingly wakes from a slumber that must have spanned countless years.

[Companion Name] gives you one of her signature glares, as if your words brought the creature into being. So much for wishful thinking.

The beast staggers back with a cry as your blows connect with its hard flesh. It falls to the ground with a mighty crash, and slumps back against the cavern wall. It releases a breath and begins to... fade away to crystals of ice that melt shortly afterward. Whatever the beast was, it wasn't natural. As you begin to look over the murals etched and painted into the wall, you feel quite sure of that assumption.

The murals depict the group that once inhabited the cavern. Little blue figures of people living in a beautiful blue forest. Then... the forest burning due to some unknown red assailants riding on similarly colored creatures. After that, there are far fewer blue figures in a blackened forest. The numbers dwindle further and further with each section of wall. Until the blue figures leave the charred forest. The murals show them travelling far... very far. Almost half the cavern wall depicts them travelling from one place to another, in all manner of places. They settle for short periods of time, with each move always predicated by a clash with some new color of figure. Brown, grey, green, red, orange, and even a lighter color blue towards the end. These figures are accompanied by beasts. All drawn simply in nature, but clearly terrifying to those who lived here. You catch yourself wiping your eyes more than once as you spend over an hour trying to follow their story.

Finally, in the last tenth of the wall, it shows the figures... finding what you presume to be this place. They find a book. They create their own creatures. The figures leave the wall and travel across the floor, to spires of ice that jut out from the ground, one nearly touching the ceiling.

You realize, the center of the the room looks... similar to a page of the book you cannot read. You lay it out and [Companion Name] holds the her lantern overhead as you trace out places that line up. Two pages of the book, when lined up with the central pillar of ice, resemble the eastern portion of the continent. And within that map, a shining tower lays just off the coast. Comparing it to current maps, it'd be far north of the capitol. Your next destination.

You spare a last glance to the figures on the ground, crowded around the spire of ice. It's the last of their journey, none left their last destination. You can only imagine what the spire represents, but it's a mystery for another time.

In their quest to find the shining tower shown to them by the history book stolen from the Ivory Athenaeum, [Player Name] and [Companion Name] find themselves travelling far north of the capitol, to a lonely little fishing village tucked into the coast.
Head inland enough, should be able to grow something.
That should be enough. Let's see our vessel.

Having made it to Tidebreak, PC seek the help of an young fisherman, who is willing to trade his boat in exchange for helping him change his livelihood since he cannot stand the sea or fish. PC help him plant fields of crops (Farming) and he trades them his boat, a horrendously trashed little dingy. PC fix it up, with Player creating a new keel for it to withstand the rocks (Smithing), along with a sail (Crafting). (3 Steps)

An old cobbled road takes you and your companion far north, just outside of a town by the name of Tidebreak. The population is said to be rather reclusively, mostly prefering to keep to their own and subsist on what they can fish up. The sea breeze goes from refreshing to... almost sour the further north you get. You get why not many people decided to live up this way, and question the motives of those that do. You push on ahead as the sun begins to set.

The town itself is... quaint. You feel eyes on you everywhere you go, and kids are pulled inside ahead of your path. You find yourself on the coast, where a lone young man works a length of rope, hardly sparing you a glance. Another man, who almost seems like he could be his brother, looks on and even gives you a smile, which you almost find weirder. You try your chances with the rope worker first.
You've got a lovely little town here, might I say.
Fortunate enough to still have my vision...
Oh, leave the poor boy be. Joshry's always grumpy when he gets shown up at the Hauling.
Yes ya do, and the rest of 'em too.
The Hauling. Weekly little get together when all us sailors show off whatever we managed to scrape off the ocean floor.
Not to inner-esting less you's an academic.
That's why everyone here cares so much. Bunch of scholars, we are.
Bet our findings will get added to that big ivory building in the capitol, soon enough. Should go take a look at it yourself someday, real purdy.
Well, I'm quite over it all, myself. No one here seems to care much about pulling up ten corpses for every half rusted spoon they can dredge out of the ocean.
No one but yours truly. Can't stand it.
Tidebreak look like a place where we've got an abundance of career diversity?
Everyone that's been here has been doing what they do for more years than ol' Josh and I put together.
Opening comes up when they kick the bucket.
Fancy making some gold by ferrying us around, then?
What, you two come here for a bita sightseeing?
Close. We want to go to the island way off the coast.
...oh. We don't go other there. Gloomstone's a ba-
Now now now, I'm sure our friends here are well aware of the risks.
Just a bit of choppy water n' the like, of course. Couple beasties if you're tasty. Nothin' they can't handle.
But tell you what. You can have my boat, if you do me a lil' favor.

Rommard goes into detail about grand visions for the town. All the little things he wants to do to 'give back'. Neither you nor [Companion Name] buy it for a second, of course, but you feel as though the man in front of you is the best option you'll get. As dire as that sounds.

His ire for having to fish out Gods know what from the sea seems true, as he'd rather work the land and earn his keep that way. Only issue, Tidebreak has never bothered trying to trade for seeds. 'The sea will provide' is something you hear around, often.'
I'll need to make something that'll help it weather the rocky shore.
This ought to do it. Let's see how [Companion Name] is coming along.

[Companion Name] and you plant row after row of crops, then run through the details of crop rotations and how to care for seedlings. To his credit, Rommard does actually pay attention and even takes some pretty extensive notes. He does leave the two of you do actually do all the work, though.

Once you're done, Rommard jumps upright and brings you back over to the docks, detailing how all deals are final, and that his boat's a bit of a fixer-upper, but will get you to the island. Probably.

The only 'boat' left on the docks could be mistaken for a wreck that someone tethered to the pier. Rommard presents it with a flourish, then turns on his heel, setting off into town. He calls out to you one last time.
The F.V. Not My Problem Anymore!
It's not... that bad. Is it?
[Player Name], it might be easier to start from scratch. I'm shocked the thing's even floating to begin with.
Judging by the coastline, the island's gonna be rocky. And, I don't fancy paddling to a place I can't even see.
I'll work on a keel and a sail.
...I'll see what I can do about getting this thing... sea-worthy.
[Companion Name] grumbles to herself and begins prodding at the boat. It drops concerningly low under the water when she puts her weight on it, which elicits a string of curses.
It can't be that hard, can it?

You arrive at the docks to see something akin to a miracle. The boat - if you could even call it that - has been worked into a proper skiff. It wasn't fancy, but it looked like it could support a couple of people and make it more than two minutes off the shore without capsizing, which is leagues better than it used to be. [Companion Name] beams with pride.
I don't know how you made it down to the capitol and bought a proper boat, but I'm glad you did!
As if I was going to let that gross little creature pull one over on us. He'll be begging for this boat back when we're done.
Start thinking of a name, hm?
Spite is quite the motivator, ain't it?

The two of you get to work, fitting the keel to the boat. It takes ages, replacing the scrap metal that used to serve the same purpose. Once the worst of it is over, [Companion Name] waves you off, telling you to get to weaving or knitting or whatever you need to do for creating a sail.

You bring you sail to the dock and find [Companion Name] floating in the water, treating the boat with what you presume to be waterproofing. You set the sail on the ground and help haul them out of the brine, to which they shake like a dog and get you drenched. You threaten to shove them in, so they wrap their arms around you and threaten to haul you both back in. You shove them off and roll your eyes, to which they give one of the first genuinely laughs you've heard from them in a long while.

Why they decided that smelling like stale water and rotting wood was their happy place, you may never know, but you can't help but smile after seeing them happy. The two of you fit the sail to your skiff and sit on the dock, admiring your handiwork. You each carve your name into its railing, and give it a firm pat. It's ready for its journey. Are you?
All signs point to Gloomstone, and you're as ready as you'll ever be. It's time to learn what the Soulsmiths are after, or sink somewhere far off the coast.

Glass shatters as you break a bottle of wine over the ship's bow. [Companion Name] holds her steady as you jump aboard, cutting the rope loose and gracefully landing on the deck, your momentum carrying the boat out into the water. The sheepish townsfolk of Tidebreak silently watch as you set off, several of them actually tracing marks of good fortune in the air. You're pleasantly surprised.

The two of you move about the skiff, setting the sail and getting it as ready as you can to sail.
Guess they don't want to haul any fresh bodies out of the water, hm?
It's anyone's guess. Maybe Rommard put in a good word for us?
So. How many days of stuff do we got?
A week, at least. I really hope it doesn't take that long though.
I hope the tower is actually out there.
The cavern was fine, sure. But this is a bit more... hostile of an environment.
We'll see when we get there!

You two chat back and forth, enjoying the pretty peaceful trip. The shore slowly fades further... and further... and further away, until it's just the two of you gliding across the dark blue water. You're long past the point of being able to swim back to shore. Even without your gear on, the water is cold, and hypothermia would set in long before you made it even a tenth of the way back, assuming the current was cooperating with you.

The two of you catch sleep in waves, each trading off, hoping that you're vaguely headed in the right direction. From what you were able to find, Gloomstone is... quite large but even still, half a day into sailing, you start to wonder if you missed it, or if a children's book in a dead language may have not been the best reference material.

You awake to [Companion Name] calling for you. Something is ahead. A lot of somethings. Giant pillars jut from the icy waters like fingers of stone that threaten to pull you into the depths. [Companion Name] mans the sails, and pleads for you to get them through this safely. With the pillars being barely lit by the moon, you turn to the stars.
I think we're doing them a favor.

Your boat bumps and scrapes against the rocks, and you're glad you spent so long forging its keel. Wind whips at the sail, pulling the two of you through the stone spires at a breakneck pace. While nothing like using Era's telescope, your skills in astrology prove fruitful, guiding you through the pillars relatively unscathed.

The two of you float further and further into the cluster of rocks until you can make out... land. You scrape along the shore a bit harder than you're comfortable with, but the two of you and your boat seem to be intact. [Companion Name] shouts with joy and nervous energy leaving her body.
Oh by the Gods we made it! I can't believe it.
By the Gods? Not used to you referring to them.
We've been talking with two immortals that play with the dead and fighting against a force that creates monsters from darkness.
We fought a golbin horde and travelled across most of the continent.
We've saved dozens of people in our travels, and now, we just pulled off one of the most miraculous feats of sailing I've ever seen or heard of.
We live in interesting times. If the Gods just so happened to pop out of the sea and ask us for tea, I'd call that a boring day, at this point.
We... really did make it. That was some fine steering you did.
You're the one that pulled it out of the stars. You pointed, I moved. Let's just call it a joint effort, eh?

You nod and give out a shout of your own, happy to have your feet on dry land. You anchor the boat and pull it as far ashore as you can. The skiff is large, and the moment the majority of it leaves the water, you can't pull it any further.

The two of you grab what you need and head inland. One spire stands out amongst them all, and this one is much larger than the rest. After a small trek, you enter into the old tower, its doors surprisingly open, as if something was waiting for you. And once you're inside, you realize... something is. Piles of bodies shift towards you. It reminds you of Talm's thralls on a much larger and more horrific scale. The amalgamations of flesh and metal twist and moan in horrific fashion, and doubtlessly hostile intent.

The piles of corpses stop moving, the which is as good to dead as you can imagine they can get. It's not just the bodies, though. The whole tower seems... still. Stale. As if it was frozen in time. 

Despite its incredible height, you can only see a single floor, the one you're on. The two of you search high and low, finding... nothing. The place is decorated with stone benches and tables and lit with pale yellow-green lights that make you feel sick, but little else. You sit by the pool in the center of the room, watching the corpse piles slowly turn to ash.
They must be summoned beasts, like the Yeti we fought.
Reminds you of Talm, doesn't it?
You read my mind. I wonder... Do you think this tower belonged to the...
How many ages have those miserable piles of souls haunted this place?
At least they can rest now. Whoever or whatever they were.
Can't say the same for us, though. I refuse to have come all this way just for a creepy little tower with no answers.

As you trail off, you take a deeper look into the pool. Unlike the rest of the tower, it almost exudes warmth. It's inviting. You pull out the gilded black book and flip through the pages of scrawl you cannot read. Several pages after the map shows the tower. Several pages after that, an overhead view of a circular room. Within that room a smaller circle of... paradise, is the only word that comes to mind.

On the next page, the page is cut in half. On the top half, people stand in water on the 'real' side of the world. These people seem sad, angry, and some even sport wounds in a way that's a bit surprising for what's meant to be a children's book. Among them are people holding purple vials, who seem to be in the process of passing out. Some of the tables in the illustration seem to be open in the center.

The other half of the page is lovely, mirroring the top half. These people are upside down, holding hands and smiling with one another. You look to the sheet of placid water in the center of the room once again, and motion for [Companion Name] to sit beside you.

You come to the same conclusion. You need to pass through. After splashing about in the warm water for a while feeling no different - as crazy as it may be - you come to the same conclusion. You need to find and make the purple vials. You wedge blades into the center of tables around the room until one gives way, revealing the same vials as the book held, along with herbs and ingredients you assume go inside.

The moment the liquid hits your tongue, you feel... nothing. Your body falls backward into the water, but you're not in it any longer. You watch as the liquid washes over you, then [Companion Name]. You scream, but hear nothing. You want to try to push yourself back into your body, but cannot seem to will yourself forward. You feel still, but your mind cries out over and over again that what's happening is wrong.

Bit by bit you see your body wither away, like the rotting of a fruit sped up a hundred-fold. You feel regret at everything you never got the chance to do. Bitter over falling for such a stupid trick. Remorse for getting [Companion Name] involved. Calm, over knowing that it's... out of your hands now. Warmth for the hundreds of happy memories you've made through the years, even if it was cut short. Thankful for everyone you've gotten to know, good and bad. You're a mixture of countless emotions, good and bad, but this is all you've got. Nothing left to be done about it.

You pass through the other side, your consciousness slamming back into your body. You feel your body materialize and peel away from the sickly sweet membrane of the mirrored pool. You fall through the air and weightlessly hit the stone ground. Feeling slowly returns to your body as you remember how to move. How to breathe.

You rub your eyes as you sit up... You're... in paradise.

Grey flesh coats the walls and pulses like the beat of a heart. The stone beneath you is an endless path of mottled bone held together with sinew. You hear screams echo out around you as you move to your feet. But where is it-
PLEASE! I WILL NOT LEAVE YOU HERE BUT YOU NEED TO GET UP!

Your eyes snap open. [Companion Name]'s eyes are wide in fear, in a way you haven't seen since the Soulsmiths first attacked Azamire.

You look back and see it. A twisted being formed of... human matter. The creature drags itself down pathway and towards you with frightening speed. Everything about it seems... incompatible with life. With each movement its claws tear into the walls of this hellscape and it pulls itself towards you. Closer. 

You grab [Companion Name] by the arm and drag her with you, knowing that if you opened your mouth you'd fail to produce anything other than screams.

You need to leave.

Arms of gray skin and bone reach out to grab you from the corridor walls. You and [Companion Name] run through the fetid halls along the only path laid out for you. There's nothing else you can do. Each step becomes heavier and heavier as the bone beneath you turns spongy and slick with blood that pours from the ceiling and walls.

You lost track of time ages ago, and focus on your breathing. In. Out. In. Out. You reach out to steady [Companion Name]. Flinch back as she cuts a hand away from your throat.

The tunnel grows more narrow, and all the while, the beast crawls towards you faster and faster. Its breath curls down your back as you sprint through the halls, the feeling reminds you of how you the purple vial touching your lips and bringing you to this nightmare. You feel the beast's nails bite into your skin. Just a glancing blow, but you know the next time it touches you, it will be fatal.

You see light up ahead. You jump off the bridge.

And then... it ends.

You reach a large room made of the same stone as the tower that brought you here. Your lungs burn and tears stream down your face. [Companion Name] lands beside you with a thud.

You look back, and the tunnel you came from isn't there.

Maybe it never was.

You turn back and see Talm, arm in arm with his wife Era. The two of them look at you with so much hatred that you almost feel like you deserve it, though you haven't the slightest idea on why. Their fingers elongate into claws that scrape against the stone floor, while their bodies twist into malformed ideas of human anatomy.
This is where my people went, all those years ago!
This is the culmination of everything they worked towards.

You pull [Companion Name] to her feet. She is breathless, but her body moves on instinct as Era swipes towards her. You hear a clash of metal and hope it was enough. 

You barely have time to defend yourself as Talm's full weight slams into you, sending the two of you careening towards the edge of the stone platform. You now see that you stand on disk, and that over the edges of the platform lead to... nothing.

You turn back towards Talm, ready to face him... it... head on.

Talm's broken body lays before you. You hold your weapon in front of you, knowing that the moment you look away, it'll lunge for you, looking to take advantage of your weakness. Your breaths come in ragged heaves. The chance that you'd even be able to fend off a casual swat of Talm's claws is bordering on zero, but you stand at the ready regardless. You lost track of [Companion Name] ages ago, and can only hope that she was able to hold Era off.

You stare at the corpse as long as you can, your whole body threatening to collapse. You risk a blink of your eyes... and he's gone. Replaced by the Talm you know. Mostly.

The man before you wears a bright white crown of bone, and regal garb made of blackened leather. You can tell that it's... alive. But life may be be a stretch for the sorrowful creature wrapped around his body. He lets gives you a slow clap, before turning to Era, who dons similar 'clothes'. He whispers something you cannot hear to her, and she smiles slightly.

You take a step back, consciousness fading. Your weapon wavers, but does not fall.

The platform beneath you shifts and begins to descend into darkness.
What Comes After - After surviving Talm's initial onslaught, what will become of you next?

The chamber's walls shift as the platform you stand upon descends. Talm's regal form slowly begins to bleed into the darkness as the ground shifts beneath you, descending lower and lower. You try to keep your eyes trained on him, but without moving he fades from your vision. Fatigue sets in as your tense body begins to give out without a target in front of you.

As the gloom begins to swallow you, you feel... warm. At peace. Mentally, you lash out, knowing that something is wrong, but you've pushed yourself beyond your limits. Your weapon slips from your grasp as you collapse sideways. You don't even feel the cold stone floor as you fall. Only warmth.

You dream.

You wear dark grey robe made of a material that dances and swirls chaotically whenever you take your eyes off of it. You stand amidst an endless sea of bodies. Your chest wracks with silent sobs as you gaze upon them, not at all comforted by their peaceful smiles. As you walk amongst them, you make it to your king and lift the pearly white bone crown from his cold brow.

The weight it holds is incomparable to that which still rests on your shoulders. There's still so much work to do.

You awaken with a start and find yourself warm... but not cloying so. You're wrapped in devilishly silken sheets and buried in a bed so plush you fear your worn body won't be able to rise. Era stands far on the opposite corner of the room, stoking a fireplace of smooth, black stone.

You try to move, but every inch of your body screams in protest, and your groan catches her attention. She looks at you with... what'd seem to be genuine concern had she and her husband not just tried to kill you. You involuntarily shudder as she drops her bundle of wood and rushes to your side. She tries to begin speaking several times, before sighing and offering a small chuckle.
Hello darling... How do you feel?
...what do you want? Why am I here? Is...
Yes. She's alright. Recovering, like you, though she got it a bit rougher than you did.

Talm and I will explain in more detail as we can, but I know you must have several thousand questions, my child. I will do my best to answer them, but you'll come to learn more in time. Even here, there are laws that dictate against what I can and cannot speak.
Welcome to Respite. We're within the domain of the Lifebinders, a... world between worlds, so-to-speak. It was created as a safe haven during the calamity that brought Talm and I together.
I presume you found the entrance from your pilfered book, yes? The book came from here, and was written for Lifebinder children to act as a source of comfort while the world fell apart around them.
How could that book, or this place, bring anyone comfort?
What you've seen of Respite was it's entrance. The beast at the front, its guardian. There are many that would have wished to see Respite burn.

The chamber's walls shift as the platform you stand upon descends. Talm's regal form slowly begins to bleed into the darkness as the ground shifts beneath you, descending lower and lower. You try to keep your eyes trained on him, but without moving he fades from your vision. Fatigue sets in as your tense body begins to give out without a target in front of you.

As the gloom begins to swallow you, you feel... warm. At peace. Mentally, you lash out, knowing that something is wrong, but you've pushed yourself beyond your limits. Your weapon slips from your grasp as you collapse sideways. You don't even feel the cold stone floor as you fall. Only warmth.

You dream.

You wear dark grey robe made of a material that dances and swirls chaotically whenever you take your eyes off of it. You stand amidst an endless sea of bodies. Your chest wracks with silent sobs as you gaze upon them, not at all comforted by their peaceful smiles. As you walk amongst them, you make it to your king and lift the pearly white bone crown from his cold brow.

The weight it holds is incomparable to that which still rests on your shoulders. There's still so much work to do.

You awaken with a start and find yourself warm... but not cloying so. You're wrapped in devilishly silken sheets and buried in a bed so plush you fear your worn body won't be able to rise. Era stands far on the opposite corner of the room, stoking a fireplace of smooth, black stone.

You try to move, but every inch of your body screams in protest. You try not to make a sound, but your involuntary groan catches her attention. She looks at you with... what'd seem to be genuine concern had she and her husband not just tried to kill you. You involuntarily shudder as she drops her bundle of wood and rushes to your side. She tries to begin speaking several times, before sighing and offering a small chuckle.
Given [Companion Name] and I's reception, I see that peaceful nature has died out.
I won't ask for either of you to forgiven Talm and I's transgressions against you, only explain why we chose this path.

My people sought to ascertain the fates through communion with the stars, as you've gathered by now. Our use of summoning itself was rather limited, and focused on the practical, usually creating messengers to help us made sense of the fates.
We were called the Fateseekers, and we learned of the calamity far before it ever was set into motion.
You'll hear more of this calamity as you rest here, I promise you that.
Nevertheless. The Fateseekers' visions all culminated in one final premonition of the future.
A creature so vile, born of a nation of sacrificed life. As it let out its first breath, the world in its entirety twisted and died.
My people's visions can be esoteric at times, but this was seen with perfect clarity across my entire clan.
This is what the calamity would culminate in.
But this 'calamity' you cannot speak of happened already, no? That's why there aren't many summoners left, outside of the Soulsmiths.
Unless the world underwent some kind of rebirth afterward, assuming your clan was even correct in the first place, what does this have to do with why you attacked us?
...My people were correct. The only thing we were unsure of was the timeframe.
This creature... It is what the Soulsmiths seek to bring about.
Before you can understand, you must learn this history of Respite.

But I've already kept you so long, I thank you for your patience. I'll explain more to you, in time, but please, acquaint yourself with this place first. Leave if you must, just come and find me. You may always return later.

Era rises from the bedside and offers a small curtsy. Your next question is answered before it even leaves your mouth. [Companion Name] is in the next room over, but hasn't yet awakened.

You follow Era out, who wanders off down the hall. You knock on [Companion Name]'s door before letting yourself in. Like you were, she rests in a large bed and is seemingly unharmed, but you see that she's restless, perhaps having strange dreams like yours before you awoke.

You go to her and speak her name softly, and hold her hand. You feel the first bit of relief you have since you woke, Era's earlier words having more of the opposite effect on you.

You stay for a long while, before heading to the window and pulling open the curtain. You weren't sure what you'd find, but you weren't expecting... endless rows of white lily-like flowers amidst a field of grey grass that stretch out further than you can see. In their own small clusters are other flowers, almost always another distinct color. You see blues, greens, browns, and occasional bright reds as well. They all seem pristine, and the field of dark grass is free from any other growth.

As you look at the sky, the dark purple sky feels alien to you, the stars burn a deep, lush green, their patterns completely unfamiliar to you.
Bring me back to what you wish to show me. (Divination)
I just... hope I can understand it. (Divination)

As you practice the divination methods Era taught you back in her tower, the green stars push themselves into your mind. Unlike your out-of-body experience then, you find yourself... back in your earlier dream. The bone crown feels more comfortable on your head now, and you feel more... at peace.

You walk amongst the bodies and realize that they aren't corpses. Yet. They lay somewhere between life and death, much like the plane you currently reside.

This was the dream your people, the Lifebinders, chose for themselves. To fall into an endless, beautiful dream, far removed from the horrors the world faces.

Alongside your people are others, from more clans. Respite was open to all who chose it.

You want so desperately to lay down and join them in the grass, but... you know you can't. The ritual isn't complete, and you're the only one who can see it to its end.

You'll pulled out of the dream as you feel a hand on your real shoulder. [Companion Name] looks at you with concern.
[Player Name]? Oh... I'm so happy to see you.
Are you okay? Why are you crying?
I... I don't know. But I'm so glad that you're okay.
She clearly didn't do a good enough job, though, since I'm still... here. Wherever here is.
Back in that dark chamber, after that flesh monster?
Yeah. She ran her claws through my chest. But uh... I don't seem to have so much as a scratch on me.
We saw Talm bring Era back from the dead, or close to it. Maybe they did the same for you?
I passed out shortly after fighting Talm off.
So, you beat your opponent, huh? You're gonna make me look bad.
...You know, for a dead woman, you seem to be taking things in stride.
Well, I feel like I've gotten the best sleep I've had in months, and you're here, so... I figure we're somewhat safe.
But I do hope you'll fill me in on how exactly we got here.

You wipe your face and join [Companion Name] on the bed, and do your best to fill her in on everything you know. She nods along, and asks dozens of questions that you don't have the answers to. Yet, you hope to yourself.

You talk about your dreams, and [Companion Name] speaks of hers. She has seen flashes of time, all over the world in lands neither of you can even begin to guess the location of. In each, clans of summoners from endless walks of life all fighting to survive against... each other.

[Companion Name] describes battle after battle. Some with large armies of man and beast, others... darkly similar to the attack on Azamire, but with creatures far different to those of the Soulsmiths'.

When she finishes, she mentions how it feels like she's been stopped mid-sentence, and needs to know how the stories end. She figures that if you continued to dream while looking at the stars outside, she plans to do the same soon.

You both return to the window and find that the sky has shifted from purple to a hazy pink, with the stars taking on a lighter hue. Whether it's due to the passage of time or what, you cannot begin to tell, but as you gaze at them together, you feel the same draw as before.

After a long while, you're able to urge yourself back into your dream, but find yourself in a distant land, completely unfamiliar to you. 

You clutch a wooden railing tight enough to splinter the wood as you look out over the city in front of you.

Brightly painted wooden structures fly high above a jungle canopy, suspended in the air as if held on strings tied to passing clouds. People float to-and-fro, passing between buildings calmly, living their lives blissfully untouched by the battles their people raged against your own halfway across the world. You're the last of the Lifebinders, all others now peacefully awaiting you to deliver to them the paradise they were promised. An endless dream where they'll never again be subject to the ongoing horrors of the world.

As you withdraw the black gemstone from your cloak, you know you're dooming these people. It doesn't stop you. With shaking hands, you piece the stone with a blackened dagger made exclusively for this day. Dark mist begins to leak from the stone, curling around your hands and forming a thick cloud in front of you. It's not enough for you to release it.

The hungry beast needs guidance. Direction.

You will it forward.
The Price of Paradise - Little by little, Respite has begun to show you what it took to build, yet, you've only scratched the surface of what summoning has wrought upon the land.

You feel... wrong. The body you inhabited was doubtlessly Talm's, though untold centuries past. What... how could someone be so driven to do something they know is so horrifically wrong. You felt his very being recoil as he carved into the gemstone, but... it didn't stop him.

You need to know.

You leave the room and [Companion Name] behind you, who still seems lost within her own mind.

The halls are lined with endless murals and depictions of the world, but you hardly see them as you're driven forward with righteous purpose. You find yourself outside. The monster you seek sits far out in the field of grey grass, in front of a set of two white flowers.

The path through the grass is well-worn, seemingly travelled countless times.
I'm afraid you'll need to be a bit more specific than that.
The floating city. The gemstone. I saw it.
Ah. And here I thought you'd be a bit more interested in why I tried to kill you.
I can't even recall the name of the city anymore.
Amongst the dozens of clans my people fought, none were more... through in their eradication on the Lifebinders.
You've seen what I've done for Era, back in the tower. My people were exceptional healers.
Lifebinders focused more on the body than the Soulsmiths, who focus more on the... Well. You can puzzle that one out.
But our control of one's spirit was quite impressive as well. These skills made us incredibly sought after allies in the calamity.
Better yet. How about you ask my people yourself?
After all this time, I'm sure they're quite tired of having me as their sole point of contact with the outside world.
You want to learn, don't you?
I'll tell you whatever you want to know after you speak to the Dreamers.
I don't want to do this, but I doubt you'll listen to me otherwise...

All thoughts of resistance vanish as you find yourself dropping to your knees against your will after Talm snaps his fingers, the muscles in your legs giving out completely. Talm slowly cups one of the white flowers in front of him and plucks several petals from it with a mix of reverence and practiced effort, as though he's done it a million times before. He waves you off, telling you to go gather as many as wish. Just as you consider telling him to do it himself, he sighs, saying that it's 'for your own good'.
The Dreamers... what can they teach me?

You thought multiple times about ripping the flowers from the ground as you delicately plucked a few petals from each, but felt like you'd look more like a rebelling child than properly offering any form of legitimate resistance. You move throughout the fields efficiently, taking care not to step on any of the flowers, and return once you've gathered a sizeable number of petals.
There. What do you want these for?
I told you. To speak with the Dreamers.
Take my hand, I'll show you.

Talm raises his hand once again, preparing to snap, but you begrudgingly sigh and take the man's hand. He slowly walks you through the process of... bringing Dreamers forth from the petals. Talm does so in seconds, and a pale, wispy silhouette of a young girl dances forth from one of the petals he took from you. She greets Talm warmly, asking how long it's been for him since the last she awoke. The two go back and forth for a time until the girl notices you, and she excitedly runs through more questions than you can possibly keep up with, all before you even get your name out.

Talm calms her, saying that you're there to learn about the Dreamers, and to tell the others within the Dream to prepare themselves. Her silhouette dissipates a second later.

The man walks you through the process, and you find it very similar to summoning creatures, but a lot harder than anything you've done before. Talm's effortless display earlier clearly came from an untold amount of practice.

The last petal withers away in your hand, the last Dreamer you spoke with having left to go check on her child somewhere deep within the Dream. You feel... exhausted. You're unsure of just how long passed, as time within Respite doesn't seem to move like it does in the real world. You feel no hunger, no fatigue, but time does seem to pass. At the very least, the sky changes colors, though not in any pattern you were able to notice. It could have been hours, or it could have been months since you started talking to the Dreamers, you simply don't know or have any way of telling.

The Dreamers you spoke with all shared the same initial excitement the first girl had at seeing a stranger, and countless questions about what the world was like. Like Talm had said, it'd seem that he's the only one they've talked to outside of the dream since they first entered. [Companion Name] eventually came out to join some of the conversations, and then once she was shown the process, have her own. Not everyone was from the Lifebinders... dozens of names were given, all in-line with some different discipline or school of thought, all joined the Lifebinders here in Respite to escape.

They told you what Era and Talm couldn't. What they lived through.

The Titan Wars.

That was the calamity they spoke of.

Titans were beasts that dwarved even the Ivory Athenaeum by several magnitudes of size. What the Dreamers described sounded more like forces of nature or vengeful Gods rather than anything a group of people could bring forth. When the Titans of two rival summoning clans fought, it was heard across the continent. Mountains were crushed to dust, a quarter of the mainland was buried under water, lakes of fire rose from the ground and killed thousands... 

Clans that did not raise their own Titan for protection were quickly destroyed by those that did. Each clan saw one another as a threat that could generate a world-changing force, and the only way to stay alive was to have your own and use it against the others, or create a plane of existence like Respite and lose the metaphorical key.

Talm approaches quietly as the last Dreamer fades away.
I... I don't know what to say.
Assuming this isn't all one horrid trick... that each of these people truly are... somewhere... in this Dream.
The calamity was so horrid, and the dangers of the outside world so prevalent, my people decided to never face it again.
No living summoner from my time can speak of it, but you know what we faced. We couldn't compete. We wouldn't have wanted to even if we could.
And so, the Dream was born.
The book from the Archive is a history book. How Respite came to be and... the Dream we were building towards.
A world without war. Without death. Without wondering if we'd make it through the next year. That book let kids hold onto hope for a better future.
The city you attacked... they had people that wished for the same, I'm sure.
I know that. Do you think for a moment that I don't know that?
There's never a night where my actions don't haunt me.
Then how could you do it?
I needed a source of power to enact the ritual that let my people enter the Dream.
Other clans got their power in other ways, but it always came from somewhere.
