A forest clan, the Vieshar, when they brought forth their... you know.
The energy it required caused all of the plant-life across half the continent to wither and die. Millions starved when their plants couldn't grow as the ground was fallow for a decade.
My people gave so much to create Respite, but it wasn't enough. There's a reason we have that beast at the front. We were still pursued by those who sought our power.
We tried so hard to be left in peace. My people needed a place where they could never be hurt again.
...I killed thousands all those years ago. I will never not feel the weight of what I did.
But now, my people, my kids, are safe. So are thousands of others. Each and every single one of these flowers was a person saved through what I did that day.
...I don't expect you to understand. But I do want you to know that what I did was hardly even a footnote in history.
Why did you and Era bring us here, Talm?
Go ask Era yourselves. She'll be waiting where you entered. There's nothing more for us to show you.
I mean this sincerely, good luck.

Talm takes a shaky breath and waves you and [Companion Name] off, looking back down at the two flowers you first saw him tending to. The two of you look to each other, not even knowing where to begin with everything dropped on you. [Companion Name] brings you to a tower that stretches endlessly into the sky, and once you enter, you realize the circular platform was the one you fought Era and Talm on.

After a ride to the top, the horrid, fleshy hallway you were chased in stretches out in front of you. Only one way out, it'd seem.
That's the best I've felt in a while.

The fetid hallway offers more resistance than it did before. Arms of twisted, mottled flesh grasp at the pair of you as you run by, narrow passages threaten to crush you as you pass. No beast chases you this time, but the urgency you feel to leave is no lesser for it.

True to Talm's word, Era waits for you by the exit with a sad smile.
I saw that you two and Talm talked...
I trust that you're ready to leave?
Yes. We learned of... The Titan Wars, and bringing forth the Dreamers was... enlightening when it came to practicing Summoning.
Though I don't know if I want anything to do with it after... all of this.
Running from your pet was great for cardio, and when you ran me through with your claws, I learned an important lesson about never trusting summoners again.
What we don't get is... why. Why all of this? If you fought so hard to bring us here, why are you just... letting us go?
I've seen what you two must face as you continue to face off against the Soulsmiths.
What was... described to you by the Dreamers is nothing compared to what the Fateseekers saw all those years ago, at the end of the calamity.
Going off of what Talm was saying...
Bringing forth a Titan comes at an enormous cost to the world, but it wouldn't outright end it.
This is true... if the Soulsmiths intended to stop there.
They will go further than any clan of my time ever could, as there are none who can keep them in check.
The calamity my people lived through shaped the world into what it is today. Despite the devastation, there was a delicate balance between the clans.
Each had clan a... the same level of power. After decades of war, the world was nearly uninhabitable.
To prevent their own extinction, those that remained released their...
Yes. Back to the world. Plants grew again. The winds blew through the trees. Rain fell anew. The world began to heal with its natural power restored.
...But what does this have to do with us?

[Companion Name] and I... We came to the capitol chasing after ghosts, wanting to know why our home was burnt to the ground by the Soulsmiths. To make them pay, and return our people if they still lived.
Why did you and Talm test us? To what end?
Your people will be used as fuel for the Soulsmith's beast. Like thousands... no... millions, of others will be.
The two of you are the first new summoners to learn the art within centuries, outside of the Soulsmiths themselves.
How and why could we ever hope to stop them? Why does this fall on us, and not you and Talm?
Talm and I have been around for centuries, child.
In the few years the two of you have existed on this world in comparison, you've already long-since exceeded our potential.
I will never expect you to understand or forgive our appearent betrayal, but I promise you...
This was the fastest, most effective way we could see to help you continue to surpass us.
I wish with all my heart that this was not your burden to bare.
But the world is unkind to us all, some more than others.
...What if we just... stopped? What then? Went back to Azamire, settled down, and never thought about any of this ever again?
Could you, knowing that there's even a sliver of a chance I'm correct?
...Where would we even begin, without you and Talm?
Far to the west are the Perilous Peaks, as I'm sure you know. Deep within, the Nalidasi Dwarves maintain archives that far predate even the oldest human civilizations.
For what it's worth, I'm sorry that this what Talm and I could offer you. I wish we had more time to do this the right way.

[Companion Name] seems like she may have more to say, but turns a second later and reaches upward. The moment her hand touches the still, reflected pool of water that brought you into Respite, she bolts upward and out of the plane. You look to Era for only a moment before following after her.

The trek back to the mainland is much calmer than the one here, especially now with experience. You and [Companion Name] hardly share a word the entire trip back.

You sail further south than Tidebreak, heading back towards the capitol, unsure of what to do or where to go. Both of you go through the motions as you arrive at port, register your vessel, and pay for it to remain docked for some time. Checking with locals and accounting for travel to and from Gloomstone, it'd seem you were only in Respite for an hour, but you know it was much longer than that, and you guess that time moves differently there.

You wander the streets for a while before [Companion Name] suggests a nearby tavern. The two of you share a room, feeling a bit too unsteady to be apart for now. You don't even know where to begin, and your best friend seems to feel similarly, until she tosses your weapon to you. She's determined not to let anyone get the best of her again, and wants to spar. You smile for the first time in a while.

Your time in Respite left you shaken and unsure of yourself. You definitely grew in the untold amount of time you stayed there, but if you were to follow the path laid out for you, is there any amount of growth that'd prepare you for what's to come? These thoughts come and go as you clash with [Companion Name]. As the two of you duel into the night, doubtlessly disturbing the other guests, you slowly let your time in Respite wash away from your mind.

Whatever tomorrow brings will be tomorrow's problem. For now, [Companion Name] is safe, alive, and so are you.

And for now, that's enough.

Path to the Peaks - The next leg of your journey has been laid out before you. The Perilous Peaks lay far to the north, the surrounding lands mostly untouched by civilization, but with no better leads, it remains your best path forward.
I've got first watch, I suppose.

Stocked up on provisions and as mentally prepared as you can be, you and [Companion Name], set off, leaving the capitol far behind. Things remain in this strange state of... flux, where the both of you try your best to pretend the weight of everything that happened in Respite hasn't been weighing on your shoulders.

As you sit by this night's campfire, several days into your journey now, [Companion Name] drives her hatchet into a log she was splitting for kindling and turns to face you.
I don't mind splitting the wood tonight, just give me a sec-
You know that's not what I mean.
This whole... funk. It's like we both died a little in Respite and have been little walking corpses ever since.
I haven't been me, and you... haven't been you.
I don't know... how we're meant to act, now.
I feel so deep in over my head. We came out here to find a couple people from Azamire and now we're...
What, heading to the home of the Dwarves to learn about Summoning? To what end?
I always knew that you'd leave Azamire and do something great, but me?
You've gone through everything I have, and I'd argue more.
I have no idea if what Era says is true. I truly hope it isn't.
But... Despite how stupid their little test was, and how much I wish they would have just been honest from the get go...
Era is right, at least about needing to help. I've seen too much to just... go back home.
I mean, how could we? I feel that our days back in Azamire, even before the attack, are so far behind us.
I just... don't know where we belong anymore.
Believe me, I'm in the same boat...
I don't want to lose ourselves while we figure out where that is.

You leave it there as [Companion Name] sits beside you on your log-turned-seat and rests her head on your shoulder. You feel... lighter, and only hope that you find your place in all this mess. You shift a bit, getting ready to stand before you hear [Companion Name] start to snore.
It looks like a whole pack has come out to greet us.
We're gonna have to move camp.

Your mind wasn't playing tricks on you. The small snap of a branch here, something disturbing the underbrush there. It's always difficult to differentiate between the general comings and goings of creatures in the night, and when something is actively stalking you.

Unfortunately, this is the later. You bolt upright and draw your weapon, waking [Companion Name] in the process as a particularly large Rockwolf charges right for you.
Dinner came to us tonight, it looks like.

Seeing you prepared for it, the beast diverts its charge and instead runs past you, and darting back into the woods, outside of the light of your campfire.

Just outside of the clearing you can see the firelight reflect off of eyes. Lots of eyes.
This is some of the toughest meat I've worked with...
This smells and looks way better than expected.

Huffing and puffing the cool night air, you hold your weapon aloft, challenging more of the beasts to come out. Far fewer of the pack remain, and those that do decide that they've bitten off more than they can chew once the biggest of them lies dead at your feet and dart off into the trees, but not before one grabs your pack of provisions out of the tree it was hung up in. No one had said anything about wolves about the size of horses, so you didn't think to hang your food that high.
You know how I always told you I wanted a dog?
I might get a cat instead.
Don't bring that evil on us, I know there's some scary kitties up in the Peaks.
Knowing our luck, we'd wake up with one nibbling one of our arms.
Wolves took our food, didn't they?
If they just wanted that, they could have grabbed it and been gone without trying to go for our throats.
I think they just took it as a consolation prize.
They'll need some consoling after eating it. Hardtack and some... absolutely foul pemmican isn't exactly the height of camping food.
Well, we do still have to eat something. Nothing stopping us from having them, right?
Gotta do something with the bodies.
I've never had wolf before, but they have to be stringy right?
And I don't know how keen I am on eating something that has maybe eaten a person before.
It's a rare day someone comes this far north, I'd say the odds they've eaten someone are low.
...Dunno. Something I heard people in the capitol saying.
You get some rest, I'll work on getting all these bodies prepared.
Surely nothing will get attracted by all the corpses.
I'll feed you to them first, if you just jinxed us.
I will never expect you to understand or forgive our apparent betrayal, but I promise you...
It's almost like they don't want people coming up here!
Surely they'll be glad to see us.

The magic-enhanced tools you picked up back in the capitol help you make quick work of the pile, at least compared to what it'd usually take you. [Companion Name] takes the freshly cooked steaks as you finish with them and gives them a bit of extra love and seasoning once you're done. With fresh food and better spirits, you pack up camp and head further towards the peaks.

The two of you nibble smoked strips of rockwolf as you walk. It's very crunchy.
I think every meal is made a little better if it tried to eat you first.
I mean, really, it's only fair when you think about it. Spite tastes good.
Though, these herbs you found definitely help.
The forest provides. Makes me wonder what other kinds of creatures taste like.
I really liked that Stonehopper back in the Broken Pass, too.
Well, both these and the wolves are pretty much just bigger, scarier versions of creatures we already know.
I didn't expect to like the wolf this much, but what about some weird stuff?
Ooo, that's interesting. Maybe they'd be like some kind of... gelatin?
If we run out of food, maybe we go check out a dungeon and see what kind of creatures we can find?
Might be delicious, might poison us and we die horribly.

As you travel onward, the dense forest gives way to rocky slopes. Little by little you find yourselves walking less and scrambling more, until the journey has turned into an outright climb. The entrance to the Dwarves' home is not one they wanted visitors to get to easily, it'd seem.

You and [Companion Name] take turns lugging your gear up the mountainside. You're sure you were told the entrance to the dwarven capitol was somewhere around here, but "lower eastern side of those mountains over there" weren't exactly prime directions from a group of what seemed to be well-meaning schoolkids. They said the entrance was hidden, and that those seeking the dwarves would likely have to climb for days or weeks, to find the entrance. Nevertheless, blissfully far from the peak but still not easy to access, a large gate carved into the stone stands before you, presumably leading deeper into the mountain. On a low wall flanking either side of the gate, a squat dwarf with a short-trimmed blond beard naps soundly, resting his chin on the pommel of his large maul in what appears to be a heavily practiced position.

You clear your throat a couple of times, trying to get his attention, but to no avail. So, you walk up and his helmet with your knuckle, just barely able to reach him atop the wall. He wakes with a shout, wide-eyed and startled by your presence, so much so that he careens backward off the wall. You quickly scramble after him and find the dwarf unconscious - but breathing - on the other side.

You don't know how you're going to explain this to the rest of the dwarves.
Dwarf Blood - With the sole Nalidasi guard unconscious at your feet and a gate blocking your path, you're going to have some explaining to do.
Ah! A push door! Oh... wait, no.
You quickly look around as [Companion Name] scrambles up the low wall after you. She lightly thumps your back once she stands beside you, then bends down to check the dwarf.
They should consider making you an ambassador, truly remarkable work [Player Name].
He was sleeping, I just wanted to wake him up!
Just giving you a hard time.
Unfortunately - intentions aside - it looks like you've had a bit of the opposite effect.
I guess we'll have to let ourselves in, and then find some way of explaining... this.

You look over the gate and wall and just barely spot it. A small stone hatch, likely more typically used as an entrance so they don't have to open and close the main gate all the time. Though, with a path like the one you travelled, it's a wonder they made such a gate in the first place.

As expected the hatch is shut and locked, with no apparent keyhole or method of opening. You get to work trying to open it regardless while [Companion Name] wraps the dwarf's head.
Let's see what this dwarf has got!

You try half a dozen methods of opening the hatch until you realize that it's magically imbued. While there are methods for figuring out the words for opening magic locks, you hardly feel you have the time to do so. Eventually you give up on any gentle method of opening and just jam your tools through the side and start to pry while saying every version of 'open' you can think of.

Eventually, it gives way, and you're not sure about what worked specifically, but it hardly matters. You peer down the hatch to find a squat tunnel. You grab the unconscious dwarf and throw him over your shoulder, then head down the tunnel with [Companion] just behind you.

Eventually the tunnel opens up into a small chamber with two dwarves cheerfully playing some form of dice game. The two look at you with shock, the shorter of the two runs for the door leading out and latches it - keeping you from progressing further - while the one who is more stout hefts a large blade in your direction and frowns.
Oi! What are you doin' with Humphrey?
Attackers! Thought you'd pull a fast one on us, eh?
No, no! Easy now, I'm not here to hurt anyone.
Little late for that, don't ya think?
Your friend was so startled by seeing two humans pop up over the cliff that he fell off the wall he was sitting on.
Yeah, that sounds like our Humphrey. Thanks for haulin' him down here
Suppose so. I'm Tee, human. Short one over there is Pout.
It's a pleasure, sorry we gave you and your friend quite the start.
Meh, it's good to get the heart racing every once in a while.
Gotta ask ya though, why'd you come up through our expedition entrance?
Oh yeah, just another stone's throw north. Got it all freshly paved n' everything.
It's real nice, you shoulda gone there. We don't get visitors often, especially not humans.
This one is for our... well, don't know if we can share that. But suffice to say, it's mainly an exit.
Honestly surprised you even found it, let alone climbed up here!
We'll buy ya a drink later if we see ya, wanna hear about that climb!
I'm going to find those kids when we get back to the capitol.
Well! It's a pleasure to meet you both. Shall we leave Humphry with you, then?
...Well, we'll bring ya to the capitol, but we need to go ask around first. I think the two of you are the first human visitors we've had in a few years at least!

Tee nods at the statement and unlatches the door and heads out to whether it may lead. Pout fishes around in a pouch on his waist and withdraws a flask and wafts it under Humphrey's nose, who groggily comes to. He takes the flask and takes a sip, instantly regaining his ruddy complexion. As he looks around in a daze, he blushes, embarrassed by the whole endeavor.

As the four of you wait, Humphrey asks if you'd give him a chance to regain a bit of his pride with a little bout.
Don't have much of a choice now, do we?

Every time you knock the dwarf down, he sips a bit from the flask again and gets right back up, ready to go again. He's a good fighter, and though you are better, it feels like you are fighting a small platoon one-by-one. [Companion Name] steps in a few times as well, either looking to give you a break or flex her own skills.

Despite the fact that the chamber is well-lit and Pout dragged all the furniture out of the way, the low ceilings make for a cramped fighting place for the two of you, and you have to spend a lot of mental energy to not bash your head or weapons on the ceiling while dodging the dwarf's blows.

Eventually Tee re-enters the room with another dwarf alongside him. The newcomer has a bushy white beard that nearly trails down to the floor, and sits atop a floating disk of metal, lit by intricate patterns of runes and glowing engravings all throughout its surface. You hardly have the time to inspect it before the newcomer clears his throat.
*Ahem*. Greetings, tall-folk. I am the grand Archivist and royal advisor to the king.
I bring tidings from our 37th ruler, Oyadazminis, who welcomes you into our home to look upon our works, cherish our history, and hopefully... and I quote, "drink until you hit the floor."
If you have any other desires or aspirations while visiting Koganusan, they may be granted, should we deem you worthy of such requests.
This may be too lofty of an ask - please forgive our trespasses if so - but we hear the Nalidasi Archives are quite the sight to behold.
...is that so? I can count the number of times a human has been allowed into our archives on one hand since Koganusan was just a hole in the dirt.
So, forgive me if I think you're full of silt.
...They've almost doubtlessly changed their names through the years, but do Era and Talm ring a bell?

As the word starts to leave your mouth, the Archivist's eyes go wide and he snaps his fingers, and you find the words silent as they leave your mouth. He chuckles and bids the guards farewell, then snaps again. You find yourselves in front of a grand throne that's equal parts imposing and gaudy. In it sits a dwarf you'd guess is middle aged, with a dark beard studded with gemstones and clasps of metal, similar to the crown atop his head.

You've been brought into what would seem to be a lavish banquet as table after table of divine looking food and immaculately dressed dwarves fill the throne room.

The guests look at your studden entrance with curiosity and excitement, which you consider to be better than suspicion and fear. The Archivist floats up to the king and whispers in his ear, and his eyes go from interest, to shock, and then... excitement. He claps his hands once and hands before the room, then announces to everyone that the entertainment has arrived.

The two of you are ushered into the center of the room, then, one by one, several of the more rugged nobles in the room, along with their guards, encircle you.

The king announces that you're not to be killed, only to be given a proper welcome to the kingdom, whatever that may mean. You don't know if it particularly matters based on how quickly you're swarmed by the nobles and their guards.

As you beat down the guards and nobles who look at you expectantly, you wouldn't have guessed the king himself would have risen to join in on the fun, but through no small deal of effort, he fell like the rest of his people. You tried your best to not kill the man, but with how hard he hit the ground, you wonder if you overdid it.

You clutch your weapon, covered in more blood than you ever would have expected for a 'friendly' bout. With the Nalidaian king at your feet, you eye the Archivist, worried that despite the promise of this just being for 'entertainment,' you'd find yourself at the hands of a much more upset populace. Instead, he shrugs towards you and gives a small nod.

Oyadazminis groans and pushes himself up, he beams with a giant smile, several of his missing teeth having been replaced by intricately carved gemstones. If this is 'entertainment' to these dwarves, you're surprised he's not missing more.

He waves to the nobles and grabs you and [Companion Name] by your shoulders, dragging you off behind the throne room to an lavishly decorated room, with the Archivist following closely behind. The floating man waves his hand over the door, causing the entrance to vanish entirely under a waterfall of blue sparks.
Haven't had a proper bout like that in half a dozen years!
Don't get visitors with as much fire n' 'em as the both of you everyday. Thanks for indulging my people, they'll like you a lot more for that.
It didn't seem that any of you were particularly keen on letting us not participate.
You could have gone crying to your mothers at any moment, but you would have been laughed out of the courtroom.
The Archivist told me what you seek. At least, part of it.
If I were to let anyone into the Archives, they'd have to work their stones off for half a human lifetime to even glimpse the outermost door.
I don't imagine the two of you have the time for such things, if you're telling the truth about our... mutual acquaintances.
I don't know if I'd call them that at this point...
But the two of you are familiar with Talm and Era, then?
Aye. They translated half the... special materials we've got in the Archives long ago.
Decided that as payment, they'd take the other half. So many years of history lost...
Under normal circumstances I'd agree, but if those books had anything to do with the nastiness that tall fella could do...
We got rather well acquainted with it ourselves.
Why we need to get into the Archives is a long story, but... it was under their recommendation.
I believe that, which is the only reason I didn't toss you out the second it was mentioned.
That whole art... It's dangerous. Most everyone at my level of station across the continent is at least loosely aware of Summoning.
Mostly because each nation has their own collection of histories and magic under lock and key. Too treacherous to share. Using it is out of the question.
To be honest, your arrival and need for said materials has us more... concerned more than anything.
Talm and Era are two of the most trusted individuals to the kingdom, but we cannot simply give the materials to you.
Aye. We trust their judgement, but both protocol and public perception hold a lot of sway here.
Can we do anything else that doesn't involve public beatdowns or ballroom brawls to earn our way in, then?
Yes, and it'll be your great pleasure to do so. My lovely daughter will be your ward. You couldn't find yourself in better hands if you tried.

As Oyadazminis finishes, there's a shimmer in the corner of the room. A young red haired dwarf steps out from seemingly thin air, a cloak of woven blue metal thread billowing out around her. She introduces herself as Redilok and gives a small curtsy and mentions she enjoyed watching you give her father quite the wallop out in the ballroom. The king turns about as red as his daughter's hair and shakes his head before motioning for the Archivist to rematerialize the door, then the two of them depart.

The princess opens a new door in a different section of wall and motions for the two of you to follow. You pass through the doorway and find yourselves on the balcony of a large tower connected to - what you presume is - the castle you were just in. The balcony overlooks the whole of Koganusan, the whole of the capitol fitting within an unbelievable hollow under the Perilous Peaks. You hardly have the time to take it in before the princess starts running through its extensive history, and that of their western neighbors, a smaller kingdom of dwarves who live under a large volcanic mountain range.

What she wants your assistance with is no small task. Connecting the two kingdoms via a magical transport line that allows a stone platform to accelerate to incredible speeds. The 'Stoneway' as she calls it is already well underway, but still needs an extraordinary amount of work. Before you're allowed to begin though, you must show her how you go about summoning creatures, purely to satisfy her curiosity. If she's to vouch for you, she wants to know just what secrets her father intends to give away to humans.

Since she was in the room when her father mentioned the closely guarded art of Summoning, you don't find any harm in indulging the princess's request. You and [Companion Name] show princess Redilok several of the creatures you've learned to create over your journey here, much to her pleasure. She takes several sketches of the beasts, and asks for you to make them perform... all manner of things, some practical, some a bit silly. She questions you on your journey here throughout the 'tests' as she calls them. You fill her in. The Soulsmiths, your travels. Talm and Era's trials. She listens without a single comment, enraptured by your tales.

After a long while and the summoning of several more creatures, Redilok closes her notepad and makes it vanish, much like the Archivist did with the door, earlier. She thanks you for your time and asks you to make yourself at home, and that she'll be in touch very soon regarding the Stoneway, then promptly slips off the balcony backward and disappears.

After confirming you didn't just witness the princess fall to her untimely death, you enter what seems to be 'your' room from the balcony and find a room that likely cost several thousand gold just to furnish, let alone build. A two plush four poster beds, a pool of steaming water kept warm by some arcane source you're unfamiliar with. Thick carpet, beautiful silken drapes, and various pieces of artwork depicting lands you've never seen nor heard of.

The sight is made a bit warmer by the fact that [Companion Name] has already launched herself at the nearest bed and started to snore before even making contact with the pillow, a sentiment you cannot help but share moments later.

Stoneway Yourway - After a warm welcome to the kingdom of the Nalidasi Dwarves, Princess Redilok is primed to accept your help in finishing the last of the Stoneway, which will earn your entry into the Royal Archives.
I've been working on the Stoneeeeway~
All the live long... is it daytime down here?

You wake to find breakfast floating towards you, with Princess Redilok floating just behind it. She pours over a large scroll, as your meal assembles itself on a silver tray inches above your lap. You feel horrendously underdressed and disheveled to be in the presence of royalty, but she hardly seems to notice. Her fault for coming unannounced. You still do your best to make yourself marginally more presentable, then lightly pick at the meal in front of you. You glance towards [Companion Name] who seems even more flustered by the princess's sudden arrival. You catch her eye and lightly wipe at the corner of your mouth, trying to get her to wipe the drool away. She hardly contains a groan before doing so as subtly as she can.

Once satisfied with whatever she was looking through, Redilok looks up to address you both, her smile as sweet as the flaky pastry you bite into.
Please, you two. If you couldn't tell by the way my father welcomed you to our home with a kerfuffle by all the top-brass in the kingdom, we do things a bit differently here.
Your human modesty and decorum will only get you funny looks here. Dig in!
Tsk tsk. What'd I just say?
None of that stuffy business. You need to eat up if you're going to help our Stoneway workers.
I'd like to ask... if you already have people working on this project, why would our aid be needed, exactly?
And not that we mind, but that's all it'll take to get us into the archives?
The tunnel to excavate the Stoneway met with a bit of a... snag. There was a cavern right near the middle of our kingdoms that seemed man or dwarfmade.
Not too uncommon considering the distance, but the cavern was guarded by beasts made of the same magic I had you show me earlier.
For such scary beasties, they didn't put up much of a fight and we finished excavating the route for the Stoneway. Not without some losses, though.
Seems a bit miraculous to stumble across a cavern filled with ancient beasts.
We're on the same page, then.
My father - bless the foolhardy man - is sure it was a trap set by the Flamberian Dwarves, despite the fact the Stoneway is meant to connect us.
You don't seem to share the sentiment though. You think it was someone else?
I do. There was a war between our kingdoms long before my father was even a pebble in his father's eye, but Dwarven grudges run deep.
Despite the years, our elders are worried something will go awry and are jumping at the chance to reignite the old war.
The tunnel to excavate the Stoneway met with a bit of a... snag. There was a cavern right near the middle of our kingdoms that seemed man or dwarf-made.
I've been working with their prince for half a decade on the Stoneway now, and he's an honest man. This wasn't them.
Maybe something else, then? You remember the Soulsmiths from our stories earlier?
I'd be surprised, but it's not as though there's other Summoning clans running amok nowadays, are there?
If there are, we haven't had the misfortune of meeting them. Can you think of any reason why they'd target your people?
No, I can't, and that's what worries me, and why I want the two of you there as we complete the Stoneway.
The rulers won't be there in person, but several high-ranking nobles - along with the Flamberian Prince and myself - will hold a small celebration in the center of the Stoneway as it's finished.
And we're to be there incase something happens with the Soulsmiths.

Redilok nods, then leaves to let the two of you eat and get prepared. When she returns, another magical doorway that she creates takes you to what she calls the Stoneway Station. Several deep set rails of metal stretch along the ground, far, far into a tunnel that stretches into the distance. The underground pathway is lit by blue-green balls of floating light spaced evenly apart, giving as much light as if the Stoneway was above ground instead of thousands of meters below it. 

Dozens of dwarves carry lengths of rails etched with glowing runes onto the stone platform hovering above the metal path. Making sure you're not in the way, you step upon the rectangular 'Slabglider' at Redilok's request. The Slabglider is the length of several carts stacked end-to-end, with comfy seating along its outer edge, with plenty of space for the rails and cargo between.

Once fully loaded, Redilok smiles and snaps her fingers, sending the platform cruising through the tunnel at dizzying speed. Despite how fast the three of you hurtle down the path, the ride seems remarkably calm. Your body feels still, but the lights whizzing by faster than your eyes can track show you're definitely moving.

It's not long before the Slabglider begins to slow and then stop. You worry something is wrong before Redilok confirms that you're near the center of the Stoneway, meaning that you crossed nearly a fourth of the continent in minutes. It's hard to even wrap your head around.

Once you disembark, several dwarves - some Nalidasi, some Flamberian - jump aboard and start unloading metal rails. You figure you 'ought to help instead of just standing around waiting.
Come on... Someone has to be out of place...

You're able to follow along with the dwarves quite well, and they're a bit impressed as you and [Companion Name] keep up with laying the railings and locking them into place. The Flamberians get to work as you set each in place and you finally take a good look at them. Each appears almost molten lacking any traditional skin and instead seeming to be made out of a stone-like material with bright red magma heating the rock as some sort of vein system, serving a purpose you can't even begin to guess at. Among them is their own royal, Prince Cintak.

They grip the newly connected rails at heat it until it's red-hot, binding individual sections together into one fully linked pathway. Once that's done, the Nalidasi etch in a last set of runes, activating the section of rail. Both Redilok and Cintak are active participants in the Stoneway creation, though you do note they do disappear alone together more than a few times throughout your time working on the path.

Construction goes on for a long time, and you end up returning to Koganusan several times, eating, sleeping, and enjoying the luxuries of staying within the royal palace, getting more acquainted with Redilok and several nobles within the kingdom's upper-ranks.

Finally, days after you began, the blue lights that light the corridor give way to red, and the rail you lay connects to that of the Flamberian's side of the Stoneway. It isn't sealed into place just yet, as this will be done at the ceremony Redilok informs you is called the 'Linking'.
Several years in the making... I can hardly believe we're done.
Hopefully the first step among many in soothing the wounds of the past.
Though I'm surprised Redilok sought it fit to bring along two humans, I trust her judgement.
We're just happy we could help out.
I'm sure... Though, I know you're here to ensure the Linking goes well. The royal princess has informed me of such.
You have my gratitude. Please ensure her safety over mine. I couldn't bare it to-
Cinny, please! All this propriety is going to put them off.
It's just a nickname of sorts the royal princess is fond of. It really doesn't mean much, pay it no mind.
Doesn't mean much, hm? You told me you loved it.
Of course I do my precious little cabochon! I-
The two of you are observant, I'm sure you've noticed the princess and I's...
Disappearances off into the dark of the tunnels?
I am in no position to ask this of you, but I must do so anyway.
Please keep this between yourselves for now. After the Linking the two of us intend to announce...
Oh Cinny. I'm sure they figured it out on day one.
Neither of us have any reason to mind, but isn't that a bit...
Cinny darling, it's a party! Drop a couple stones and lighten up, I've never gotten to tell anyone about this~

Prince Cintak simply holds his stony face in his hands as the princess starts to divulge far more detail than you would have thought she'd offer up. The Slabglider departs back towards Koganusan and comes back with half a village of dwarves, tables, decor, and liquor. Then it speeds off towards the Flamberian capitol and brings back even more. Just like that, the Linking is underway.

You and [Companion Name] stroll about the thrown together party. The Stoneglider comes and goes multiple times, bringing more people, food, and furnishings, all of which are tucked into the carved out alcove you all reside in. The atmosphere is lively, sometimes too much so. It'd seem the king isn't the only one with longstanding grudges, and several scuffles break out through the celebration, but they're quickly quelled.

You're on edge, waiting for any sign of the Soulsmiths. You scan every new arrival, take stock of each good brought in, and... the small hint of blood left on one of the chairs.

With the small fights, rowdy dwarves, and free flowing alcohol, it's no wonder someone could have gotten hurt, but the chair hadn't been unloaded from the Slabglider yet.

Something is awry, you just don't know what yet.

You move through the crowds and finally spot who you were looking for. The Nalidasi dwarf is almost indistinguishable from everyone else, except the fact that she's a bit more pale, and seems far less into the festivities than anyone else. She carries a large barrel draped in cloth and tucks it amongst many others at the back of the alcove.

You stop her by grabbing her arm, and the pale dwarf doesn't even react to your presence. [Companion Name] pulls up the dwarf's sleeve and you see her arm coated by a thick stream of blood. The woman drops the barrel, but stands motionless in your grip, lifeless eyes staring up at you. Quickly checking the woman over, you peel back her collar, you see that the blood on her arm must have come from her slit neck, which was intentionally hidden under her bulky garb. The dwarf's blank look reminds you of Talm controlling the Soulsmith back in the capitol, and judging by her state, you know she's being controlled by someone. 

But it's too late. Volatile runes spill out from the dropped barrel, similar to those you made with Gloob, though these look substantially better crafted.

Another dwarf - this one Flamberian - breaks the top of a barrel at the back of the room and sinks his hands inside of it before heating himself red hot.

[Companion Name] draws her bow and shoots at the dwarf, but the damage is done. You hear the sizzling of the volatile runes and cry out to anyone nearby.

You see several dwarves by the wall turn towards you, startled by the arrow whizzing in their direction and your shout. They disappear as the runes in the barrel and several others nearby explode with a burst of magical energy, swallowing them entirely in a flash of white light.

The whole world heaves upward. [Companion Name] grabs you as you're sent careening out of the alcove and down the tunnel, crashing to the ground with a sickening series of cracks then rolling several meters.

The two of you stagger towards your feet and rush back inside to see that half the cavity has been reduced to rubble, and many of those attending were killed instantly by the blast. The cleared out section is... far larger than it should be, as a large cavern is revealed by the blast. Soulsmiths adorned with gold trimmed robes and long, black metal weapons begin to flood out from the hole and descend on the Dwarves alongside their dark summoned monsters. 

The sight is horrifyingly similar to that dark night in Azamire.

Behind the cultists is a slug-like monster that pulls itself along the ground on countless sets of arms, pulling itself into the opening with sickening, twitchy movements. The creature is nearly as long as the Stoneglider, and twice as tall. A large black metal vessel protrudes from the beast's back, seemingly fused to it. You watch the device on its back begins to glow as it pulls itself towards the dead dwarves on the ground.

A pulse of dark green light washes over the bombed-out alcove.

Then the dead begin to move again.

When the dwarves that remain see you crash against the Soulsmiths, any who are able follow close behind you, burning with unbridled rage. You do your best to defend those too dazed or injured to help or run, but many are cut down by the Soulsmiths who weave through the crowd of undead.

This entire attack was planned out meticulously, maybe even your presence was accounted for. You try to intercept a group that head towards the Stoneglider, but the horde of undead stop you each time. Several Soulsmiths board the Stoneglider, load barrels of volatile runes onto the platform, then send it hurtling towards Koganusan. There's nothing you can do, there's too many things to deal with at once.

In the heat of battle you catch a glimpse of Prince Cintak standing over Princess Redilok, who clutches the new stump of her arm and tries to stem the bleeding. You try to reach them, but there's simply too many undead between you. It's not long before the prince is run through by one of the Soulsmith's black metal blades. He's then hefted into the air and unceremoniously pinned onto the back of the horrific slug creature who cries out as it's blubbery flesh is pierced. 

[Companion Name] is much closer, she reaches the princess just in time to spare her from the same fate as the prince. Moments after she cuts down the Soulsmith, those that remain call out to one another, escaping with the body of the prince, following after their beast who now scampers deeper into the cavern.

The undead remain, but without the threat of the gold-robed Soulsmiths probing for weaknesses or distractions, you're able to cut down the rest of them in short order. You rush to the princess's side. Undeterred by her missing arm, she stands, eyes piercing the dark of the cavern and staring towards those who took the prince. She claims that it'd take more than that to kill him, and that the Soulsmiths wanted him alive. [Companion Name] tries to stop the princess from following into the cavern, but she's undeterred.

Only thing you can do is follow after.

Prince Procurement - After the Soulsmith attack on the Linking, you and [Companion Name] follow after Princess Redilok who is out for blood. Will you find the prince at the end of the path, or lose another royal in the process?
I'll focus on breaking up the bigger rocks.
Light? We're close to the surface?

You hold a lantern aloft as the three of you jog through the cavern, barely illuminating the ancient tunnels. [Companion Name] continually tries to stop the princess - at least long enough to properly tend to her missing arm - but Redilok forces herself onward.

Another blast echoes down the winding passage in front of you, the sudden rush of wind nearly knocking you off your feet. You find the source not long after. The Soulsmiths collapsed the cave behind them, the rubble still settling as rocks shift into place.
Both of you, give me a hand, will you?
I seem to have just lost one. And then some.
We want to, princess, but we can't.
You're injured, and by the time we cut through this, they'll be long gone.
We should go back to Koganusan, regroup, and come back.
If they took [Companion Name] would you say the same?
Can you do one of those doorway thinggies you did before to get us to the other side of these rocks?
I can only set the destination to somewhere I've been before, it won't help here.
Then we'll have to go through. When we rescue the prince, can you get us back to the capitol?
I don't think so. The further the destination, the more magic it takes out of me. We're quite a ways from home.
If we're lucky, some of the survivors will realize I'm a bit limited and will wait for us.
Or... they'd be sensible and get themselves home, leaving us out here to this foolish mission alone.
Do you want to rest while we get this stone moved, then?
Hey now. I said I can't make a doorway through it, I didn't say I was gonna sit around and let you do all the work.

You set your jaw and take out your tools. The rock is dense and you're worried about a cave-in, but Redilok extends her hand and begins moving stone with her magic. Smaller boulders lift into the air and are thrown backward, crashing into the cavern walls far behind you.
Please don't blow up, please don't blow up, please don't blo-

The three of you make short work of the blockage and climb out of the caverns through what appears to have been a natural entrance to the cave system. The sun is just beginning to set over the western horizon, which initially gives you pause. It'd taken a while to get out of the caves, but the Soulsmiths are on foot as well, many of which are injured. There's a good chance they'd have to stop nearby.

You and [Companion Name] see it at the same time. A thin trail of smoke in this distance, not too far from you. A camp, it has to be.
Either of you any good at trackin'?
I... ugh. This is all a bit overwhelmin' for me.
The sun's so bright... grass is too smelly. Dwarves belong in the ground, not out in all this mess.
Yes, but we don't need to be. They clearly didn't think they'd be followed, because they've set up camp just over the hill.
We will. You're going to stay put. I promise you we'll get him back.
I'm fine. Don't need any babyin'.
I'm not asking. It seems like you'll hardly make the trek to their camp, let alone be ready for another fight.
Well, course I'm a little tired. I got my arm blown off and half the royal court got butchered in front of me, then they stood back up and tried to gnaw on me.
Speaking of you arm... you should tend to that wound, because your wrappings are already coming undone.

Redilok jabs her stump towards [Companion Name] and looks like she's about to say something protest before she realizes she's dripping blood on her boot. She sits with a grumble and waves you off. That's about as good of a blessing as you figure you're going to get.

As you get closer to camp, the two of you start to move more carefully, crawling on your stomachs through the plain's waist-high grass. The Soulsmiths may not have expected you to make it through the cave-in, but that didn't stop them from protecting themselves by littering the ground with volatile runes. [Companion Name] crawls towards one, trying to slowly pry it out of the ground with her knife.

Slowly but surely, she wiggles it out of the ground, then passes it back to you, then moves onto the next one. As tempting as it may be to keep it for later, keeping a small pile of bombs in your backpack it bound to lead to an untimely end. You'll have to carefully destroy them.

You roughly know how the magic works from your time creating similar charges with Gloob way back in Azamire, but these are far more complex.

As [Companion Name] very delicately extracts the volatile runes and passed them off, you slowly wither away their power. It's a nerve-wrecking process, and you feel time moving by glacially slow as you crawl closer and closer towards the Soulsmith's camp.

Eventually, you find yourself just outside the camp. You look over the wretched summoners, and one stands out among the elites: An elderly woman whose robes are instead lined with light strips of blue and green instead of gold. Someone important, doubtlessly, though you don't remember seeing her during the attack on the Linking. Dozing by the fire, patrolling around the slug monster, and even cozying up with a few resting cultists are a dozen or so large wolf-like creatures the Soulsmiths seem fond of. These ones are a lot larger than those they attacked Azamire with, though. Watching one of them nuzzle one of the murderers and seemingly beg for a scrap of food... makes you feel strange. These creatures may be summoned beasts, but they are alive and maybe even close with those who brought them to life. 

Back in the tunnels, the monsters ended the lives of dozens of dwarves, but it's not like they had a choice. You know as much from the creatures you've summoned yourself. You will them to do something, and they obey. 

You'll try to end them quickly.

You pry your eyes away and find Prince Cintak's corpse, still pinned to the slug creature by the black metal blade he was stabbed with. [Companion Name] scoots close and whispers to you.
Why'd they take him, and only him?
I don't know. The Soulsmiths were able to control those dead Dwarves during the Linking, maybe it has something to do with that?
Figure they'll tell us if we ask?
We'd have to leave one alive for that.
I didn't want to ask in front of the princess...
Do you think the prince is still alive?
...Well, we lived through the explosion and we're made of flesh. He's made of stone and magma...
Guess it's a good thing we didn't save some of those explosive runes then, huh? Wouldn't have minded putting them to good use.
If he is alive, and then we blew him up...
Well... we'd be lucky if we were only banished from both Dwarven kingdoms.
[Companion Name] grimaces at the thought. After a moment, she turns her attention towards the camp. She nods towards the Soulsmiths, and you nod back. No point in waiting.

You clash against the Soulsmith Elites, knowing that they're going to use their summoned creatures to frontline for them like they did with the undead back during the Linking. As the elites fall, the vessel attached to the slug monster whirrs to life and bathes the area in flashes of green light, and the elites rise again. It doesn't stop you.

Eventually, the monster runs out of bodies to throw at you, and the leader of this band of Soulsmiths throws herself at you directly, but even she falls. As you strike the killing blow, she commands the slug beast to escape, then falls silent in the tall grass of the plains. Following the orders of its master, the beast tears through the field, slimy arms tearing chunks out of the ground as it scuttles north. You keep pace with it, barely, but when you or [Companion] strike it, your weapons bounce off it, it's thick flesh seemingly resistant to conventional weaponry.

Suddenly, Prince Cintak stirs. It's hard to tell if the man is trying to free himself, or if his corpse is just being flung about, but sure enough, he is able to sink his feet into the monster's meat and push. The black metal sword that pinned him to the beast slides out from it's body with a nauseating squelch and the prince tumbles to the ground. Both you and [Companion Name] let the monster run, quickly attending to the prince instead. He lives, though the weapon that bound him to the slug is still firmly stuck within his stone body. For now, you're just happy he's in one piece. You watch as the Soulsmith's Shambling Beast drags itself far to the north and wish you could give chase, but it's a problem for another day.

Both of the royals support one another as the four of you head back down into the tunnels to reunite with the rest of the survivors. The molten Flamberians cheer with relief at the sight of their prince and surround him, offering to help tend his wounds or swear revenge on those who attacked the Linking. The Nalidasi greet the princess much the same. The wounded have been tended to through a mix of cauterization and sterilization from the party's booze, and many of the decorative tapestries have been torn to fashion bandages.

Once everyone is settled, the magically inclined amongst the Nalidasi join together and open a large doorway in the wall of the Stoneway tunnel, bringing you right to the smoking crater that was once the station you left from. Stone buildings all around you have been leveled by a blast that far outweighs the Soulsmith's attack on the Linking. Now you know what they did with the Stoneglide.

Both the Archivist and king Oyadazminis look upon the blast sight with anger and pain, but then relief upon seeing your group step out from the ashes. The man's eyes are wet with tears as he embraces his daughter, originally having feared the worst. He pulls you aside after breaking apart from the princess, and begs for your aid. He promises access to the Archive, the treasury, and whatever else you may desire in exchange for purging the Soulsmith blight from the land. Despite the Archivist trying in vain to slightly temper the king's impassioned promises of remuneration, his resolve is similarly hardened.

Koganusan is going to war, and you will help guide them to victory.

Repairing What Remains - The Soulsmiths successfully hijacked the Stoneglide and loaded it with explosives while those attending the Linking were preoccupied on all sides by assailants. Their efforts resulted in a massive swathe of Koganusan being reduced to rubble. Any amount of relief will go a long way towards caring for the populace.
Her house simply isn't enough. How about a proper cookhouse? Maybe she'll be able to get some help then, too?
Hopefully this will work a bit better than her home.

King Oyadazminis and the Archivist move with purpose through the ruined market district of Koganusan, handing out food to those who lost their homes and businesses, comforting others, and lending a hand where they can. Though it's a small comfort to those figuring out how to go on, it's still more than enough to get some following in their footsteps if they're able. The pair catch your eye and rush over after excusing themselves from a small group of young dwarves.
I never thought there'd be a day where I'm pleased to see two humans waiting for me, but these are trying times.
I haven't had the chance to properly thank you for returning my daughter to me, and unfortunately I am rather tied down at present.
We can see that. It feels rare to see someone of your station handling a crisis hands on.
Would you rather I leave it to those beneath me?
No, not at all. If anything, I find it refreshing, and it's clear your people do too.
I just wish I could have prevented it in the first place...
...I wish [Companion Name] and I could have done more.
Excuse me for speaking out of turn, but from the reports I've seen, it sounds as though there wouldn't have been a single survivor were it not for your efforts.
We owe you quite the debt, but it'll be some time before we can properly return the favor.
We're not worried about it in the slightest, we're just trying to do what we can to prepare to drive the Soulsmiths out of here for good.
You have my blessing and what I can spare of my men, though free hands are in short supply.
Speaking of which... If you find yourself in need of a bit more than I can offer...
I'm sure that the townsfolk would be even more willing to lend a hand with a bit of food in their bellies, or if you're able to help cure what ails them.
I'm sure we can figure something out, can't we [Player Name]?

Not sure where to start, you decide on the easiest of the options you can think of. Food. Easy to make in bulk, and something that everyone needs. You ask around until you hear of a kindly woman named Zotty, who has been taking care of as many of the districts kids as she can. From what you gather, she was a baker, but her business was destroyed in the attack, a story like many others in Koganusan. When you visit her house on the edge of the ruined district, you see a line of several kids line up by the door, each of them getting a small but well-seasoned portion of stew and a bit of bread.

Zotty is a bit wary of you at first, but your reputations proceed you both, and she simply says that any help you can offer is more than enough. It's clear she doesn't expect much, but you hope to prove her wrong.
Do we just plant these in the ground or..?

The devastation left by the Soulsmith attack has both fortunately and unfortunately left behind no small number of plots free of their original buildings. All it takes is a small chat with the king and one of them is requisitioned from its deceased owner and then attributed to the two of you. You draft up and begin construction on a sizeable cookhouse, capable of feeding a large portion of those displaced by the attack, and giving new purpose to a few as well, should they choose to help Zotty.

Building the structure goes much faster than expected. When townsfolk see you working on the structure, many come to help for any number of reasons. Dwarven pride, giving back to their community, or even trying to help the two of you in return for saving as many as you could at the Linking. Before you know it, the dwarven cookhouse stands tall amidst the rubble, ready to feed those in need. Zotty admires the building with her hands on her hips, save for a couple small dabs at her eyes when she thinks you aren't looking.
When I said I wanted a spot of help, I was expecting a bag of tubers, or maybe a scrap of meat.
Didn't expect you to drop a whole bleedin' building on my head!
Hopefully it'll be a good starting point. Lots of folks from around town pitched in, and there's a ton of cookware and raw foods as well.
It's more than I'll be able to handle alone. You two bring an army to help me keep the place runnin' too?
Not quite, but we figure if it's anything like building the place, once you start whipping up meals, others will start leaping over the counter to help you out.
You think I'm lettin' just any schmuck make food for the town?
I'm pleased the Nalidasi have left such an impression on you as to make you think we can do anything.
But let me tell you, cooking is not a strongsuit of our kind.
We've seen a few displays of... less proper ettique, but you all seem to take such pride in your craftsdwarfship, I almost find it hard to believe the Nalidasi don't treat food the same.
Let's just say that there's a reason you've seen our crafts and not our fine dining experiences.
I swear, folks are more inclined to start chewing gravel and wash it down with ale than to enjoy a proper meal half the time.
I was tryin' to do my best to fix that before my bakery got blown to bits.
Any ideas on where we could find you some help, then?
We just gotta give folks something they cannot possibly mess up. Cobblestone Soup.
...doesn't seem all that much better than the gravel you mentioned...

Zotty lets out a hearty chuckle before digging in her pocket and handing over a pouch of what looks like small bits of quartz. She assures you that they'll grow into Stonemelons, which are used in a soup that's hearty and filling, and practically impossible to mess up.
I should probably wash my pickaxe.

The stonemelons grow strong with little supervision, which doesn't surprise you based on the name. Continuing to live up to their title, these small boulder-like melons look nearly identical to any ordinary rock you'd see out and about, except that they're almost perfectly spherical orbs. They're heavy, but you manage to lug your harvest back to Zotty's new cookhouse.
Proper dwarven farmers, the lot of you! Hardly seen any Stonemelons this size in my days, almost as good as my ol' pappy Xon could grow.
I'm glad you're impressed, though almost surprised you could tell them apart from any old rock.
Clear as day to my dwarvern eyes, surprised you don't see it.
Clear as day? But we don't get any sunlight down here...
It's awfully clear though, ain't it?
Well, how do we get these open? Should have plenty of knives around.
Our knives are for cuttin' up veggies and carvin' out meat. Step aside.

Zotty grabs a pickaxe from the wall she seems to have brought out for just this purpose. She brings it down on the melon several times to no avail - to the point you're concerned you brought her an actual rock - until eventually, the melon cracks open like a geode. Inside, the stonemelon is filled with white flesh, which Zotty then extends out to you. You scrape a bit off and are surprised by its rubbery texture, and the fact that it's almost savory, like smoked meat. Zotty waves her hand towards your pile and gets to work cutting open a few more herself.
A bit of this, and a bit of that...

You do a better job of mashing the stonemelons to bits than splitting them perfectly in half like Zotty does in the beginning until she gives you a few pointers. You slowly but surely make your way through the pile, leaving behind a crime scene that'd inspire fear in all but the bravest of produce.
The two of you done makin' a mess?
Think so! What do ya do with 'em now?
I ain't just gonna tell ya, I'm gonna show ya.
I know the two of ya' got some proper worldsaving to go do, but if everyone here starves by the time you get back, what's it for?
I won't keep ya long, promise.

Zotty starts the stoves and begins carving out the melon flesh, dicing and seasoning it with a handful of herbs. Once her pot of water begin to boil, she tosses the prepared flesh back in, then combines it with some meat and veggies and stirs. Once done, she pours it into the hollowed out shell of the stonemelon and pushes it towards the two of you.

The Nalidasi may not value cooking much, but with food like this, it's sure to change.

Before either you or [Companion Name] can finish cooking your first pots, both Nalidasi and many of the Flamberian survivors from the Linking start trickling into the cookhouse, asking how they can help - in exchange for a bit of food of course - and Zotty begins barking out orders like a trained general. Flamberians heat their bodies and are used as stoves, much to the amusement of both races of dwarves. Zotty moves through the kitchen with purpose, correcting well-intentioned helpers and directing them to watch you and [Companion Name] as examples.

It takes a while, but those in the cookhouse start to produce Cobblestone Soup that Zotty is willing to serve to the long line of hungry survivors of the market district disaster. The two of you do so well Zotty is reluctant to let you go, until King Ozadazminis himself offers himself and the Archivist as replacements during a visit to the building's opening night. Zotty grumbles and mentions that good help is hard to find, but allows to you go after making sure you've both eaten your fill.

Slug Slayer - There's only one thing you've seen that can pierce the Soulsmith slug monster's thick flesh, and it's currently embeded within the chest of the Flamberian Prince. Surely he's willing to part with it... if he can.
Should come to a point here, maybe a handle made of...

You wander outside of the room Prince Cintak has been being kept in, but were blocked by Princess Redilok before you could see the man.You and [Companion Name]'s plan is absurd, but if you intend to take down the Shambling Beast, you see no other path forward. You lay it out in detail to Princess Redilok, who blanches at the thought.
Oh, right. You'll carefully rip the spike of unknown material out of Prince Cintak's chest and close him up before he bleeds out.
Which of you is the surgeon, hm? I'm sure my father has an axe or something you could use...
...I know the concept is scary, but we're going to ask the prince what kind of... wound care his people even use.
We've banadaged ourselves up countless times, but I'm not really sure where we'd start with someone made of stone and lava.
And we're not going to be the ones operating on him, don't worry.
I remember being introduced to someone at the Linking that seemed to be a big-shot in Flamberian society because they were a doctor.
If he's still around, he would have come back with the rest of the survivors. He'd be the surgeon.
But if the prince doesn't make it, I'll see you both tried for treason. You won't leave Koganusan alive.

Redilok seems to mull on the idea, before stepping aside and opening the door to his room. Prince Cintak is in rough shape. He put on a brave front while trekking back to the Dwarven capital, but the events of the Linking have doubtlessly worn away at the man. His breaths are labored, and the twisted black metal rod peircing his chest seems to have fused more with him. Despite his state, he still manages a smile as the three of you enter the room. After catching him up on current events, you detail your reason for visiting. You want to pry the metal from his chest and fashion it into a weapon to kill the Shambling Beast the Soulsmiths attacking the Linking with.

He digests the words for only a moment before praising the idea, reiterating that it seems to be the only thing that's pieced the beast's flesh, and that he's more than willing to help and details what he knows. First-aid for Flamberians seems to be more akin to working on a forged good than a living being, but you suppose that that makes sense for a being comprised of stone and magma. His people use emerald-tipped blades that are magically enhanced to cut into thier rocky exteriors. Then, for a wound that'll be as severe as his, a concoction of golden stardust and sporlyle would be able to help his body seal the wound, but he'd need to be hammered closed, like working on a platebody.

Princess Rodilok nearly faints as the man details beating on his chest with hammers to close the wound.

You decide to search for your doctor first. He's easy to find, as the man has been helping treat some of the more severely wounded folks in the Nalidasi market district, which has gone a long ways towards lightening some of concern that the Flamberians were behind the attack. When you detail your plan for working on the prince, Doctor Hacksmith is able to draw up a detailed schematic for this emerald blade that Cintak mentioned, but all of the doctor's handwriting is next to indesipherable. At least the diagram is detailed enough for you to work on.
I wonder how Flamberian bodies handle stardust...
Can't imagine something like this would have a regenerative effect on human flesh... Maybe the opposite.

When king Oyadazminis said that you'd have the backing of the whole kingdom when it came to getting them ready to go against the Soulsmiths, you didn't expect the level of support he decided to show. When one of his aids found you and [Companion Name] hammering out prototypes of the emerald tool in the palance courtyard, Oyadazminis himself had his people gather your things and walked you through the capitol until you found a lovely, well-stocked workshop built within the stalk of a large plant that you've never seen anywhere outside of the cavern. The workshop itself is outfitted with dozens of tools and workstations you couldn't even begin to guess at the function of. He bought the workshop from the owner, who tried to protest up until the kings' aids draped him in jeweled necklaces and sacks of gold were dropped in front of him until he couldn't see over the pile. In exchange, him and his workers found a perfect balance of handing you tools before you even asked for them, pointers in working with emerald, and giving you space when you needed it.

After a few dozen failed attempts, you finally create a blade that was strong enough to chip away at stone with nary a scratch, and that is without the magical enhancements the prince mentioned. The former workshop owner - an older dwarf with gold-blonde hair who introduced himself as Kajc -  takes the blade and plunges it into the wall, before leaning back and stroking his chin.
Now, that's a fine tool you've got there, folks.
What'd you say it was for, again?
Eh... it might be better if you don't know.
Make sure you come on back here though if you've got more stuff to work on.
I suppose my workshop is more the king's workshop, so it's not like I'd be able to stop you even if I wanted to.
And how do you feel about that?
Oh, it's wonderful! Do you know how long its been since I've had to help make something important?
It's just been random bits and bobs for years. A ring here, a golden egg that'll sit on a shelf collecting dust for ages there.
At least this fancy poker you've got is going to be used for something. Makes me feel useful.

You head back to the palace with your emerald tool and hand it off to the princess, who promises she'll make it capable of withstanding the staggering heat of Cintak's blood. She mentions few things can handle someone as hot as him, and you get the feeling that she stopped talking about his blood a long while ago, but you let her babble, as she's clearly nervous about the whole ordeal of cutting open her not-so-secret love. Eventually she shoos you away, to get you working on the potion that should help seal up the prince once Hacksmith is done cutting the metal out of his body.

You come back with the sparkling concoction and bring it into the bedroom-turned-surgery suite. A few Flamberians have joined Doctor Hacksmith, their purpose seemingly to be there to heat up the Prince's body, and then help hammer him closed afterward. The princess presents your emerald blade, now with glowing runestones etched into its hilt. Hacksmith presses one and the blade glows red, waves of heat scorching the air around it. The doctor tests the blade lightly on his own leg, then takes your potion and dribbles a few drops on the wound. Just as easily as the blade cut stone, your elixir quickly helps his rocky flesh knit back together.
I think we're about ready to begin.
Prince, I apologize that we hardly have an ideal room, staff, or tools to treat you.
Your family is well known to mine, I know I'm in good hands.
You say that when you're worse off than me. You're missing a whole arm.
But I'm stable. They're practially cutting your heart out!

Cintak pulls the princess close and whispers something in her ear, which seems to help her settle, and blush. You turn away to let the two of them have their moment, but soon enough, everyone's ferried out of the room.

The surgery is long. Several times you and [Companion Name] have to settle Princess Redilok from interrupting, but she hardly seems that intent on entering. Just the idea of having to wait outside and feeling like she can't help further drives her up the wall.

After multiple hours, you begin to hear loud thuds from the Prince's room. Hammering Cintak's chest back closed sounds lightly terrifying, but you trust the Flamberians know their own anatomy better than you do. Eventually, the door swings open, and Hacksmith declares his work done, before handing you the rock of dark twisted metal. After a quick peek to check in on the Prince, you let Redilok stay with him herself, then head back to the workshop to fashion a weapon out of the weird material.

As you beat the metal rod into a speartip, something becomes distrubingly clear. The metal that was burried inside the prince is alive. [Companion Name] suggests the name Soulsteel, keeping in line with the Soulsmiths' unoriginal naming conventions, and the name sticks. The dwarves in the workshop are more fascinated than horrified by the material and frequently suggest... unconventional smithing methods to combat the metal's unwillingness to take shape the way you want it to. You try hammering it for hours on end, taking turns with [Companion Name] and Kajc. You try etching it in acid, heating it and cooling it in a way that'd make any other metal crack, all to no avail. The only thing that works is when you... speak with it. The Soulsteel doesn't speak back, but it wavers in all sorts of fashions, communicating in a language you haven't got the slightest clue on how to begin desciphering.

Eventually, you manage to learn its version of positive and negative wiggles, you're able to tell it that you intend to kill off the beast it originally came from, to which it seems thrilled. At least, you think that's what it is trying to communicate to you. It stops resisting being shaped and you're able to use it to make the cutting edge of a long, curved blade. You don't like how the metal seems to shiver whenever it is close to something, but you can't think of any other way to cut through the beast it came from. For now, this will have to do.

Misty Mystery - The Soulsmith's Shambling Beast was last seen dragging its pitiful form north from the center of the Stoneway. As long as it didn't change directions, that'd place it somewhere within the Misty Thicket... an incredibly dense bog covered in a perpectual blanket of mist. The perfect place to go searching for a monster.

It feels good to be outside the caverns that hold the Nalidasi capital, but unfortunately, it's not like your planned adventure is going to be particularly fun. You take in a deep breath of fresh air and wipe off a layer of dust that you're sure has been perptually stuck to your body during your subterranean stay, despite your adherance to basic hygenie. You and [Companion Name] take the time to map out the area, lining up your current position with where the Linking took place, and then plotting the trajectory of where the Shambling Beast could have shuffled off to, assuming it stayed the same course across an unknown amount of distance. It should be somewhere within the Misty Thicket, though you can't begin to wager where, you'll just have to deal with that once you get there.

A long shot, but the best you've got, considering the current circumstances.
It's... quite a ways away, isn't it?
I don't suppose the Nalidasi have a second, smaller, portable Stoneglider, that doesn't need rails, huh?
It'd be a mix of amazing and terrifying if they did. If I was moving that fast over land, it'd only be a matter of time before I hit something a little too big.
I imagine it'd look a little like a balloon filled with red paint hitting a wall.
Maybe it is best they keep those on rails, eh?
It's so much distance to cover on foot. We'll have to keep ourselves stocked up along the way.
Just like travelling to the capitol! Feels like that was so long ago. I won-

Both of you drop into combat position as you hear a shout from the cliffs up above you. Several loud growls and snarls follow, followed by several swears and exclamations of 'bad doggy'. You look to [Companion Name] who shrugs and starts climbing the cliffside.

You weren't too sure what you'd find when you climbed the cliffface, but it wasn't a young Flamberian dwarf being chased by half a dozen Rockwolves. The young man dangles from a twiggy looking tree growing out of the mountainside while Rockwolves jump up to nip at his heels, trying to grab a bite.

The moment that the two of you pull yourselves up over the side, the Rockwolves turn towards you. They snarl and start angling towards the pair of you instead, until a brief moment of familiarity washes over them. A Rockwolf with an outer shell of a sandy-looking stone carefully approaches you, then flips over at your feet in submission. These wolves must have been from the same pack as the one you fought when you first arrived at the Perilous Peaks, it's the only thing that explains their current behavior. The large rock-covered wolves gaze down at you, seemingly waiting for your next move. Some yawn and lay down, or snarl at the Flamberian as he tries to push his way over to you. The Rockwolves are immense creatures, easily twice your size, which make the Flamberian look even smaller in comparison.
I figured they'd be out for revenge after we...
Took care of the big one.
Seems that we're the big ones, now.
We are? You hardly come up to the things' shoulder.
Tell that to it. Seems pretty supplicant to me.
How in the names of the Great Flame did you two do that?
We had a run in with their leader a while back, and it seems that they aren't too mad that we... turned it into jerky.
Incredible. Animal Behaviorial Specialist Brunite at your service. Humans are a rarity in these parts...
Well, normally they are, at least. The last time I saw some was actually...
Wait. You were at the Linking! You saved our prince!
Well, we helped out a bit.
Please, please, you're far too modest. I doubt any of us would have gotten out of there alive were it not for your efforts.
And... me doubly so, it'd seem. Thank you for saving me once again.
We didn't have to do much, we're able to get a better vantage up here anyway.
Oh? And what are you scouting out, if I may ask?
We're headed out to the Misty Thicket. It'll be quite the journey.
What'd you learn about the behaviors of the Rockwolves? That they're hungry?
They seem to designate members of their pack to hunt, while others serve other purposes.
For example, the one at your feet there, its stone hide is closely related to sandstone. Hunters will sharpen their teeth by gnawing on its hide, like you'd sharpen your blade on a whetstone.
They metabolize both meat and stone, with different Rockwolves prioritizing different stone and mineral types to change their hides in accordance with what the pack needs.
I'd imagine you were acting in self-defense when you fought against the pack earlier. Well, it seems they're missing a handful of crucial roles now.
Maybe there's something that can be done for your journey...

Brunite details his plans. He'd originally wanted to use the wolves as mounts to help his people return back to their home once things were sorted with the Soulsmiths, but maybe with your help, he could expidite his plans, in exchange for letting you bring some of the wolves with you. They already seem plenty docile with you around, what's the harm in trying, right? 

You return to the capitol, and run the idea of starting a breeding program for the Rockwolves to the king, who simply laughs and waves his hand, seemingly letting the Archivist write down and deal with aquiring the materials to set up a place to store, raise, and train wolves, assuming they don't break out and eat you.
I just want to find the beast and get back home.

The wolves are equal parts stone and organic, and with sufficent meat and sources of minerals, they grow much faster than you'd ever expect. In conjunction with preparing a route to the Misty Thicket, you frequently stop in to help Brunite with the Rockwolf study, creating wolves that didn't seem to appear naturally before. Soon enough, by the time you're ready to head out, you have three wolves with hides made of a material similar to quartz, hoping it'd be light enough for travel but hard enough to protect the beasts from any kind of dangerous monsters you may come across in the countryside.
I can't believe it! Rockwolves feel like they were made to be domesticated. Most of them are generally of good temperment, and they're so friendly too!
Milkbone here hardly stops licking me! I'm shocked at how fast they can grow under controlled conditions, too, it reminds me of growing crystals as a boy.
Are you sure that Milkbone isn't just seeing if you'd be a good addition to her hide? Flamberians are mostly stone, right?
[Companion Name] be nice, I'm sure she's just a friendly, mostly feral wolf.
Are you sure you want to join us though, Brunite? The Misty Thicket is a long ways away.
We're just scouting a path and locating that monster that attacked the Linking, but we'll almost definitely get into some trouble at some point.
