And miss the opportunity to see how the first wolves we've bred behave in uncontrolled conditions? Not a chance!

Atop the quartz rockwolves, you make extrodinary time. The beasts are fast, incredibly easy to care for, and defend themselves well enough that you feel comfortable sleeping through the night without anyone on watch. Despite his shaky introduction, Brunite proves to be quite capable while travelling to the Misty Wetlands with you, though he does still jump a bit whenever Milkbone licks him, wondering if [Companion Name]'s joke held any truth.

Finding the Shambling Beast will be like finding a needle in a haystack - and that's if it's even here in the first place - but you trudge into the wetlands regardless. The Misty Wetlands have both mist and wetland in abundance, and you frequently have to stop and cut your way through underbrush or use lumber to cross particularly deep stretches of water, especially with your heavy Rockwolves accompanying you.
I wonder what they may have...

As you sink your axe into yet another tree to cross another endless stretch of water, a flaming bolt glances your shoulder and sinks into the thick bark. You drop your axe and whip your head around to see the burning shilloette of a Flamberian far behind you, with a hefty crossbow held aloft. You cry out and everyone dives into the water, narrowly avoiding further projectiles. A volley of similar bolts follows soon after, peppering the ground and trees around you, your party, and mounts. You poke your head out of the water and see [Companion Name] fire a bolt of magic that freezes the water in the air, providing a thin shield against the attacks' bolts.
I fear you're right. I hope the two of you are... capable of dealing with them?
If we have to. Any clue on why they're out here, and what problem they'd have with us?
I mean, you're one of them, no?
Not all Flamberians were too interested in peace with the Naladasi.
I'm sure the defectors have some way of identifying one another, and I'm sure I don't look the part.
Any idea on if this will cause any problems for us later on down the line?
Oh, I highly doubt it! There's a reason why they're hiding all the way out here.
Those that are willing to reject the Naladasi with violence aren't welcome in our kingdom.

That's enough for the two of you. Brunite gets your mounts to cover while you and [Companion Name] do your best to move towards the Flamberians as quietly as you can through the wetland bogs. Shrouded by the mist and setting sun, you're upon them before they even know it. You reach up from the water and drag one of the attackers under, silencing them as quickly as you can. The Flamberian next to him cries out, and the group is thrown into chaos.
Has to be what we're looking for.

You and [Companion Name] pant in the mist, happy to be done with such messy work. Killing monsters is one thing, but it's always a little bit different to be fighting against human - or human adjacent - opponents, even if they're the aggressors. Brunite brings your rockwolves over once the sounds of fighting die down, trying to avert his eyes from the dead dwarves in the water.
I'm sorry. They didn't seem to be too interested in talking through things.
We didn't have much choice in the matter.
Oh, don't get me wrong, I won't shed any tears for them.
They probably feared we'd give them up to Flamberian authorities if we found them out here, and thought it'd be better to silence us.
The two of you are just...
I can't think of many people who could move that quickly and leave that much death in their wake. Regardless of the reason.

Brunite grimaces as Milkbone starts to sniff the corpse of one of the attackers, and pulls her away from the body. You and [Companion Name] start to go through the defectors' posessions and find a map and various plans they'd made. Several drafts of ransom notes which lead you to believe they intended to kidnap Prince Cintak at some point... they were ambitious if nothing else. They seemed to have a nearby camp, but what interests you far more is an old ruined castle, the Flamberians had marked, circled, and drawn several warnings of "Death" and "Stay away" around. Seems like a good place to start your search. As you get closer to the old ruined castle, you find tracks that stick out in the murk. Tracks made by hundreds of pairs of arms.

The Shambling Beast made a mess of a trail through the Misty Thicket, and you wager you'd be able to follow it all the way out pretty easily, now that you've found its trail. Downed trees, a huge gouge through the ground thats already filled with water, and occasional lumps of flesh are pretty telling that you're on the right track. As you get closer and closer to what you presume would be the castle, the stench of death seems to hang in the air, which is impressive for such a horrid bog that already doesn't smell like a bundle of roses.

The two of you leave Brunite and the Rockwolves behind, trusting in your ability to move more quietly and take up less space than huge beasts with stone for fur. You follow the trail until you find what the Flamberians detailed on their map. Row upon row of corpses are pinned to the outer walls of a ancient castle. All of the bodies are seemingly frozen in space, but doubtlessly alive, since the wall adornments seem to moan and twitch from time to time. The mist-shrouded moat surrounding the castle does little to brighten the image in your mind. You let out an involentary shiver as you gaze up at the macbre sight.

[Companion Name] pulls you away, sure that the monster you're looking for is within the walls. This is definitely not something you can take on alone. It's time to see just how serious King Oyadazminis is about going to war, because it'll take quite the siege to bring down these walls. The journey back is much faster than your journey in, perhaps in part due to the back you know you'll have dry feet for the first time in a while. It's still quite the trek to return to the capitol, but it's comparatively smooth sailing than your trip to the Misty Thicket.

Bring Down The House - The weapon to defeat the Shambling Beast is ready, and a path to the Soulsmith's Ruin is cleared. Prince Cintak and Princess Redilok will lead their people into battle, with you and [Companion Name] at the head.
I can't wait to see them in action.

The path to the Misty Keep is plotted, a weapon to slay the Shambling Beast is strapped to your back, and things are slowly returning to normal in Koganusan. As you walk through the outer courtyard of the palace, you notice a large number of guards out and training against one another, with the occasional Flamberian even dotting their ranks - holdovers from the Linking that haven't been able to start the trek back to their homeland yet, and have decided to accompany the prince until he sees it fit to return.

When you enter the throne room, King Oyadazminis looks down from his seat with a knowing expression.
It's been many long years since we actively sought dealings with your kind, but what transpired at the Linking has given me much to think about.
Though I doubt most humans would be willing to help even a fraction as much as the two of you have, perhaps we've been... avoidant, for far too long.
Once those who attacked my people are burried in thier marsh, we'll send an envoy or two around. Let your people know that we'd be willing to entertain more than a few tourists, from time to time.
The world would be much better off for it.
You know they would be. We'll see if your fancy nobles can stay standing after a single glass of fine Naladasi liqour.
But, as much as I'd like to, I can't entertain the thought of festivities yet.
We've read over your reports and path to the Soulsmiths' keep.
As the king has so kindly promised, our people are at your disposal, though we'll be joining you as well.
As will my daughter... Try as I might, she refuses to stay off the battlefield, despite her injuries. The...
...Prince, seems to have taken a liking to my daughter, and is joining her.
We'd be fortunate to have the four of you alongside us, but wouldn't that be... dangerous for you all?
What kind of father would I be if I let my daughter fight my battles for me?
The king has also expressed interest in making sure nothing... untoward occ-
Ahem. We've prepared several wagons. I hear that your little breeding program with the Rockwolves has gone well?
We feel they'd be far better for handling any outdoor excursions than our current beasts of burden. Brunite was more than happy to help create some wolves that could help.
It sounds like we're just about ready then, yes?

As you leave the palace, the most of training guards have already mobilized, with the remainer saluting the two of you as you pass by. You meet Brunite at the caverns set aside for the Rockwolf breeding program, and even he dawns an axe and simple armor. He brings the two of you your wolves, then takes a seat upon Milkbone and takes off down a long line of pens, cutting open the fences as he runs along, a growing pack of Stonewolves following behind him as he charges through the caverns and out of the caverns.

It's a little startling to see just how many wolves can be made in the right conditions, and hope that Brunite hasn't made too much of a fuss in the capitol. Despite the sight, many citizens cheer after you as you race through the city and out into the fresh air above. The pack slows as you step outside to see a large procession of Naladasi with armed wagons, some topped with braziers you imagine are to ward off the mists of the thicket.

There are numerous shouts as you arrive, but not because of you, it's because of the similarly sized horde growing in the distance. A large, orderly rank of Flamberians march towards the Naladasi, carrying large waving banners that make the whole army appear as if they're on fire. You spot Prince Cintak flag down king Oyadazminis, and the two of them march out to meet the army. An hour passes before the army continues its advance, banners now down. Hopefully that's a good thing?

The Prince announces that due to the silence that followed after the Linking, the Flamberians had reason to suspect the Naladasi had attacked the procession and kidnapped him, but he's informed his mother - the queen - of the full situation, and the army that was sent to attack the Naladasi are instead joining them to attack Soulsmiths. Apperently.

The journey back out to the Misty Thicket starts tense, but as more and more stories are traded between the rank and file, the dwarves stoke one another's passion towards their shared enemy, and find themselves growing closer in the process.

The wagons are pulled around to create a wall of sorts a few hours out from the Misty Keep, and you and [Companion Name] keep yourselves busy by helping to prepare the massive bolts that'll be loaded into the ballista-carrying wagons.
I just have to reel them in before the shadows do.

You're pleased to take a bit of time to yourself, even if it is to do more work. The journey over had been long and tiring, constantly riding between the ranks and guiding troops. The Flamberian queen has repeatedly called for your attention, but with as many moving parts as this war procession has had, you simply haven't had the time. Thankfully, Prince Cintak has reassured you that his mother is aware of the stakes and your part in keeping everything moving, and is more than happy to wait. You lay down after having earned your rest, and try to calm your nerves before finally falling to sleep.

After nowhere near enough time, you open your eyes to the daylight, you realize... there shouldn't be daylight. You were in a covered wagon. You look around and notice that four Flamberians have lifted your cot and carried you out in front of the queen. [Companion Name] is in a similarly dazzed, groggy state as yourself, both of you seemingly having been tired and secure enough to sleep through the... basically kidnapping. Prince Cintak stands beside his mother, mortified, and shoots you an apologetic look.
It is a pleasure to finally see the faces of my son's saviors.
I apologize for disrupting your sleep, but I wished to make myself known to you before we are to head into battle alongside one another.
I- I- Good morning, your excellency, queen...
Rest, child. I've done away with my name long ago, like all those who ascend to my rank. You may refer to me as the Flame.
I tried to get her to hold off a while longer, but she was insistant.
Pleased to meet you, your grace, but... may I ask why you've brought us here?
From what I've heard, the two of you are the reason my son still breathes.
My nation is in your debt, as am I. Were it not for your efforts, my people would have surely clashed against the Naladasi, and we'd be all the worse for it.
We were just doing what is right. The Soulsmiths... they've torn apart so many homes, our own included.
I'm just glad we were able to get to him in time.
I just wanted to bring it to your attention that I'm endlessly thankful for your assistance, and for your efforts, I wish to reward you once we return to our homeland. I'd like to-
She wants to show off that she can give you more than the Naladasi and keep you around as my personal bodyguards.
My darling little lava rock is right! You're heroes and should be treated as such! AND I find it outrageous that that cheapskate king has you sleeping in a cart!
Are you sure the two of you want to be on the front lines?

Perhaps the three of you, or four since my precious son seems to have a thing for that cute little Naladasi princess, can wait back here while we level the castle of those rotten Soulsmiths for ever daring to-
Shush dear, you can't fault a mother for trying to keep her baby safe.
Since you're all so determined to join us on the battlefield, see to it that he's safe, will you?
Of course, we'll do our best to make sure as many people make it back alive as we can.
Please do... I can't lose my son a second time.

The queen seems to be at least partially assuaged by this and nods her head. The Flamberians that carried you out now pick your cots up and carry you back to the wagon, and you try to digest what just happened.

After a couple more hours, the camp begins to shuffle once more. The dwarves break down camp and begin to move out once more. You and [Companion Name] mount your Rockwolves and lead the way, guiding the group across the more percarious bits of terrain and waiting for them to create paths to get wagons across large stretches of water when required. The castle looms in the distance, almost seemingly a source of the Misty Thicket's fog itself. The walls covered in corpses only shake the resolve of the dwarves for a moment, though you hear several utterances of how sick the people inside must be.

Soulsmiths line the walls, along with summoned beasts that remind you of bats, with mouths that are far too large.

Wagons are pulled up to form an armored wall, and then, everyone bursts into motion. Several large balls of energy soar over the walls of Misty Keep, but are burned away by Flamberian mages, or sent far off course by Naladasi mages interferring with their course. Four of the wagons' walls fall away to reveal giant ballista, which are loaded with bolts created just last night. You and [Companion Name] move through the ranks and direct their fire, and the balista shots land true. When they sink into the wall, glowing runestones across their surface glow bright, then explode, ripping large sections of the ancient castle apart. You hear and see King Oyadazminis let out a battlecry as he hefts a large javilen towards the ramparts and snaps his fingers just before contact, causing the bolt to explode in a dazzling ball of light that blows twenty Soulsmiths apart. The Archivist twists his staff in the air and halts another ball of green energy above the army before sending it back over the wall towards whatever sent it in the first place, causing the entire castle to shake with the impact.

Soulsmiths fire all manner of bolt, arrow, and magic towards the dwarves, and they return fire, but the evergrowing swarm of bat-like creatures harass the them. You watch as several dwarves are picked up by the beasts and are dropped into the moat around the castle, where large, dark shadows quickly pull the soliders under the water. Bats are burned away, and more balista shots are loosed at the walls, but with the force you're now taking, one of the balls of green energy makes it through your defenses and crashes into one of the wagons, leaving it a smoldering pile of scrap. The bats grow further in number, and your find a startling number of dwarves being carried away, while the Flamberian Queen seems to be frozen in shock. You grab a length of rope with a hook on the end, meant to scale the walls, and instead use it to fish out a dwarf from the water. Many others around you follow suit, while the back ranks cover you.

You do what you can, hauling as many dwarves out of the water as you have time for. Tons of hooks fly into the water once the others catch wind of your idea. You haul up more dwarves than you can count, but as you reel in another, your rope goes taught and is ripped from your hands, then goes slack. Whatever is in the water is very, very, big.

The Flame is ripped from her trance-like state. It wasn't shock, the woman was preparing. The thicket behind the dwarves cracks and screams as a wave of golden fire washes overhead like a wave crashing on the beach. The sky is blotted out by golden flame that sweeps through the air and rips through the majority of the Soulsmiths' bats and crashes against the wall, lighting the corpses ablaze. Where they were still before, the living wall now screams at your forces, with many of them tearing away bits of their body and turning it into balls of black magic which they then pelt you with.

Each one explodes in black flashes with concussive force, sending those they hit to the ground. Another wagon is destroyed as a volley of green magic comes over the wall once more. Soulsmiths atop the wall fire at the undefended dwarves, but both races return with their own bolts in turn. Princess Redilok stands atop one of the balista wagons and charges the bolt that is fired from it. It connects with the south-western tower, and explodes with startling force. The tower groans and collapses due to the damage, Soulsmiths try in vain to jump from its collapsing weight, but land in the water amongst whatever monster they have patrolling the depths.
It's time! Their forces are scattered!
For those who died at the Linking!
For all the lives the Soulsmiths have claimed!

Only two of the four balista carts still stand, but it's enough. Ropes are already tied to the large bolts which are launched and burried into the top of the drawbridge. Brunite sees to the Rockwolves and orders them to charge away from the keep, pulling the ropes taught. Another pair of bolts are launched. Then another. Then another. You lose another of the carts to a group of Soulsmiths that has flown over the wall atop giant versions of the bats that swarmed you before the golden flames burned the from the sky, but they're eventually cut down.

Finally, the drawbridge gives and comes crashing down. The path into the Misty Keep is open.  Wolves are unteathered and then sent back towards the keep, their stony bodies deflecting some of the smaller projectiles as they crash into the ranks of Soulsmiths on the other side of the gate. Flamberian and Naladasi charge side-by-side across the bridge, some stopping to pull up comrades from the water. As dwarf and Soulsmith fall, an all too familiar sight that brings back memories of the Linking washes over you. A pulse of green light, then the dead begin to move once more. The Shambling Beast is here.

You charge amongst the dwarves with [Companion Name] at your side, and you find yourself face-to-face with a Soulsmith. A butcher. A monster. She raises her staff towards you, but is carved down by Prince Cintak, who leads the charge. The man yells to those around him to clear a path.

The Shambling Beast crawls towards you, endless rows of arms churning the earth beneath it. You lift your Soulmetal-lined Blade and charge through the crowd.

With each stroke of your blade, its Soulsteel edge seems to quiver with delight. You find the blade actively pulling towards its source and relishing in the pain it inflicts upon the Shambling Beast. You carve through the beast, the blade pulls you further, and you climb atop the spongey flesh of the creature. 

Hundreds of arms grasp at you as it tries in vain to pull you off, but [Companion Name] batters them away, ripping a spike of Soulsteel from the monster and weilding it like a mallet, repeatedly crashing down upon the beast. Your sword continues to delight in cleaving through flesh, but you wrest control of it long enough to drive the sword into cage fused with the back of the Shambling Beast.

With that, another pulse of green light is unleashed and you're thrown from the creature, leaving your sword wedged in the metal of the cage. As you sail through the air, you see the undead begin to drop, but the Soulsmiths fight on. However, without support from the undead, they're far outnumbered by the dwarves. 

The Shambling Beast is dead. You've won.

You feel nothing but relief as you crash into the ground, and everything goes dark.

Battle enemies to gain [color=#FFD16D]Combat Skill XP[/color] and collect valuable rewards as loot. [color=#FFD16D]Combat Skill XP[/color] is granted based on the [color=#FFD16D]weapon damage[/color] you deal.
Select from [color=#FFD16D]Combat Areas, Slayer Zones[/color] or [color=#FFD16D]Dungeons[/color] to find different enemies to battle.

[color=#FFD16D]Equip [u]Food[/u][/color] to automatically restore Health when it falls below a set threshold, helping you survive longer battles.

More information is contained by hovering over the [color=#FFD16D]Auto Eat icon on your Health Bar[/color].

There are three Combat Styles: [color=#FFD16D]Melee, Ranged[/color] and [color=#FFD16D]Magic[/color]. Your equipped [color=#FFD16D]weapon[/color] determines which style you use.

[color=#FFD16D]Melee[/color] beats [color=#FFD16D]Ranged[/color]
[color=#FFD16D]Ranged[/color] beats [color=#FFD16D]Magic[/color]
[color=#FFD16D]Magic[/color] beats [color=#FFD16D]Melee[/color]

Beating a Combat Style [color=green]increases your Max Hit by 10%[/color], while losing [color=orange_red]decreases it by 10%[/color]. This is only applied to you, and never the Enemy.

Using the [color=#FFD16D]Ranged Combat Style[/color] requires a [color=#FFD16D]Ranged Weapon[/color] plus its [color=#FFD16D]ammunition[/color]. For example, using a [u]Bow[/u] requires [u]Arrows[/u] as ammunition primarily obtained from Fletching.

Some [color=#FFD16D]Ranged Weapons[/color] like [u]Javelins[/u] can be their own [color=#FFD16D]ammunition[/color].

The [color=#FFD16D]Magic Combat Style[/color] requires a [color=#FFD16D]Magic Weapon[/color] in combination with the the use of [color=aqua]Magic Spells[/color]. These cost [u]Runes[/u] primarily obtained from Runecrafting.
Each weapon has different [color=#FFD16D]Stances[/color] to choose from. Your selected [color=#FFD16D]Stance[/color] determines which Combat Skills gain XP.

The [color=#FFD16D]weapon[/color] you use determines the [color=#FFD16D]Stances[/color] available to choose from. Not all [color=#FFD16D]weapons[/color] have access to all [color=#FFD16D]Stances[/color].
Take a look at the [color=#FFD16D]Equipment Stats[/color] tab to see how this is calculated in relation to your [color=#FFD16D]Stance[/color].

Your [color=#FFD16D]chance to hit[/color] depends on your [color=#FFD16D]Stance's Accuracy[/color] compared to the [color=#FFD16D]Enemy's Evasion[/color] against that same [color=#FFD16D]Stance[/color].

When fighting an Enemy, aim to have a higher [color=#FFD16D]Accuracy Rating[/color] than their [color=#FFD16D]Evasion Rating[/color].

Damage from attacks is reduced by a percentage depending on [color=#FFD16D]Power[/color] and [color=#FFD16D]Protection[/color].

Your [color=#FFD16D]Power[/color] compared to the [color=#FFD16D]Enemy's Protection[/color] determines how much of your damage is reduced. Higher [color=#FFD16D]Power[/color] helps overcome enemy [color=#FFD16D]Protection[/color].

[color=#FFD16D]Power[/color] is primarily obtained from [color=#FFD16D]weapons[/color].
[color=#FFD16D]Protection[/color] is primarily obtained from other gear.

You can reduce an Enemy's damage dealt to you by increasing your [color=#FFD16D]Protection[/color].

[color=#FFD16D]Magic Weapons[/color] have [color=#FFD16D]Elements[/color] attached to them which determine what type of [color=aqua]Magic Spells[/color] you can use in Combat.

Monsters may also have an [color=#FFD16D]Element[/color], which can either buff or debuff your character.

Beating an Element grants you with [color=green]+15% Max Hit[/color].
Losing to an Element debuffs you with [color=orange_red]-15% Max Hit[/color].

This is only applied to you, and never to the Enemy.
[color=#FFD16D]Prayers[/color] are toggleable passive effects that can buff your Character. These cost [color=#FFD16D]Prayer Points[/color] to remain active.
[color=#FFD16D]Prayer Points[/color] are obtained by burying [u]Bones[/u] dropped from slain Enemies (via your Bank), or through other methods such as Firemaking.

[color=#FFD16D]Prayer XP[/color] is gained while actively using [color=#FFD16D]Prayers[/color]. Your damage dealt and cost of the Prayer determines the XP gained, with higher cost Prayers providing more XP per damage.
Cook various types of Food to restore Health when consumed. Some Food also provides special bonuses when used.

Your chance to successfully cook Food depends on your Cooking Proficiency compared to the Food's Difficulty.

Cooking Proficiency can be increased by leveling Cooking, equipping Items, or via the Shop or other Skills.

Hunting is a Skill that tasks you to hunt a variety of wild Animals & Beasts in order to acquire their rewards.

Hunting feeds directly into [b]Beastcrafting[/b] as its primary use, while also rewarding you with various other Items such as [b]Herb Seeds[/b] and [b]Bones[/b]

Before you can hunt, you must craft a Trap in Crafting.

Each Animal requires a specific Trap, which is listed in Hunting when you select the Animal.

You can then hunt the Animal, which is an automatic 3-step process, rewarding you with Skill XP and Items upon successfully trapping the Animal.

[ul]Search the location to find the Animal’s tracks.[/ul]

[ul]YFollow the tracks to locate the Animal.[/ul]

[ul]Use your crafted Trap and attempt to catch it.

[color=green]Begin the Skill by purchasing your first plot of [b][color=white]Land[/color][/b] and building an [b][color=white]Enclosure[/color][/b].[/color]
Select a rock to begin mining for Ore, Essence, Gems and other rewards.
Each hit has a chance to break the rock. If the Rock Break Bar reaches 100%, the rock automatically breaks.
Breaking a rock grants its rewards.
Some rocks also provide rewards with every hit, even before they break.
Purchase Land, build Enclosures, and buy Animals using Gold Pieces. Each Animal has a limited lifespan before it moves on.
Most Animals require Food to stay healthy, while some can survive without being fed.
Maintain your Animals' Comfort and increase their Satisfaction to improve the rewards they produce.
Repair Enclosures to keep them in good condition, and give your Animals Pets to meet their needs.
Animals automatically produce XP and item rewards every hour. Proper care increases their output.

Ranching is a [b]Passive[/b] Skill designed to provide important raw resources used around the game in a passive manner.

It is not designed to be the primary source of these resources, but instead be a source that can produce as you work on other Skills.

You are tasked to purchase plots of [b]Land[/b] to build [b]Enclosures[/b] and look after various types of [b]Animals[/b].

Each [b]Animal[/b] has a [img height=1.25em]res://Assets/Skills/AnimalHusbandry/happiness.png[/img] [b]Happiness[/b] stat that needs to be managed, where your primary goal is to keep this at or above 100%.

[img height=1.25em]res://Assets/Icons/SkillIcon.png[/img] [b]Skill XP[/b] and resources are generated every 1 hour, multiplied by [img height=1.25em]res://Assets/Skills/AnimalHusbandry/happiness.png[/img] [b]Happiness[/b].
Create Runes required to cast Magic spells in Combat.
Craft Magic weapons and armour to improve your effectiveness in Combat.
Smelt Ores obtained from Mining into Bars used for crafting equipment and other items.
Use Bars to forge Melee-focused weapons and armour.
Create components used in Fletching to craft Ranged equipment.
This Skill is dangerous and can deal damage to you.
Steal from NPCs, Stalls, Locked Chests and Heists to obtain various rewards.
Your chance to successfully steal depends on your Stealth compared to the target's Perception.

Failing to steal causes you to take damage and become stunned. Dying may result in losing an equipped item.

Equip Food from Cooking to automatically heal when your Health is low.
Increasing your Fortune boosts the quantity of item rewards received from Thieving.
Use Lockpicks to open Locked Chests, or find their Keys to greatly reduce the Lockpick requirement.
Complete multi-step Heists to earn rewards at each successful step, with rare rewards available upon completion.
Select a tree to begin cutting it for Logs and other rewards.
Each hit reduces the tree's Health. Reduce its Health to 0 to collect its  primary rewards.
Some trees also provide rewards with every hit, even before their Health reaches zero.
Created items have a chance to be destroyed based on the number of steps required.
When an item is destroyed, a gift is received instead:
All outputs are destroyed upon creation.
The sale value of each destroyed item is gained instead.

As you walk back into Azamire, you feel a swell of pride at the number of newly constructed buildings. They're small, and you hardly takes you long to count them on two hands, but still, Azamire is rebuilding, bit by bit.

Your delight is interrupted by a shriek as you hear a... Golbin run by, chased by the newly appointed Militia Captain - Jass. The chase doesn't last long, and Gloob is held down while Jass berates it, talking about how she's no fool and knows a trap when she sees one.

en:
[color=#E9DFC1]Thank you for joining us during [color=FFD16D]Steam Next Fest[/color]!

Melvor Idle 2 is still in active development, and the version you're about to play is an [color=FFD16D]early limited look at the game[/color]. Many systems, features, visuals, and balance are still being developed and refined as we work towards an Early Access release.

For this demo, progression is limited to [color=FFD16D]Level 60[/color], with only a limited selection of Skills and content available to test out. The Early Access release will have far more content available!

As this is an early build, you may encounter unfinished content, balance that isn't quite right, missing features, or bugs.

Your feedback during Next Fest is incredibly valuable to us. We'd love to hear about your experience, any bugs you may have encountered, or general discussions around the game.

Most importantly, have fun, explore, experiment, and enjoy your first steps into Melvor Idle 2!

And remember - [color=FFD16D]Melvor Idle 2 is an idle game![/color] You can set your character on a task, let them make progress in the background, and check out some of the other great games taking part in Steam Next Fest. Melvor will be here when you get back!

Thank you for being part of the journey![/color]

- [i][color=light_gray]Malcs, Coolrox, Prat, Tapi & Ash[/color][/i]

en: After a short stay back in Azamire, you and [Companion Name] find it hard to rest. There's still so much to be done. The Ringleader was merely the first step.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
The day following your attack on the Ringleader's fort is met with a mixture of joy, relief, grief, and... uncertainty. 
While the assault was successful, casualties number in the range of a few dozen, a large blow to the already wavering population of your home.

However, with the number of refugees coming and going nowadays, ebbs and flows in the local populace are getting hard to keep track of. While callous, you are thankful that no one you knew well fell - though a few of the original militia recruits you and [Companion Name] trained were among the bodies you brought back on the wagons.

Yesterday's events weren't enough to keep you or [Companion Name] down for long, though. The two of you set off back to the fort at first light, searching for tracks of the caravan you saw leave the fort on your first scouting mission. The set of buildings behind their thick wall still smouldered from the night before, reminding you both of the battle.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
Following the caravan takes you ages. You travel north, out of the Elder Grove and just an hour's walk outside of the town of Hirane until the tracks stop. Several wagons were stopped here and burned, presumably by the hobgolbins bringing them. It seems that several captives were killed, though for what reason, you don't know. From what you're able to gather, the group split into well over thirty different parties, all heading off in different directions. Doubtlessly impossible to follow them all, even without the added difficulty of being much harder to track than the wagons.

You worry for a moment about Hirane's safety until you realize that the golbins would have to have a small army to raze a town of their size. Being situated on the Heartroad - one of the main throughputs to the capital of Melvor - certainly had its advantages. Being able to trade for finely crafted arms and armor was chief among them, but the Golbin's presence still gave you pause.

You and [Companion Name] decide to head into town, and the general mood of the place is... tense. Folks who seem to be citizens quickly hurry past haggard, haunted-looking villagers. It's a sight you're well acquainted with, though you're surprised to see it here. You and [Companion Name] are quickly approached by a fussy-looking man with an immaculately cared for mustache and a permanent scowl etched on his face.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: I simply do not have the time for idle chit-chat. You two are just one group of many flowing into town.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
Curo purses his lips at that, seemingly a bit lost on what to say after that. He opts for a slight nod and then excuses himself, his chaperones following quickly after.

The woman you dropped off your goods with politely, but shyly, asks if the two of you could lend just a bit more help since it sounds like you'll be stuck here anyway. You look to [Companion Name], who just shrugs. Might as well. She quickly leads you off to a nearby cooking tent, where a line of hungry refugees waits eagerly. It seems that the current staff are struggling to keep up.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: After poring over the reports from Hirane's scouts, you're sure of one thing. The hooded figures that attacked Azamire and seem to be kidnapping and transporting townsfolk have headed far to the east. To what end, you couldn't even begin to wager a guess.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
You exit Hirane's gate and find yourself deep within the countryside. You travel east along the Heartroad, knowing that if you go far enough, it should be next to impossible to miss Clearwater. From what you were able to gather from folks in Hirane, Clearwater acts as the major waystation between the east and west sides of the Desert Plains. You heard of many small resting points and hamlets between here and there, but few were notable enough to commit to memory.

The Heartroad is generally well constructed and maintained - even this far from the capital - but as grass turned to arid soil, and then eventually sand, the Heartroad becomes harder to keep track of. Despite what the locals in Hirane said about there being places to rest between there and Clearwater, most of the buildings you pass are abandoned, swallowed by the sands.

The sun beats down on you overhead in a way you're unfamiliar with except for on Azamire's hottest summer days. There's no reprieve from the heat, just sand stretching out in what seems endless waves of gold.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: You wipe the cactus water from your mouth. The two of you tapped into many of the ones nearby and start to stray from the original patch. You find yourselves giggling and swaying to and fro, despite definitely being more hydrated. You're worried that something may be wrong, but how could it be? You feel so good. [Companion Name] nearly collapses against you in a fit of giggles, the sand undulating in mesmerizing patterns underneath you.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
The cacti that stand in front of you now seem... bigger. And they move. But everything is moving, so that's not particularly strange. What is strange is that one of the cacti swing one of its spiny arms at your head when you try to cut into it with your axe. The needles in the side of your face snap you out of the cactus water's hallucinogenic effects.

Everything around you stops moving, except for the... angry cactus in front of you. And all of the ones behind it. They shift through the sands and reach out with their arms. They're real. You call out to [Companion Name] who seems to be having a similar revelation.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
The cacti's spines are rough to contend with, and require a far more protective approach to fighting than you're used to employing, but all is well. The patch of cacti lays slain at your feet, and the... effects of the cactus water seem to have subsided.

You press on to Clearwater, only taking occasional, small sips of the cactus water you collected when you absolutely need to. You're definitely more giggly than usual and sway lightly on your feet, but the worst of the effects never take hold with your moderate approach.

The town of Clearwater is a sight for sore, sun-baked eyes. Your feet ache, your skin is sunburnt, and you're absolutely parched. A small crowd of townsfolk gather about, laughing at your misfortune and warning of some of the dangers you may see deeper within in the desert.

When you ask about the figures, much of the levity is replaced by fear. A good chunk of the population here seems to have come from the abandoned exterior towns fleeing the... Soulsmiths. It feels weird to finally have a name to the group that destroyed your home. Here, dealing with them has been a constant, and the name holds no gravitas. The townspeople say they've seen the caravans head east, towards the capital, and warn you to stay far away from the eastern Heartroad for now. When you and [Companion Name] tell tales of Azamire and the Ringleader, and your goal of seeing the Soulsmiths brought to justice, it seems like half the town opens their homes to you, keeping you fed and hydrated as you two recover.

After some well-deserved rest, the two of you continue east finally out of the dunes and back into grassy fields. You pass into rockier terrain as you approach the Flintcrest Highlands. Large jagged boulders dot the rocky soil, jutting out at odd angles.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
With that, [Companion Name] continues to peer over the boulders as the two of you travel along the Heartroad, as if they'd spring to life and tell her where they came from. You've had enough of sentient things that should otherwise not be, so you try to avoid staring too much.

Finally, you arrive at a little inn that seems to have been built into a stone wall and garrison that takes up the expansive entrance of the Broken Pass. The Sleeping Stone is legendary, and for good reason. Not only is it the home of the Slayers Guild for the eastern region of the continent, it attracts world renowned adventurers who wish to venture into the Perilous Peaks to prove themselves to be the best of the best.

The Broken Pass is the quickest way to the capital, but it's typically travelled by highly armed caravans that can both pay the toll to pass the gate, and can fend off any beasts that travelled down from the mountain proper. When you hear of caravans being rerouted south - around the mountain range - due to a particularly feisty pack of Stonehoppers, you're quick to offer you and [Companion Name]'s services. 

The owner of the Sleeping Stone does you one better, saying that if you take care of them, you'll get free passage through the Broken Pass for life. The deal's too good to pass up.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
You tally up the bodies of the tall, awkward beasts. Stonehoppers were a bit of an odd blend of creatures. They were scaly like a lizard and use a long whip-like tail for stability. They have two large wings that aid them in jumping from rock to rock - hence their name - but they were technically flightless. The 'birds' walk on two powerful legs that they use to kick at their prey, which fortunately made it easy to get them tangled up in traps.

What surprised you about them was their number. It felt like every time you caught one, you'd see two more jumping overhead.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: Fine then. Let's make it a bet, then. Whichever of us takes down the least cooks dinner out of them, then.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
You and [Companion Name] tally up your kills and... somehow, it's a dead tie. You do a once-over of the den just to make sure you got them all and neither of you could squeak out a last minute victory, but you really did get them all.

You both throw up your hands and congratulate one another on a job well done and camp out in the Broken Pass, cooking a meal together. Usually you just dig into your travel rations, but this is about as good of a chance as you'll get on the road. With some local herbs and a generous bit of seasoning... yeah, it does taste like chicken. Quite a bit more gamey, and virtually zero fat, but a great meal nonetheless.

You settle into your sleeping roll and watch the embers of the fire float up into the sky.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: We'll finally be in the capital, soon. I've dreamed about it ever since I was a kid.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
After a bit of shuteye, the rest of the trip is... uneventful in a positive way. You pass by the eastern gate to the Broken Pass and tell them how you've dealt with the Stonehoppers and show them proof, to which the guards are both impressed and thankful, and promise to let those at the Sleeping Stone know.

You pass by a few villages along the rest of the Heartroad, many of them clearly prospering due to their proximity to the capital. As you pass over the Bridge of Kings, you see the grand gates of Melvor before you, with a long trail of people waiting to be let inside.

Through talking with the crowd and a few guards who do their best to keep the peace, it sounds like the city has been under a light lockdown to new travellers because of an influx of smuggled goods. Only those bearing visitor passes or proof of citizenship are allowed entry. These visitor passes are sold for... rather exorbitant amounts.

A group of pompous aristocrats wave their passes and bottles of wine about flamboyantly and shuffle along the pathway. They let out strings of taunts and insults as they walk past the line of those looking to be let into the capital. You and [Companion Name] look to one another with wry smiles.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
You follow the group along for a while until one of the richly dressed men smacks a wide-eyed child on the nose with their pass, then hurries along. The child's mother shouts after them, and the angry line of onlookers finally snaps at the mistreatment. Some of the drunken nobles cower in fear, afraid of the consequences of their own actions, while others egg the crowd on further, clearly enjoying the attention. The guards try to keep the peace, though they are clearly fed up with the 'social elite' as well, judging by their glares.

Taking advantage of the situation, you bump into one of the nobles in the crowd and slip your hand into their coat, withdrawing a sleek sky blue visitor's pass. You keep walking as its original owner shouts after you for daring to touch them, but they're drowned out by the angry mob soon enough. [Companion Name] slides in right beside you, holding one of her own. The two of you open them up, realizing that there's no identifying information that is required, the pass alone is proof enough that you may enter.

Just like that, the gates of the capital won't stop you. You don't even feel a little bad.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: By following crumbs of information regarding the group you now know as the Soulsmiths, you've found yourself thrust into the middle of the capital of Melvor with hardly a clue on what to do or where to go next.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
You'd heard tales of the capital many times by those who'd travelled the continent and happened to stop by Azamire for trade or rest, but their stories hardly even begin to scratch just how... much was laid out before the two of you. Thousands of people, many speaking languages that you couldn't even begin to place. Buildings that stretch so high into the sky that you have to crane your neck to fully see. Market stalls filled with an endless number of trinkets and clothes, while some on the other side of the random plaza you'd entered emit smells so strange and tantalizing you involuntarily start to drool.

You try your best to take in everything, excitedly chatting with [Companion Name] as you both try to point out the endless rush of... everything, until you find yourself pushing out of the crowds for the first time. You're thankful for the space, until you feel a strong hand clamp down on your shoulder and yank you backwards. Your hand goes to the weapon at your side until you realize you... walked onto a firing range! An arrow whizzes past your nose as you turn to the person who grabbed you. A tall, tanned man dressed in a gaudy purple cloak and a longbow strapped to his back pulls you out of danger, to [Companion Name] who breathlessly catches up to you.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: New to the capital, I presume?
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: Can't blame you. Melvor is a real beaute, ain't it?
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
Talm winks at the two of you and then holds a finger to his lips, clearly giving no further information than he's already provided. Based on how quickly you and [Companion Name] looked to one another at the mention of Soulsmiths, he knew he had you hooked. Without even asking if you'd be interested, he talks about how arrows fashioned with the feathers of a Sea Griffon always seem to find their mark, and would quite fancy having some of the arrows for himself. Unfortunately, he has no feathers, just the location of one that has been terrorizing a few fishing boats.

You and [Companion Name] leave the capital as quickly as you came, and after a few hours of travel, find the windy cliffside that the nest was said to be. And sure enough, a large pack of the beasts swoop overhead, clearly upset by your arrival.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: Feathers gathered, the two of you make the trek back to the capital. The city is just as overwhelming as before, but the clear goal of finding Talm again manages to help you push through the enthralling nature of the new sights and smells with ease. Talm is amongst the competitors, warming up. He's doing a remarkable job even without the feathers, nearly splitting his own arrows far down the range, and you begin to wonder why he feels the need to cheat at all.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: Talm's sing-songy taunt elicits a glare from [Companion Name], but after a brief standoff, she sighs and hauls you away, grumpily beginning to cut some arrow shafts. You get the impression she'd rather use that knife elsewhere, but has decided to behave, for now.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: The two of you make your way back to Talm, this time with a bundle of arrows, to which he receives with a small, polite show of clapping. He takes one and inspects it carefully, before bending it so far that it snaps in two. He tuts to himself and shoves the splintered arrow back into your hands.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: Now now, this simply won't do. My bow may also be a bit special. Like I said, I really want to win this. With the force I'll be sending these arrows down range, they don't stand a chance.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
Even in a city as bustling as Melvor, Talm is a remarkably easy figure to find. After just a few minutes of asking around the range, you find yourself face to face with the tall, smiling man. Without a word he gestures for you to follow him, so you do, trusting he knows what you're after. You're led deep within the alleys and byways of the capital, some better, some worse. As you round a corner you find yourself at the back entrance of a brightly painted stone building, door already open for you to enter. As the three of you enter, the door quietly shuts behind you without any prompting.

You're brought before an absolutely stunning woman who greets the three of you with a wordless smile, and gestures for you to sit on cushions laid out in front of her. You do, and the room quickly fills with a twinkling blue fog. You panic for a moment before deciding that they don't seem to mean you harm, and you inhale deeply.

Your vision fades away, then comes back to you as you're flying far overhead a large white building, whose doors seem to suck you in. You fall through the floor of the building and weave through shelf and shelf of books, all the way to a large vault made of a blend of metals and magic you instinctively know as you pass through its walls. Within, you find a gilded tome that seems to glow with power. The moment you touch it, you snap back awake next to [Companion Name]. She seems... upset, seemingly a bit disturbed by whatever she saw.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: What... was that? Did you see the same thing, [Companion Name]?
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
And with that, Talm helps Era up and takes her to a room behind a nearby curtain. It doesn't seem like you're invited. You check on [Companion Name] once again, about the vision she had. She gently, tells you that she'll talk about it later, just that it was a bit scary. 

The two of you wander around the city, a bit less awestruck than when you first arrived, and soon enough, find yourselves on the doorstep of the Ivory Athenaeum. From what you learn, speaking with some of the guests and staff, it'd seem that the titanic structure holds the largest compilation of humanity's knowledge ever created, with a near endless number of books on every subject one could think of.

You ask about the lower floors, and learn that they are restricted from the general public, needing a direct invitation from the King himself to be let inside, since the books down there contain dangerous information. The process of obtaining an invitation is told to you through a long, well-rehearsed deluge of information. What sticks out to you is the time involved. An average of thirty years for those prestigious enough to be allowed a chance. Too long.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
You want to let out a cheer as the Abyssal Vault comes into view, but you obviously know better than that. You put [Companion Name] up on your shoulders and she slowly but surely presses a wedge of clay into the arcane locking mechanism. The vault is exactly as it appeared in your vision, and you do your best to memorize the magic that courses through it as [Companion Name] deals with the mould. You know from your vision that you'll have to imbue the key with the same magic for it to actually work when you come back and let yourself in.

Now that you've properly mapped out the route to the vault, you're able to get back to the entrance with little trouble. Understandably, the patrolling guards are both few in number and a bit inattentive, it's not like many people would be crazy enough to try this. You and [Companion Name] make it back out of the Ivory Athenaeum, and finally allow yourself to breathe.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
The two of you quickly search through the displayed items until you find what you're looking for. The black, gilded tome from your vision. Amongst everything else in the vault, you'd almost call it unassuming. 

It hums with some unknown magic, and you give it a ginger touch with your hand. When you don't immediately get vaporized by some unknown power, you lift it from its resting place and crack it open. The first page says... Something in a language you've never seen before. You snap it closed and gently wave it for [Companion Name] to see. She carefully crosses the vault and takes the book, and the two of you head back to the entrance. However, the moment your hand touches the metal of the door to push it back open, it snaps shut. A loud hum fills the room, along with what sounds like an alarm outside of the vault.

As you look to [Companion Name], a large golem seems to coalesce from the ground, made of the same alloy as the rest of the vault. [Companion Name] readies her weapon, and you follow suit.

en:
The two of you run like your lives depend on it, because they likely do. Every time you're singed by a magical barrier or narrowly dodge a guardsman's pike, you just think about how many lifetimes you'd likely spend in Melvor's jails. That is, if they didn't just outright execute you. You make sure not to hurt anyone, because murder wouldn't likely get you any better treatment if you were to be captured.

By some miracle, you manage to make it to the stairwell leading up out of the lower floors. Stunned guardsmen scramble to bring their weapons at the ready - clearly not anticipating any intruders actually making it back to the entrance - and the two of you manage to burst back out into the main floor of the athenaeum.

You rush outside and into the throngs of people being evacuated outside. Guards point and shout at the two of you as you melt into the crowds but fail to give chase as you quickly slip deeper and deeper into the mass of concerned citizens. The two of you find yourselves at the edge of a canal and jump in, swimming under the water all the way to an exposed sewer grate. You let yourselves inside and strip off your disguises and toss them into the water, both silent as the adrenaline slowly works its way through your bodies. You quietly laugh and lean against the wall of the sewer with a sick squelch you don't even notice. You did it. You got out, somehow.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
[Companion Name] flicks the gilded tome open and closed, looking at it from every angle she can, and trying a few different pages. Like you, she hasn't the foggiest clue about what the book says, and the place that would likely know, is still searching high and low for it. You and [Companion Name] have left your little sewer hideaway and sure enough, the disguises you donned before the heist worked. No one comes to put you in shackles and haul you off to some dark dungeon. As far as anyone else is concerned, you're just one of the many thousands of tourists to the capital.

You head back to Era and Talm's home and find it in flames. Talm worriedly tries to douse the flames with many other passersby, until a capital mage buries the building under a deluge of water. You rush to Talm. Your presence gives him pause, and he gestures for you two to follow him.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
The three of you set off, leaving the burned building behind. Talm leads you through the city with such ease and purpose you get the feeling he's been here a long, long, time. As you travel, the people you see become less friendly, and more dirty. Desperate. The slums were doubtlessly going to be here, like any other large city, but to see them up close was a staunch difference to when you first arrived in the capital a few weeks ago.

Rougher looking folks give you a large berth when they lock eyes with Talm. The generally friendly man now walks with murderous intent, his bow now set aside for a longsword and shield that he carries openly. He looks back to you frequently, making sure you're looking out for the shack as diligently as he'd hope for. And sure enough, you see it. The crescent shape by the door - just like in your vision - is so loud to your eyes, you almost don't understand how [Companion Name] and Talm don't see it.

You point it out, and without a word, Talm approaches the door and sends it off its hinges with a startlingly powerful kick. You eye [Companion Name], who charges in right behind him. Swords clash almost immediately.

en: I was around before... this capital. And the one before it. Era too.

en: You raided one of the most secure locations in the capital for... what's basically a children's history book.

en:
You caught [Companion Name]'s flinch when Talm said that Era's visions are never wrong. But why? What'd she see? You've tried asking, gently, over the last couple of weeks, but you've hardly gotten anything other than it being 'bad'.

Talm utters a command in a language you cannot understand to the thrall, and it shudders for a moment, before walking off at a leisurely pace. The three of you follow close behind until you get to the main gates of the capital. You flinch as you approach the guards and Talm pulls the thrall between you and him. He takes on a drunken sway and starts slurring gibberish as the guard looks your party over. The woman pinches her nose and remarks that you 'smell like death' and waves you off.

You do your best to wipe off the thrall's blood that leaked through his pilfered robes once you're out of eyeshot, cursing quietly to yourself. The thrall leads you far out of town and out into the countryside. Once you hit the treeline of a nearby forest, Talm curses and releases his command of the thrall, who slumps to the ground. He says he knows where they went.

You're lead to a large stone tower that blends well into the rocky landscape. It once had a large wooden door that now lays splintered in a dozen large chunks on the ground. Talm exclaims that they attacked his 'real' home, and that the security system was set off.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
[Companion Name] and you look at each other, grimacing a bit as the following silence is punctuated by the sounds of tearing flesh and sickening gurgles. You feel a bit faint listening to Talm work on his... not dead wife. If one can reverse the effects of aging then perhaps mending wounds falls under that domain as well. You see [Companion Name] shoot a glance in their direction then quickly avert her eyes, clutching her mouth after a quiet heave. You think better of it.

You nearly leap out of your skin when you feel a couple of light taps on your shoulder and come face to face with the incredibly pale visage of Era. Her wounds stitched together, the only remnant of them being the tears in dress from which any number of weapons pierced her. 

She welcomes you to her home and starts to apologize for the mess, before then frowning, realizing your part in its current state. The fact that she was on death's door just moments ago seemingly not bothering her in the slightest. If they're truly as old as Talm claims, you wonder how many times someone could have crossed a similar scene.

Era gestures for [Companion Name] and has Talm bring a chair over, to which she slumps in. She runs her hands over the book with fondness, then gives a few directions for adjusting telescope. She invites the both of you to use it.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
The stars stretch out before you, incalculable in number. As you peer up at them through Era's telescope, they twist and turn in so many beautiful arrays and patterns you almost want to weep. As you try to commit them to memory, they dance ever so carefully out of reach again and again. You take breaks when the floor beneath you sways like the gentle rocking of a ship at sea. [Companion Name] takes your place in these bits of downtime. You chat here and there with Era and Talm, who both look at you with a degree of fondness that comes off as... almost warm, though the feeling almost feels misplaced.

The sight is punctuated by that of Talm's new thralls, the broken bodies of the Soulsmiths being twisted to work on... repairs and cleanup. The sight is as macabre as it is absurd. A pair of thralls mop up after one another in a circle, each trying to clean the trailing blood from their comrade. You shudder at the sight. When one of the thralls tries to remove Talm's sword from the wall and ends up tearing its arm out of its socket. 

You nearly faint. Talm curses softly, and Era simply chuckles. You make note to never get on either of their bad sides. Ever. You know the Soulsmiths are truly wretched and you'd never spill a tear over them, but the level of... flippance that Era and Talm have at seeing their undead bodies lurch about feels unnerving, at least for now.

You rest and recuperate in their home, taking turns with [Companion Name], peering through the telescope and trying to glean insight from the stars. Once the thralls were disposed of and the traps turned off, the tower really was nice. Though, some of the things you saw may sit with you for a long while.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en: The stars have finally shown you what you needed to see. A lone cold point, deep within the mountain range west of the capital. That is your next target.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
Your head feels fuzzy, as each breath - if you even are still breathing anymore - feels shaky and labored. You've grown far more accustomed to Era's telescope, but it still makes you feel as if something within your very being is shifting after long enough. You can practice astrology without it, but as you've learned through numerous conversations, Era's telescope is special. While Talm's summoning domain is Soul, Era's is knowledge and divination. You can't even begin to imagine what kind of creatures she can bring forth. The smoke and telescope are just two tools that allow her to practice.

And now you have done so as well. Similarly to how you felt with the Sightsmoke, you feel as if you raise from the tower and pass through its walls. You grasp for the shingled roof, but your hands pass through it without so much as grazing it. You careen up into the sky, far beyond the tower and up amongst the clouds. Your body rights itself, and you feel yourself slingshot towards the Broken Pass, then turn north, to an inlet in the mountains covered with frost and snow. As you shoot towards a stone door carved into the cliffside, you close your eyes... and end up back on the floor of the tower.

You are covered in ice, and your teeth chatter violently, but you feel so... so warm.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
The beast staggers back with a cry as your blows connect with its hard flesh. It falls to the ground with a mighty crash, and slumps back against the cavern wall. It releases a breath and begins to... fade away to crystals of ice that melt shortly afterward. Whatever the beast was, it wasn't natural. As you begin to look over the murals etched and painted into the wall, you feel quite sure of that assumption.

The murals depict the group that once inhabited the cavern. Little blue figures of people living in a beautiful blue forest. Then... the forest burning due to some unknown red assailants riding on similarly colored creatures. After that, there are far fewer blue figures in a blackened forest. The numbers dwindle further and further with each section of wall. Until the blue figures leave the charred forest. The murals show them travelling far... very far. Almost half the cavern wall depicts them travelling from one place to another, in all manner of places. They settle for short periods of time, with each move always predicated by a clash with some new color of figure. Brown, grey, green, red, orange, and even a lighter color blue towards the end. These figures are accompanied by beasts. All drawn simply in nature, but clearly terrifying to those who lived here. You catch yourself wiping your eyes more than once as you spend over an hour trying to follow their story.

Finally, in the last tenth of the wall, it shows the figures... finding what you presume to be this place. They find a book. They create their own creatures. The figures leave the wall and travel across the floor, to spires of ice that jut out from the ground, one nearly touching the ceiling.

You realize, the center of the room looks... similar to a page of the book you cannot read. You lay it out and [Companion Name] holds her lantern overhead as you trace out places that line up. Two pages of the book, when lined up with the central pillar of ice, resemble the eastern portion of the continent. And within that map, a shining tower lays just off the coast. Comparing it to current maps, it'd be far north of the capital. Your next destination.

You spare a last glance to the figures on the ground, crowded around the spire of ice. It's the last of their journey, none left their last destination. You can only imagine what the spire represents, but it's a mystery for another time.

en:
You bring you sail to the dock and find [Companion Name] floating in the water, treating the boat with what you presume to be waterproofing. You set the sail on the ground and help haul them out of the brine, to which they shake like a dog and get you drenched. You threaten to shove them in, so they wrap their arms around you and threaten to haul you both back in. You shove them off and roll your eyes, to which they give one of the first genuine laughs you've heard from them in a long while.

Why they decided that smelling like stale water and rotting wood was their happy place, you may never know, but you can't help but smile after seeing them happy. The two of you fit the sail to your skiff and sit on the dock, admiring your handiwork. You each carve your name into its railing, and give it a firm pat. It's ready for its journey. Are you?

en:
The piles of corpses stop moving, which is as close to dead as you can imagine they'll get. It's not just the bodies, though. The whole tower seems... still. Stale. As if it was frozen in time. 

Despite its incredible height, you can only see a single floor, the one you're on. The two of you search high and low, finding... nothing. The place is decorated with stone benches and tables and lit with pale yellow-green lights that make you feel sick, but little else. You sit by the pool in the center of the room, watching the corpse piles slowly turn to ash.
hint: Zusatztext (C#-Code oder Laufzeit, nicht in der offiziellen Vorlage)

en:
Arms of gray skin and bone reach out to grab you from the corridor walls. You and [Companion Name] run through the fetid halls along the only path laid out for you. There's nothing else you can do. Each step becomes heavier and heavier as the bone beneath you turns spongy and slick with blood that pours from the ceiling and walls.

You lost track of time ages ago, and focus on your breathing. In. Out. In. Out. You reach out to steady [Companion Name]. Flinch back as she cuts a hand away from your throat.

The tunnel grows more narrow, and all the while, the beast crawls towards you faster and faster. Its breath curls down your back as you sprint through the halls, the feeling reminding you of how the purple vial touching your lips and bringing you to this nightmare felt. You feel the beast's nails bite into your skin. Just a glancing blow, but you know the next time it touches you, it will be fatal.

You see light up ahead. You jump off the bridge.

And then... it ends.

You reach a large room made of the same stone as the tower that brought you here. Your lungs burn and tears stream down your face. [Companion Name] lands beside you with a thud.

You look back, and the tunnel you came from isn't there.

Maybe it never was.

You turn back and see Talm, arm in arm with his wife Era. The two of them look at you with so much hatred that you almost feel like you deserve it, though you haven't the slightest idea on why. Their fingers elongate into claws that scrape against the stone floor, while their bodies twist into malformed ideas of human anatomy.

en:
An old cobbled road takes you and your companion far north, just outside of a town by the name of Tidebreak. The population is said to be rather reclusive, mostly preferring to keep to their own and subsist on what they can fish up. The sea breeze goes from refreshing to... almost sour the further north you get. You get why not many people decided to live up this way, and question the motives of those that do. You push on ahead as the sun begins to set.

The town itself is... quaint. You feel eyes on you everywhere you go, and kids are pulled inside ahead of your path. You find yourself on the coast, where a lone young man works a length of rope, hardly sparing you a glance. Another man, who almost seems like he could be his brother, looks on and even gives you a smile, which you almost find weirder. You try your chances with the rope worker first.
